News.title: Kemi to fund 50,000 more prison spaces by slashing foreign aid – after hundreds of lags freed under Early Release scheme
News.content:
Next

KEMI Badenoch will today pledge a massive 50,000 extra prison places to stop criminals being freed early.

The £2billion-a-year building blitz would boost jail capacity by more than half, with most of the new cells promised within one Parliament.



It would be funded partly by slashing the foreign aid budget to £1billion a year, alongside cuts elsewhere in government.

The extra space would be used to reverse Labour’s early-release schemes and bring back short prison sentences.



But prison capacity rose by a net total of just 482 places during the Tories’ 14 years in government.

Ms Badenoch admitted her party failed to build enough while in power, saying the places they added were “nowhere near enough”.

She went on: “We now have a plan to solve this issue and build 50,000 new prison places, the biggest prison increase since Queen Victoria, instead of papering over the cracks, investing £2 billion a year in our prisons and reversing Labour’s dangerous early-release schemes.

“The first duty of government is to keep law-abiding people safe.



“Full prisons are a reason to build more cells, not release more criminals onto our streets.”

Labour chair Bridget Phillipson warned that the Tories were “taking the public for fools” after their record in power.

“Now Kemi Badenoch expects the British people to believe they’ll build 50,000,” she said.



“These proposals are just not credible from a party who left our criminal justice system at breaking point.”

She added that Labour is “fixing the broken system” the Tories’ left behind so victims of crime “can get the justice they deserve.”

Ms Badenoch’s pledge comes as hundreds of prisoners were freed early in England and Wales this week.

They are part of the first wave of 4,500 criminal offenders to be released over the next year in an effort to tackle prison overcrowding.

This is despite concerns over a struggling Probation Service and delays to electronic monitoring tags.



Most will not be strapped with monitoring tags as the Probation Service struggles to fit them all.

But the Ministry of Justice has insisted those released will be under the “toughest supervision in British history.”

In the last three months, the number of male prisoners has risen by 1,700 and the Government says it has been forced to free up space in overcrowded jails and stop the justice system from collapsing.

Former Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer and previous Tory administrations had presided over similar plans.

News.title: Woman tricked partner she gave birth twice & said she sold his babies for £500 in sick revenge plot, court hears
News.content:
BABY 'LIES' Woman tricked partner she gave birth twice & said she sold his babies for £500 in sick revenge plot, court hears







Next

A WOMAN convinced her partner she had twice given birth and told him she had sold his babies for £500 in a sick revenge plot, a court has heard.

The man, in his 30s and who cannot be identified, said that he had even felt his partner’s “pregnant” stomach during her first pregnancy.

He never met the children he believed to exist as he was arrested after the woman made allegations after each birth, reports the Daily Mail.

A High Court heard that the woman, in her early 50s, had even sent him images and ultrasounds before later telling him she had sold the babies.





She told the judge she had deceived her partner in a revenge plot, alleging the man had abused both her and her son.

Mrs Justice Judd ruled that there was no record of the babies ever existing and they had been fabricated.

She said the woman had “engaged in a campaign of deception lasting for about three years”.

The woman said she could not have been pregnant because she was menopausal at the time.



Remarkably, the woman is even said to have claimed she has always had a large stomach and was overweight.

Meanwhile, she was shown to have visited a tanning shop on the day she was due to give birth, according to her bank statements.

She went to such lengths to convince others she had given birth that she even played a YouTube video of a baby crying in a voice message to her partner’s mother.

In late 2022, the man said the woman had become “visibly pregnant”.



But the following May, when the first baby was due, an argument culminated in the woman calling the police, claiming assault.

He was subsequently put in cuffs and held on remand for several months.

During that time, she told him the baby had been born and sent him photos and updates about their child.

Mrs Justice Judd said: “When the applicant was released from prison the relationship resumed, but he says the respondent told him the baby was with a family member.

“She said the local authority had said he was not permitted to see her, but she did show him lots of pictures of the baby.”



The nextdeception came in 2024 when she told him his second child was to be born that August.

That same month, the pair had split up but she continued to tell the man’s mother that the child had been born.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The case went to court after the man was told his two children had been sold by their mother for £500.

The judge said: “The behaviour was cruel, leading a man and his mother to believe they had children and grandchildren respectively.”

News.title: Royal Marines return to Faroe Islands just 150 miles from UK coast for first time since WW2 to deter a Russian takeover
News.content:
VLAD ALERT Royal Marines return to Faroe Islands just 150 miles from UK coast for first time since WW2 to deter a Russian takeover







Next

ROYAL Marines have returned to the Faroe Islands for the first time since World War Two to deter a takeover by Putin.

Green berets and Danish forces stormed fishing boats in drills designed to “stop Russia sneaking onto the islands”, a Navy source said.



It comes amid fears the Kremlin could use civilian trawlers to reach the Danish territory, just 150 miles from Scotland.

Similar tactics were used in Russia’s 2014 invasion of Crimea.



The Kremlin used so-called “little green men” to seize control from Ukraine in 2014.

First Sea Lord General Sir Gwyn Jenkins said: “Defending the Atlantic is fundamental to our economy, national security, and way of life.”

The former Special Boat Service commando added: “The return of the Royal Marines to the Faroe Islands should send an unequivocal message: the UK, alongside Denmark and our other allies in the Joint Expeditionary Force, stand ready to protect the waters, islands and vital routes that keep our nations secure.”

The Faroes straddle a sea route tightly controlled by Nato to monitor Russian nuclear submarines that could sneak into the Atlantic.

The Ministry of Defence said: “The UK Commando Force were dispatched to work alongside Danish forces and maritime agencies from the Faroe Islands.”

British and Danish troops joined Faroese coastguard forces for “boarding and seizing target vessels” as well as “specialist coastal landings onto steep and inaccessible terrain, and small boat missions” the MoD added.



British marines seized the remote isles in 1940 to prevent a Nazi invasion.

News.title: Shocking moment news reporter and cameraman are struck by van after vehicle skids off busy road during live broadcast
News.content:
TV HORROR Shocking moment news reporter and cameraman are struck by van after vehicle skids off busy road during live broadcast







Next

THIS is the horrifying moment a reporter and her cameraman were crushed by a van live on air as they reported from a busy motorway.

Shocking footage showed Alma de la Rosa Flores and her colleague Cristo Morales brutally slammed against a stone wall after the car slammed directly into them.



Reporting on a landslide in Monterrey, Mexico, the pair stood directly in front of a jagged wall of rubble and uprooted greenery.

Alma is speaking to the camera when the van suddenly swings around the landslide, ramming into the pair and instantly cutting the broadcast.



The live feed was switched to Mario Gámez in the studio who asked his production team where the location was so they “could send emergency services”, La Nacion reports.

He said: “They were hit by a truck that skidded while trying to avoid the landslide. I urgently need the address, please, and if there is anyone nearby.”

Incredibly, the pair – who work for the Ecuadorian TV network Gamavisión – both escaped with minor injuries.

It is understood Alma even managed to walk into the ambulance with the help of paramedics.



According to the news outlet Reporte Indigo, they were attended to by city Civil Defense teams at the scene.

The driver of the pickup truck was arrested.

Mario later gave an update on their conditions and said: “Good news, my two teammates are doing very well.

“They’re bruised, battered, and scared, but there are no serious injuries from the incident.”

It comes following a similarly horrifying incident where a teenage girl was hit by a car live on air while a journalist reported on another crash.



Shocking footage showed the victim, 14, riding her e-scooter on a road in Kościerzyna, Poland before a motorist ploughs into her.

After smashing into the windscreen, the girl is sent flying before the cameraman captures the assailant fleeing down a side street.

TVP journalist Miłosz Sieliwończyk had been at the scene reporting on a young boy being fatally crushed by a car.

He said: “At one point, I heard a bang behind me and the operator’s shout: ‘Oh Jesus!’

“When I turned around, I saw a car driving away with a shattered windshield and a child lying there.”



Miłosz told the cameraman to keep filming and zoom in on the licence plate so that they could report the incident to police.

He said: “We approached the girl. She was unable to stand. I saw blood stains on the scooter.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Paramedics decided to take the teen to hospital for a check-up, although her injuries are not thought to be serious.

According to Miłosz, the person responsible for the accident returned to the scene a few minutes later.

News.title: Dope smokers should be reported to police by their neighbours, says Tory Chris Philp
News.content:
SHOP POT HEADS Dope smokers should be reported to police by their neighbours, says Tory Chris Philp

Credit: PA







Next

WEED smokers should be shopped to the police by their neighbours, the aspiring Tory Home Secretary has said.

Chris Philp said he would personally snitch on his neighbours if he caught them doing cannabis anti-socially.

The former Policing Minister said he would expect cops to respond to reports of illegal drug taking in communities.

Critics have long claimed that taking drugs like marijuana – a Class B substance – has been virtually decriminalised with little enforcement.





Asked if he would dob on a neighbour smoking cannabis, Mr Philp told The Sun: “I think if it was associated with anti-social behaviour, yes I would.

“But I think it’s really up to the police to always take action when they come across lawbreaking.”

He added: “If it’s antisocial behaviour, then yes. And I would definitely expect the police to always follow it up if they encountered it.

“I wouldn’t want the police to ignore it, it’s their job to police that kind of thing.”

Mr Philp, who said he has never taken drugs, also said he would confront a shoplifter if he came across one.

During his time as a minister he memorably told the public to be have-a-go heroes and make a citizen’s arrest.

Asked if he stood by the comments, he said: “Yeah, I’ve been looking for one ever since.

“I’ve never had to directly, I’ve never directly had to confirm a shoplifter because no one no one’s ever shotlifted in front of me.



“But if they did, I would definitely confront them for sure, just as I confronted the people smuggler on the beaches of France just a few weeks ago.”

News.title: ‘Madonna bra’ £20k spinning sculptures blamed for burning children’s hands after becoming too hot in sun are moved
News.content:
BURNING UP ‘Madonna bra’ £20k spinning sculptures blamed for burning children’s hands after becoming too hot in sun are moved







Next

AN art installation made up of metal cones and dubbed “Madonna’s bra” has been moved after it was blamed for burning children’s hands.

The spinning sculptures – named “A Hand’s Turn” – were installed in Farnham, Surrey back in 2023, costing nearly £20,000.



The 20 metal cones were installed at a cost of £19,500 and were funded by the University of the Creative Arts.

But on a retrospective planning application, residents complained the cones, which have also been likened to Daleks, were unsightly.



Some residents also alleged that the structures, which can spin, were burning or injuring children after they became too hot in the sun.

Now, the cones have been moved to a sculpture garden on campus at the University for the Creative Arts, in Farnham.



It comes after resident Patricia Humphreys said the artwork looked “like a set of anti tank traps”.

Angela Vinnicombe added “the cones got very hot in summer in the sun and can cause injuries to children touching them.”



Nearby Farnham resident Sue Banks said she had heard “young children who have touched the cones cry out”.

And Ann Marion Hicks said they were a “hazard to children” last summer.

But it has since been confirmed the cones should no longer be affected by the hotter weather.

They have now been moved to a new location “underneath tall trees and various foliage”.

The art-installation was a collaboration between artists Natalie Bradwell and Livia Spinolo.



The cones were said to “evoke the forms of the grain’s piles going through the malting process, the traditional roofs for drying hop, the spindles used for spinning the wool or the shapes of pottery vessels” when originally installed.

Bradwell said she was “grateful to get a second chance” to renovate and re-exhibit the cones.

She said: “I hope locals find a new affection for the cones in their new home.

“They are intended to be played with, hugged and even the unintended percussive ability they provide is great fun.

“What a special place Farnham is for its commitment to craft and community. Farnham didn’t give up on the cones, so neither will I.”



The Sun has contacted the University of Creative Arts for comment and Waverley Borough Council for comment.

News.title: Influencer mum-of-three found dead with children and husband after posting chilling final message about her ‘nasty side’
News.content:
DEATH PROBE Influencer mum-of-three found dead with children and husband after posting chilling final message about her ‘nasty side’







Next

A TIKTOK influencer and her family have been found dead after a post about her “nasty side” online.

The bodies of Cindy Tamez, 34, and her two-year-old son, Gustavo, were located inside a Jeep in Montemorelos, Mexico, on Wednesday morning.



Her two other children, Bruno, 11, and Christian, 12, as well as her partner, Leodegario Moya, were discovered at their home, a few streets away – all shot dead.

It was just hours before that the glam content creator had posted a clip from inside a car captioned: “Not everyone knows my nasty side.



“I would burn down my own house just to watch my neighbour’s go up in flames, even knowing I’d get f***ed over too.”

A handgun, a mobile phone and a cartridge were inside the Jeep, beside the two bodies.

Prosecutors have searched her home and are analysing CCTV footage and other evidence to reconstruct what happened as part of the probe.

Neighbours reportedly told authorities they had heard loud music coming from her property in the early hours of Wednesday.



Cindy, whose full name was Cinthia Abigail Tamez Rivera, was reportedly involved in lending money and organising informal savings schemes.

Part of her work reportedly involved buying, selling and raffling items including cars, chains, watches and mobile phones.

On TikTok, she had amassed over 74,000 followers.

Cindy posted snapshots of her daily life, including off-road vehicles and parties, and appeared to project an image of affluence.

One of her early posts showed her in a stunning pink dress with her three boys, displaying a picture-perfect family.



But another included messages about getting revenge on people who had hurt her.

“I can take it, but I can give it back twice as hard, so don’t think I give a f*** – I can be twice as much of a c*** as you,” it said.

Another said: “I’m probably just as much of a piece of s**t as you, or even worse.



“But I never screw someone over unless they’ve screwed me over first.”

Prosecutors are investigating whether Cindy’s moneylending activities were connected to the tragedy.

News.title: Newcastle University 'suspicious item' recap: Man, 33, arrested as emergency services swarm city centre campus
News.content:
A 33-year-old man has been arrested on suspicion of communicating false information following a report of a suspicious item at Newcastle University - searches were carried out before the incident was stood down

A 33-year-old man has been arrested on suspicion of communicating false information following a report of a suspicious item at Newcastle University.

Northumbria Police said officers were called at 2.10pm on Friday to a report that an item had been found at a university building on King's Walk in Newcastle city centre.

Several university buildings were evacuated while searches were carried out. The incident was later stood down and the man was arrested. He remains in police custody.

Police cordons that had been put in place on roads including Queen Victoria Road, Brewery Lane, King's Road and St Thomas' Street have since been removed.

News.title: UK facing 'serious threats' from Iran Shabana Mahmood warns after 'terror plot' arrests
News.content:
UK facing 'serious threats' from Iran Shabana Mahmood warns after 'terror plot' arrests

Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood said Tehran's regime targets 'our Jewish communities' as she warned of 'a range of serious threats' facing the UK

View 2 Images Shabana Mahmood (Image: ADAM VAUGHAN/EPA/Shutterstock)

The UK is facing "a range of serious threats" from Iran, Shabana Mahmood has said after two men were charged with an alleged bomb plot against the Jewish community.

Iranian nationals Salam Ahmadyan, 36, of Liverpool, and Rahman Salehi, 34, of Salford, were arrested on Sunday, charged with terrorism offences over an alleged plot to target the Manchester's Jewish community.

It is alleged the pair were in contact with an overseas third party who may be in Iran in relation to the plot, CTP said. Both men have been remanded in custody to appear at Westminster Magistrates' Court on Saturday.

Following the news, Ms Mahmood said it is "no secret" that the UK faces "a range of serious threats from the Iranian regime".

"They target our Jewish communities and try to silence their critics overseas, often through proxies and criminal networks to hide their involvement," she said.

View 2 Images Both men have been remanded in custody to appear at Westminster Magistrates' Court on Saturday (file image) (Image: PA)

"The Prime Minister has been clear there are strong indications of Iran's involvement in the events near RAF Fairford.

"We are responding to these threats with new powers and record funding to disrupt hostile activity. I’m grateful to our police and intelligence agencies for the exceptional work they do every day to keep us safe."

Ms Mahmood said the news that two suspects had been charged "will be deeply distressing for our Jewish communities, coming so soon after Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur."

"I know this will be especially true in Manchester, as we mark one year since the terrorist attack at Heaton Park Synagogue."

She added: "These recent events are a stark reminder of the threats posed against this country from both terrorists and foreign state actors.

"The fact both suspects arrived by small boat several years ago is a reminder of the importance of our relentless work to tackle illegal migration into this country. While numbers are down, I know there is more we must do."

"It would be inappropriate to comment further on this case. But I can say that we will be unrelenting in our efforts to protect our Jewish communities, root out antisemitism in this country, and maintain our border security."

It is said that Salehi and Ahmadyan, on or before September 20, 2026, with the intention of committing acts of terrorism, or assisting another to commit such acts, engaged in conduct in preparation for giving effect to that intention.

News.title: Christa Pike spoke of fears that lethal injection would fail weeks before 'worst nightmare' came true
News.content:
Christa Pike spoke of fears that lethal injection would fail weeks before 'worst nightmare' came true

Death row inmate Christa Pike feared her execution could go wrong, describing a failed lethal injection as her 'worst nightmare' in a prison recording just weeks ago

View 4 Images Christa Pike described a failed execution as her 'worst nightmare' (Image: AP)

Christa Pike described a botched lethal injection as her "worst nightmare" in a prison recording made just weeks before her own failed execution.

‌



‌



Pike was just 20-years-old when she was convicted of brutally torturing and murdering her Job Corps classmate Colleen Slemmer, 19, in January 1995, with the killing leaving her facing a death penalty.

‌



The Tennessee death row inmate, now aged 50, had feared her execution could go wrong after another prisoner, Tony Carruthers, was left suffering when his lethal injection was called off in May.

‌



"The concerns I have on our lethal injection method are simply that I do not have good veins, and I'm worried about our physician not being qualified to start a central line on me," Pike said in a recording obtained by the New York Times.

View 4 Images Pike cries after being sentenced to death in 1996 (Image: WBIR-TV via AP)

"Tony Carruthers lived out my worst nightmare. Detail for detail. And I don't want to go through that," she added.

‌



Pike had been due to become the first woman executed in Tennessee in more than 200 years on Wednesday. But the execution was abandoned after two attempts to administer the lethal drugs failed, with Pike rushed to hospital afterwards.

Her lawyers said she was in a critical condition and receiving lifesaving treatment, while suggesting she may have suffered brain damage during the botched execution.

Pike also described fears over the drugs used during her execution, saying they had been compared to the chemical drain cleaner Drano.

‌



View 4 Images The death row inmate is in a critical condition and receiving lifesaving treatment

"The drug… supposedly burns very bad," she said. "And so that sounds scary to me because they used the word Drano in speaking about this drug, and the thought of suffocating and drowning on my own bodily fluid and blood isn’t very appealing to me."

In the recordings, Pike also told how she was "very remorseful" for the killing of Slemmer, despite not feeling that way in the beginning.

‌



"I'm very remorseful now," she said. "I wasn't in the beginning when I first caught this charge. I didn't care what I had done or who I had done it to."

View 4 Images A Tennessee journalist stands near images of Pike's victim, Colleen Slemmer, 19 (Image: DENNY SIMMONS / THE TENNESSEAN / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images)

"The horror of the pain that I caused her family, my family, my co-defendant’s families, I have affected this world in such a negative way when all I ever wanted to do was care for people and leave love. I have done the opposite of that and that pains me," Pike said.

Article continues below

Maria DeLiberato, the lawyer of Tony Carruthers, said Pike had been put "right back in that room with Tony" during his execution attempt last May following her failed lethal injection.

"We are joining the calls for a commutation for Christa, so she never experiences this torture again," DeLiberato said.

"Moreover, we continue to ask the same for Tony, who is still recovering from his botched attempt and fighting to prove he was wrongfully convicted - all while he remains at risk of another execution attempt."

News.title: Anti-ULEZ activist jailed for 15 years after blowing up camera with improvised explosive device
News.content:
Anti-ULEZ activist jailed for 15 years after blowing up camera with improvised explosive device

Kevin Rees, from Sidcup in South London, was handed the especially lengthy sentence after the Met Police said a judge ruled the incident had a 'terrorism connection'

View 8 Images Kevin Rees has been convicted after detonating an IED on a ULEZ camera (Image: Metropolitan Police / SWNS)

An anti-ULEZ activist has been jailed for 15 years after he was found to have carried out a terrorism-linked detonation of a camera enforcing the London's low-emissions scheme.

‌



‌



Kevin Rees, 64, detonated a powerful improvised explosive device that destroyed the camera on Willersley Avenue in Sidcup, South London, at around 6.45pm on December 6. Counter-terror police were called in to investigate after the detonation caused damage to cars and property up to 100 metres away, and shrapnel struck the outside of a child's bedroom.

‌



Investigators later identified Rees, a prolific social media user who frequently posted anti-ULEZ content, as their prime suspect behind the incident.

‌



Terror cops arrest two men over London ULEZ camera explosions READ MORE :

ULEZ cameras vandalised with red spray paint as 14 destroyed in just one area READ MORE :

View 8 Images Rees' powerful explosion caused damage over a 100-metre area (Image: Metropolitan Police / SWNS)

The retired electrical appliances engineer, of Harcourt Avenue, Sidcup, was convincted in January at Woolwich Crown Court on one count of causing an explosion likely to endanger life. He was sentenced to 15 years in prison on Friday, with the Metropolitan Police saying the judge ruled the incident had a "terrorism connection".

The connection means Rees received a tougher sentence, and will be placed under strict controls when he is released from prison.

‌



Detective Chief Superintendent James Derham, who leads local policing in the Bexley area, said it was "miraculous" no one was hurt in the explosion. Chf Supt Derham said: "It was miraculous that nobody was killed or seriously injured in the large explosion caused by Rees."

View 8 Images The camera was detonated in a 'large' explosion, police said (Image: Maureen McLean/REX/Shutterstock)

"He showed a complete disregard for the welfare and safety of the people who live in, or were travelling through, the area at the time of the explosion - all because he was unhappy with the ULEZ scheme.

‌



"CCTV from a bus travelling down the road at the time shows how it narrowly missed the blast of debris by seconds." London's ULEZ scheme requires drivers to pay a daily surcharge based on how polluting the emissions from their vehicle are.

While it once covered a smaller portion of the inner city to the North and South Circulars, the ULEZ now encompasses every one of the capital's 33 boroughs.

View 8 Images The ULEZ zone was increased in 2023 (Image: Maureen McLean/REX/Shutterstock)

‌



Cameras are used by Transport for London (TfL) to monitor the cars that enter and exit the zone, triggering fines for motorists who have not paid the daily charge. The extension, which came into effect in February 2023, was largely welcomed by Londoners but garnered controversy, much of which was drummed up on social media.

That controversy prompted a major crime wave, and the Metropolitan Police said it recorded 987 crimes relating to ULEZ cameras just five months after it was extended.

Among those incidents was one that caused a road traffic accident which injured a child, police said, with pictures of others showing the cameras and the posts they were mounted on dangerously felled like trees. During the trial, Rees told the court he "strongly opposed" the ULEZ scheme - and London Mayor Lord Sadiq Khan.

‌



View 8 Images There have been hundreds of incidents of ULEZ cameras being vandalised (Image: Maureen McLean/REX/Shutterstock)

He said he disliked him and "what he has done to London". A jury heard the investigation team identified that Rees had travelled in his Smart car from his home in Sidcup to Shuttle Close shortly after 6.20pm on December 6, 2023.

The ULEZ camera was installed earlier that day, but in an unrelated incident had been cut down by another individual, who was also identified and convicted. Rees walked the short distance from his car to the camera and then planted the device and lit a fuse, police said.

‌



He was then seen by a witness walking quickly away from the scene. Rees was identified and was arrested on December 18, 2023 and his home was searched.

View 8 Images Rees said he disliked Sadiq Khan (Image: PA)

Detectives analysed Rees's social media activity and found he had posted numerous times about ULEZ cameras and encouraged the damaging of them, the Met said. Three homemade stun guns were found at his address. Rees was given a three-year sentence, to run concurrently, after he admitted three counts of having a prohibited weapon.

‌



During the trial, Rees denied all involvement in the incident, telling jurors he believed his arrest was linked to his participation in "anti-ULEZ" groups on Facebook.

When he was arrested by counter-terror police on December 18, Rees made reference to that explosion and asked officers if his arrest had "something to do with the anti-ULEZ sites". Rees told jurors he joined "anti-ULEZ" Facebook groups and pages out of "boredom" and because it provided him with a sense of community.

View 8 Images The ULEZ expansion rage was whipped up over social media (Image: SWNS)

‌



Bethan David, former head of the Crown Prosecution Service's counter-terrorism division, said: "This was not an act of protest or momentary vandalism.

"This was a deliberate and dangerous attack involving a homemade explosive device, carried out in a residential street and designed to destroy public infrastructure. Kevin Rees knowingly and intentionally placed an explosive device next to the ULEZ camera, lit the fuse and retreated before the explosion, showing clear planning and an obvious disregard for the safety of others.

"Whatever his views on the ULEZ scheme, Kevin Rees crossed a serious line by constructing a homemade bomb and detonating it in a public place."

‌



View 8 Images TFL said it hoped Rees' sentencing would serve as a warning to other would-be ULEZ vandals (Image: SWNS)

"It was pure chance that no-one suffered serious injury, or worse. The Crown Prosecution Service will always seek to prosecute dangerous offending of this nature and hopefully this conviction sends a clear message to other protesters considering taking the law into their own hands."

Siwan Hayward, TfL's director of security, policing and enforcement, said: "This was a reckless and highly dangerous act that could have caused serious harm and resulted in the loss of life.

Article continues below

"We welcome this sentencing and hope it acts as a warning to others. Tampering with or damaging TfL's property is unacceptable and seriously risks the safety of the public. Those attempting to interfere with ULEZ infrastructure show a complete disregard for the law.

"All vandalised cameras are repaired or replaced as soon as possible. Any such incident on our network is reported to the police and will not stop the ULEZ operating."

News.title: Two dead as workers 'trapped in trench collapse' on roadside in Co Down
News.content:
Two dead as workers 'trapped in trench collapse' on roadside in Co Down

A huge rescue operation was launched in Crossnacreevy, Co Down, after reports people were 'trapped in a trench' during a workplace accident which left two dead

View 3 Images Two people have died (Image: Mark Marlow/PA Wire)

Two people have died in a tragic workplace accident following reports of a number of people being "trapped in a trench".

‌



‌



A large rescue operation was launched at around 10:45am this morning as emergency services raced to Crossnacreevy in Co Down, Northern Ireland.

‌



The horror unfolded on Ballygowan Road, with police, fire crews and paramedics called to the scene alongside two Hazardous Area Response Teams (Hart).

‌



Officers closed off a section of the road between Houston Road and Knockbreda Road, reports Belfast Live.

In a statement, the Northern Ireland Ambulance Service said it received a 999 call at 10.45am on Friday.

View 3 Images Emergency services at the scene in Crossnacreevy (Image: Mark Marlow/PA Wire)

‌



"Multiple emergency resources were sent including three emergency ambulances, and two Hazardous Area Response Teams (Hart)," it said. "No-one was taken from the scene."

The Health and Safety Executive Northern Ireland said its inspectors were on site investigating the circumstances of the incident.

"HSENI is aware of an incident at a workplace in the Crossnacreevy area and inspectors are on site making inquiries into the circumstances," it said.

‌



"We are currently liaising with the emergency services and other relevant agencies."

East Belfast MP and DUP Leader Gavin Robinson said in a post on social media that two people had died and that Ballygowan Road will remain closed.

"Sadly, it has been confirmed that two people have lost their lives following an incident in Crossnacreevy," Mr Robinson said.

‌



View 3 Images The Health and Safety Executive have been advised (Image: Mark Marlow/PA Wire)

"My thoughts are with their families and loved ones at this devastating time, and with the emergency services responding to the incident.

"Ballygowan Road will remain closed. Please avoid the area and use an alternative route."

‌



A PSNI spokesperson said: "Police and other emergency services are currently at the scene of a workplace-related incident on Ballygowan Road, Crossnacreevy. The Health and Safety Executive have been advised."

A spokesperson for the Northern Ireland Ambulance Service said: "The Northern Ireland Ambulance Service received a 999 call at 10:45 on Friday, 2nd October, following reports of an incident in the Ballygoward Road area, Crossnacreevy.

"Multiple emergency resources were sent including 3 Emergency Ambulances, and 2 HART Teams. No one was taken from the scene."

Article continues below

Two fire appliances from Knock Fire Station, one from Carryduff, one from Cadogan Fire Station and two specialist rescue teams were all in attendance as the rescue operation was underway, the Northern Ireland Fire and Rescue Service said.

A spokesperson added: "Firefighters were called to reports of a rescue incident on Ballygowan Road, Crossnacreevy, Carryduff, Down. This incident is ongoing."

News.title: Ann Widdecombe murder suspect charged with preparing acts of terrorism against Reform UK leader Nigel Farage
News.content:
Ann Widdecombe murder suspect charged with preparing acts of terrorism against Reform UK leader Nigel Farage

Joshua Kerry, 28, has been charged with engaging in conduct in preparation of acts of terrorism, including against Reform UK leader Nigel Farage MP, Counter Terrorism Policing said

View 3 Images Joshua Kerry, 28, has been charged with Ann Widdecombe's murder

The man suspected to have killed Ann Widdecombe has been charged with engaging in conduct in preparation of acts of terrorism, including against Reform leader Nigel Farage.

Counter Terror Policing have said Joshua Kerry, of Byrley Road, Rotherham, South Yorkshire, was today charged with one count of preparation of terrorist acts following authorisation from the Crown Prosecution Service. The charge, police said, relates to activity which is alleged to have taken place between May 31, 2024 and July 8, 2026.

Senior National Coordinator for Counter Terrorism Policing, Deputy Assistant Commissioner Vicki Evans, said the charges against the 28-year-old came following a long-running "hugely intensive and complex investigation".

View 3 Images Police said Kerry's charges related to Nigel Farage (Image: Ben Birchall/PA Wire)

She said in a statement: “We have been running a hugely intensive and complex investigation for some time. The charge announced today is a result of the tireless work of investigators across the Counter Terrorism Policing network.

“This investigation has been led by a dedicated team of detectives, analysts, and forensic experts, working on multiple lines of enquiry, which has resulted in this very serious charge.”

Kerry was earlier this year charged with the murder of former Reform member Ann Widdecombe, and was initially arrested on suspicion of murder on July 11. He was additionally arrested two days later on July 13 on suspicion of the commission, preparation or instigation of acts of terrorism.

Widdecombe, 78, a former Conservative minister turned spokeswoman for Reform UK, was found dead on July 9 at her home in Haytor, Devon.

On July 20, Laurence Taylor, head of UK Counter Terrorism Policing said in a statement outside Scotland Yard that the investigation into Kerry, including a possible motive, was ongoing. Taylor said: "I want to make it very clear that our investigation into [Kerry], determining his motivations and any wider activity he may have been involved in is continuing.

View 3 Images Ann Widdecombe was found dead at her home this summer (Image: PA)

"As with all murder investigations, understanding the 'why' is a key part of our enquiries.” He added the investigation was "a particularly intensive and complex investigation".

Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood said the charges over an alleged terror plot against Reform UK leader Nigel Farage raised “serious questions” about the security of MPs.

Article continues below

She said: “I know the new charges made today will be extremely concerning. My profound sympathies are with Nigel Farage and his family. Let no one make any mistake: an attack on anyone in politics is an attack on us all. This case raises serious questions about the security of those in public life. We must use this as an opportunity to reset.

“Once Parliament returns, I will update on our work to strengthen protections for those who choose to serve.” Kerry is due to appear at Westminster Magistrates’ Court on Wednesday October 7, over the charges, police said.

News.title: Former Chelsea star's son died while hiking in the 'Grand Canyon of the UAE' in 40C heat
News.content:
Former Chelsea star's son died while hiking in the 'Grand Canyon of the UAE' in 40C heat

A coroner today told how Eddie Newton, who was assistant manager at Chelsea under both Roberto Di Matteo and Rafael Benítez and scored for the club in the 1997 FA Cup final, flew to the UAE to identify his son Cassius' body after he was found on July 18

View 3 Images Former Chelsea star Eddie Newton's son Cassius once played for the West London club's academy

The son of former Chelsea star Eddie Newton died with a friend in Dubai’s desert valley after ignoring his wife’s plea not to hike in 40C heat, an inquest heard.

‌



‌



Cassius Newton, 34, from Poole, Dorset, and his pal Aran Martinson, 33, were found in sweltering heat in the mountainous region of Wadi Naqab, known as the 'Grand Canyon of the UAE, after setting off on a "recreational" expedition at around 7am on July 18. Essex Coroner's Court today heard how Newton called his wife, who was in the UK, at about 2am to tell her of their planned hike and "she asked him not to go".

‌



Area coroner Michelle Brown ruled their deaths were the result of misadventure, and said the cause included cardiac and respiratory arrest, as well as severe rising body temperature, organ failure, and heat stress due to exposure to high temperature. She said: "This was an intentional trip with unintended consequences."

‌



To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 3 Images Eddie Newton and Roberto Di Matteo on the way to the Chelsea victory parade following their UEFA Champions League and FA Cup victories on May 20, 2012 (Image: Chelsea FC via Getty Images)

Speaking about Mr Newton's wife's warnings, Ms Brown added: "She knew it would be very hot and it can get to about 40C, and the feeling is higher because it's in the canyons. He was also out the night before and wouldn't have had much sleep, and she didn't think he would have charged his phone enough."

‌



Newton, originally from Poole, Dorset, and Martinson, a dad-of-three originally from Bishop's Stortford, Herts, met through their work at a "global company" and both lived in the luxury resort of Ras Al Khaimah, around 75 miles north-east of Dubai. Rescue efforts were launched after the wives of both men called the authorities, having not heard from them for hours.

Text messages between Martinson and his wife were read to the court, including one at 9:26am when she wrote: "You must be cooking." Having not heard from him five hours later, she later messaged: "[You are] actually trying to tip me over the edge I swear."

The two men were eventually discovered 350 metres apart, between 1.8 miles and 2.5 miles from where they had parked. The coroner said Cassius and Aran were both found lying on their backs surrounded by large rocks.

‌



View 3 Images Chelsea Captain Dennis Wise, right, congratulates goal scorers Eddie Newton centre and Roberto Di Matteo, left, after their two nil win over Middlesbrough in the 2007 FA Cup final (Image: mirrorpix)

She described the circular route they were walking as "a recreational hike" on a designated trail that did not require any equipment and should have taken about four hours to complete. The pair were taken to hospital in Ras Al Khaimah before being pronounced dead later that day.

Eddie Newton, who was assistant manager at Chelsea under both Roberto Di Matteo and Rafael Benítez, made 165 appearances for Chelsea between 1990 and 1999. He also scored for the club in the 1997 FA Cup final.

Article continues below

Ms Brown said Mr Newton flew to the UAE to identify his son's body. In an earlier tribute, Chelsea said it was "devastated" to learn of the death of Newton, who once played for the club's academy.

National League side Eastleigh, for who Cassius used to play, said the club was “deeply saddened” by his death.

Mr Martinson's wife wrote online that her husband was "incredibly driven, hardworking and ambitious". She added: “He had only recently started a new chapter in his career, and I know how excited he was about it.”

News.title: 'Donald Trump made his own mess with diesel crisis - we shouldn't have to clean it up for him'
News.content:
'Donald Trump made his own mess with diesel crisis - we shouldn't have to clean it up for him'

"Having unleashed the crisis, Trump now expects Europe to rescue him from the consequences - his administration is pressuring allies to release strategic diesel stocks while threatening to restrict American exports"

View Image Voice of the Mirror has its say...

Donald Trump gambled with the world’s security with his war on Iran and has helped drag Britain into an energy crisis of his own making.

‌



‌



He boasted the campaign would be over in weeks. More than seven months later, fuel supplies remain fragile, diesel has hit a record £2 a litre, and governments are discussing emergency reserves.

‌



Having unleashed the crisis, Trump now expects Europe to rescue him from the consequences. His administration is pressuring allies to release strategic diesel stocks while threatening to restrict American exports.

‌



Britain, heavily dependent on imported diesel and US supplies, is dangerously exposed. This is the arrogance and incompetence of a man unqualified to lead the free world.

He promised speed and victory. Instead, families face dearer fuel, transport, food and potentially mortgages.

Trump made this mess. The rest of the world should not have to keep paying for his failures.

‌



'Sham contracts'

Once again, the beautiful game has turned ugly.

Manchester City insist they are innocent and are appealing against a ruling that they breached Premier League financial rules over almost a decade.

At the heart of the case is the allegation that the club used sponsorship deals and “sham contracts” to disguise more than £830million in secret funding, including money said to have come from the Abu Dhabi government rather than commercial partners.

‌



Those findings cut to the heart of sporting fairness. Fans must believe success is earned on the pitch, not tilted by hidden financial advantages behind the scenes.

City are entitled to challenge the verdict, and their appeal must be heard properly. But the wider issue cannot be ducked. Football depends on trust, transparency and rules that apply equally to everyone.

'Last one standing'

There is something wonderfully British about Ritchie Wood holding out as bulldozers prepare to make way for a £5billion Universal theme park.

Article continues below

The project will bring jobs, tourists and prosperity to Bedfordshire. But before the Minions arrive, Universal should make sure its last reluctant neighbour is not left feeling completely despicable.

News.title: Widdecombe suspect charged with planning terror act against Farage
News.content:
The man accused of murdering Ann Widdecombe has also been charged with preparing acts of terror including against Reform UK leader Nigel Farage.

Counter terror police said Joshua Kerry, 28, was charged on Friday with one count of preparation of terrorist acts.

The charge relates to activity which is alleged to have taken place between May 2024 and July 2026.

Kerry was charged in July with the murder of 78-year-old Widdecombe, a former Conservative minister and Reform UK spokeswoman.

Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood said she knew the fresh charge would be "extremely concerning" and her "profound sympathies" were with Farage and his family.

"Let no one make any mistake: an attack on anyone in politics is an attack on us all.

"This case raises serious questions about the security of those in public life. We must use this as an opportunity to reset. Once parliament returns, I will update on our work to strengthen protections for those who choose to serve."

The BBC contacted Reform UK for comment and a party source said: "This is exactly why Nigel needed Â£5m to protect his security for life."

Farage is currently facing a parliamentary standards watchdog probe into a Â£5m gift from a billionaire donor before he returned as an MP in 2024. The Reform leader has previously said the money was for his personal security.

Counter Terrorism Policing Deputy Assistant Commissioner Vicki Evans said the charge on Friday was the result of a "hugely intensive and complex investigation".

"This investigation has been led by a dedicated team of detectives, analysts, and forensic experts, working on multiple lines of enquiry, which has resulted in this very serious charge," she added.

Kerry, from Rotherham, is due to appear in court over the terror charge on Wednesday, police said.

Frank Ferguson of the Crown Prosecution Service's Special Crime and Counter Terrorism Division said prosecutors "worked closely" with police to bring the charge and would continue to work alongside them as the investigation continued.

Widdecombe was found dead on Thursday 9 July at her home in Haytor, Devon, having sustained serious injuries.

She served as Conservative MP for Maidstone in Kent for 23 years and was appointed to ministerial roles in Sir John Major's government in the 1990s.

Following her departure from the Commons, Widdecombe appeared on the BBC's Strictly Come Dancing and would later become a Reform UK spokeswoman.

News.title: Watch: Why has UK diesel price hit an all time high?
News.content:
The average price of diesel has risen above Â£2 a litre in the UK for the first time, according to the RAC motoring group, with petrol also soaring to 174.71p a litre on average.

Price rises were "showing no signs of slowing, heaping more misery onto motorists," the group said.

Separately on Friday, the G7 nations agreed to release 100 million barrels of oil to head off further increases.

The BBC's Business Editor Simon Jack explains the rising prices in the UK - and how oil prices around the world affect the cost of petrol and diesel at the pump.

News.title: Men charged over alleged plot to target Manchester Jewish community
News.content:
Two Iranian nationals who arrived in the UK by small boat have been charged with terror offences over an alleged plot to target the Jewish community in Manchester.

Rahman Salehi, 35, of Salford, and Salam Ahmadyan, 36, from Liverpool, are accused of preparing to commit an act of terrorism or assisting another to commit an act of terrorism on or before 20 September.

The men were arrested in Manchester's Northern Quarter on the eve of Yom Kippur, considered the holiest day in the Jewish calendar.

Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood said news that two Iranian men had been charged over the alleged plot would be "deeply distressing" to Manchester's Jewish community, as the city marks one year since the Heaton Park Synagogue attack.

Counter Terrorism Police (CTP) allege the two men were in contact with a third-party overseas, who may be in Iran, in relation to the plot.

According to CTP, the men are accused of obtaining instructions to make a chlorine bomb, acquiring liquids, components and equipment for such a device, researching potential targets and conducting reconnaissance of potential locations for attack.

It is understood the suspects arrived via small boat in 2020 and 2023. One was granted asylum, and the other has a live asylum claim.

Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood said: "These recent events are a stark reminder of the threats posed against this country from both terrorists and foreign state actors.

"Two suspects have been charged with planning a terrorist attack against Jewish communities in Manchester.

"This news will be deeply distressing for our Jewish communities, coming so soon after Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur.

"I know this will be especially true in Manchester, as we mark one year since the terrorist attack at Heaton Park Synagogue.

"The fact both suspects arrived by small boat several years ago is a reminder of the importance of our relentless work to tackle illegal migration into this country. While numbers are down, I know there is more we must do.

"It would be inappropriate to comment further on this case. But I can say that we will be unrelenting in our efforts to protect our Jewish communities, root out antisemitism in this country, and maintain our border security."

News.title: Traitors claim their first victim as Richard E Grant tries to save his skin
News.content:
Spoiler warning: This article reveals details from the second episode of The Celebrity Traitors, series two.

A comedian, a journalist, an actor and a TV presenter walk into a church. But sadly, the punchline for one of them was becoming the first victim of this year's Celebrity Traitors.

As Friday's episode got under way, a delicious new twist saw traitors Richard E Grant and Maya Jama invite James Acaster to join them in the turret, and simultaneously murder a fellow player.

Unfortunately, it fell to Amol Rajan to become the Paloma Faith of this series - being taken away in a coffin in episode two before even having the chance to take part in a banishment.

"It's gutting to be the first out," Rajan said afterwards, noting that perhaps it was because he had been "a bit bullish with Richard" earlier in the day.

"But you know what, games are games, and just as there are winners, so there have to be losers."

The next morning, presenter Claudia Winkleman confirmed the University Challenge host's murder to the other players, joking: "That's what I call a starter for 10."

Acaster, meanwhile, reflected: "I'm gutted to not be a faithful anymore, I don't like lying. But if I don't join them, they'll kill me." You can't fault his logic.

The decision meant that Grant, an Oscar-nominated actor with a Razzie-worthy traitor strategy, did at least manage to commit one successful murder despite his shambolic first day.

News.title: Tories pledge to build 50,000 new prison places
News.content:
The Conservatives have promised to build 50,000 new prison places in England and Wales to stop criminals being released early, if they return to government.

The party said it would cost Â£2bn per year to build and run the new prisons, funded by spending cuts including to the foreign aid budget.

On Thursday hundreds of prisoners were released early, under new rules introduced to prevent jails reaching capacity, with around 4,500 due to be freed by next summer.

Labour blamed the previous Tory government for leaving "our criminal justice system at breaking point" and said the party's proposals were not "credible".

The announcement comes as Conservative members gather for the party's annual conference in Birmingham, which begins on Sunday.

Prisons in England and Wales have been running close to capacity for years, with the latest government figures showing they are 98% full.

Under the latest early release scheme, eligible prisoners can now be released on a community licence after serving one-third of their jail sentence.

Those excluded include prisoners convicted of murder, manslaughter, a sexual or grooming-related offence, or a driving offence that led to a death.

The government has also effectively scrapped one-year jail terms.

The Tories said they would use extra prison capacity to reverse these measures.

An early release programme introduced by the previous Conservative government saw more than 10,000 prisoners freed early between October 2023 and September 2024.

News.title: King's Caribbean tour will not shy away from 'darkest days of our past'
News.content:
King Charles's upcoming Caribbean tour will not shy away from "the darkest days of our past", Buckingham Palace has said.

During the visits, the King is expected to face renewed calls to apologise for the UK's role in the transatlantic slave trade and be questioned on potential reparations - compensation from countries that took part in the slave trade.

The King and Queen Camilla are set to travel to Antigua and Barbuda for the Commonwealth Heads of Government meeting, with visits also to Bahamas and Guyana as part of the eight-day trip starting on October 27.

According to PA news agency, it is understood the government has not advised the King to apologise or offer reparations.

News.title: Met Police urge students to move 7 October protest
News.content:
The Metropolitan Police is calling on the organisers of a pro-Palestinian student march planned to take place on the third anniversary of the 7 October attacks on Israel to move the event.

Deputy Assistant Commissioner James Harman said the force had been unable to identify the organisers behind the group, which calls itself the University of London Coalition.

He said that while the march did not meet the strict legal threshold at which police could request the home secretary to ban a protest, many Londoners would be marking "a day of mourning" with vigils to remember those who died.

The BBC has contacted the group for comment via social media accounts they appear to be associated with.

Harman said around 300 students were expected to march through central London, from King's College London in the Strand on Wednesday, finishing at University College London in Holborn.

He said they had demanded an end to what they described as a "genocide in Gaza".

"Serious concerns have been expressed about the impact of this march on students and staff, particularly those who are Jewish, the route, and the day it is being held," Harman said.

He urged anyone intending to join the protest to "reflect on the impact and distress it will cause on this very significant day, and exercise your right to protest on a different date".

Harman said the force had written to four London universities to ask them to engage with their students and staff and to take "all reasonable steps" to ensure students did not feel "excluded, targeted or unsafe" due to activity on their premises.

He said the letter acknowledged "the importance of freedom of expression, peaceful protest and academic debate" but also pointed to findings from the Community Security Trust over a rise in antisemitic incidents at UK universities since the attacks in 2023.

News.title: I've seen nearly 500 executions - but never one like Christa Pike's
News.content:
It's not uncommon for lethal injections - the most frequently used form of capital punishment in the 27 US states where the penalty is legal - to be "botched". The Death Penalty Information Center, a think-tank that does not take a stance on the death penalty, describes a botched execution as one with "unanticipated problems or delays that caused, at least arguably, unnecessary agony for the prisoner or that reflect gross incompetence of the executioner". The organisation has compiled a list of 64 botched executions since 1982, 51 of them lethal injections. In at least seven of those cases, the executions were halted because the IV line could not be set.

But Graczyk has never seen an execution fail after the injection was delivered.

"That has never happened here," Graczyk said of the Lone Star State.

Graczyk, who covered a wide range of topics for the AP during his 46 years with the news service, considers his prolific attendance at executions to be an important part of the job.

"There is no [greater] authority, power, or whatever you want to call it, that state or federal government has over us than the power to take our life," he said.

There have been 1,683 executions in the US since 1976, according to the Death Penalty Information Centre, which is when the US Supreme Court re-instated the death penalty. Texas has carried out by far the most of any state, with 602 executions. In 1982, it became the first state to use lethal injections to execute people.

"I always thought it was important for someone who has no stake in the outcome of a case to be there and to see the law being carried out and to make certain that it is done properly," Graczyk said.

"That someone is there to see it and tell others: Here's what I saw. Here's what happened."

News.title: Daniel Thomas in court accused of entering migrant site
News.content:
Anti-migrant activist Daniel Thomas has appeared in court charged with entering a restricted zone at a migrant processing centre in Dover.

The 37-year-old, known to his supporters as Danny Tommo, is accused of committing the offence on 31 March, according to court documents.

Thomas is further accused of using threatening words or behaviour in the Kent town on 1 April and obstructing a person engaged in a lawful activity on 6 April.

He is also charged with entering or remaining in Dover Docks without having lawful business or permission, the documents say.

Thomas faces another charge of racially aggravated harassment by allegedly using threatening or abusive words.

He appeared at Margate Magistrates' Court on Friday via videolink wearing a grey T-shirt and rosary beads.

District Judge William Nelson sent his case for a further case management hearing at Westminster Magistrates' Court on 4 November.

Earlier this week, Thomas was refused bail during a crown court hearing over the alleged slashing of a dinghy in the English Channel.

News.title: UK diesel prices top £2 a litre for first time, RAC says
News.content:
The average price of diesel has risen above Â£2 a litre in the UK for the first time, according to the RAC motoring group.

Diesel has now hit an average of 200.01p a litre, the RAC said, and petrol prices are also still rising, reaching 174.71p a litre on average.

The motoring group said price rises were "showing no signs of slowing, heaping more misery onto motorists".

Over the past seven months, the Iran war has severely disrupted the production and transportation of wholesale oil and refined products from the region, causing prices to surge worldwide.

Ukrainian attacks on Russian refiners have further constrained supplies of diesel on the world market. China has also restricted exports of refined fuels.

Separately on Friday, G7 nations agreed at an urgent meeting to release 100 million barrels of oil to head off further price increases.

The G7 also agreed member countries would not impose export restrictions on each other, after US President Donald Trump threatened to ban shipments of American diesel overseas.

The move would have pushed up global prices of the fuel, but helped ease pressure on US consumers ahead of November's midterm elections.

RAC policy head Simon Williams said Â£2 was a "price threshold no one wanted to cross".

"This will be very challenging for households and companies that drive a lot of miles, from commuters, haulage and delivery firms, businesses with large fleets all the way through to sole traders," he added.

UK businesses and consumers already feel like they are bearing the brunt of higher prices, with many saying it has made their lives increasingly difficult.

Even people who do not drive a diesel vehicle themselves face a knock-on effect from rising delivery costs or the higher cost of producing food.

News.title: Royal Navy's new attack submarine arrives at Faslane
News.content:
The Royal Navy's newest Astute-class nuclear-powered submarine has arrived at its home port in Scotland.

HMS Agamemnon will undergo sea trials and operational preparation after reaching HM Naval Base Clyde at Faslane.

The hunter-killer vessel, the sixth in the Navy's arsenal, is equipped with tomahawk land-attack missiles and torpedoes capable of striking targets up to 30 miles away.

The Navy's submarine rear admiral, Andy Perks, described HMS Agamemnon's arrival as a "significant milestone".

The 318ft-long (97m) vessel joins other Astute-class subs including HMS Astute, Ambush, Artful, Audacious and Anson, in the Navy's fleet.

A seventh sub, HMS Achilles, is currently under construction.

Astute-class submarines are the Navy's most advanced and powerful class of attack subs.

News.title: Man jailed for piloting small boat carrying 26 others
News.content:
A man has been jailed for 18 months for piloting a small boat carrying 26 other people, including six children, towards the Kent coast.

Jemal Abdela, 32, was sentenced after pleading guilty to the offence of endangering others during a sea crossing to the UK without valid entry clearance on July 25.

Winchester Crown Court heard Abdela, who is Eritrean, had also attempted to disguise the fact he had been driving the black inflatable across the Channel when it was approached by immigration officers.

A Home Office spokesman said Abdela was the 20th small boat pilot to be imprisoned in four months for endangering lives at sea.

Matthew Parris, prosecuting, told the court that the defendant was seen piloting the boat, which was being followed by French authorities.

He said Abdela had "dived into the centre of the boat and moved to another location wearing a hat" before being identified, adding that the vessel did not have flares, GPS or maps onboard.

The court heard that Abdela told police he had paid â¬800 (Â£680) for the crossing, which had begun at 17:00 BST the previous day.

He also claimed to have been sat by the captain of the boat, but was then made to take over control of the vessel by the other passengers.

News.title: Belfast boxing legend Close dies aged 57
News.content:
Ray Close, the Belfast boxer who almost handed Chris Eubank the first defeat of his career, has died at the age of 57.

One of the most gifted boxers Northern Ireland has produced, Close was born in 1969 and turned professional in 1988 after a decorated amateur career.

Close won the EBU super-middleweight title on St Patrick's Day in 1993 but it was his bouts against Eubank for which he will be most remembered.

Eubank, who had won all 35 of his professional bouts, was the defending WBO super-middleweight champion in May 1993 but Close pushed him all the way in Glasgow and the pair could not be separated on the scorecards.

A rematch took place at a raucous King's Hall in Belfast the following year and Close put in another strong performance but lost on a split decision.

A third fight was scheduled to take place but Close's boxing licence was revoked by the British Boxing Board of Control before it could take place after a MRI scan revealed two lesions on his brain.

Close would later return to the ring after obtaining a licence in the USA and he won all five of his bouts in Illinois, the last of which was a knockout victory over Larry Willis in June 1997.

His professional record reads as 25 victories, three defeats and one draw - which came against Eubank.

News.title: Alison Hammond has heart check-up in hospital after rushing off This Morning while on air
News.content:
Alison Hammond went to hospital for a heart check-up after leaving ITV's This Morning midway through Friday's show, but has assured followers she is "fine".

The presenter, 51, left the programme during its live broadcast, appearing to clutch her chest as she was assisted off the set by co-host Dermot O'Leary. He later told viewers she was "feeling a little unwell".

In a video posted from a hospital bed, external on Friday afternoon, Hammond said she had "a little bit of a palpitation" during the show but was feeling OK and was undergoing tests.

"I know you're all worried about me," she said. "Honestly, I am fine. First of all, I'm getting my old ticker checked out."

News.title: 'Cult' priest guilty of rape and assault of women
News.content:
A former priest who established a "cult" within the Church of England has been found guilty of raping a woman in his congregation.

Chris Brain was also convicted of four counts of indecent assault against three other women who were part of the Nine O'Clock Service in Sheffield in the 1980s and 1990s.

The 69-year-old was found guilty of the offences after a retrial at Inner London Crown Court, having already been found guilty of 17 indecent assaults against nine women at a trial last year.

Brain, previously of Wilmslow, in Cheshire, is in custody awaiting sentencing at a later date.

The Nine O'Clock Service, known as NOS, attracted hundreds of young people to St Thomas's church with its ground-breaking nightclub-style worship which blended rave culture, live music and prayer.

But jurors heard the group "became a cult" in which members were encouraged to cut themselves off from family and friends, leaving them "utterly dependent" on Brain, and living in fear of being ostracised if they crossed him.

Prosecutor Tim Clark KC told the court Brain had abused his position as a priest to sexually assault "a staggering number of women from his congregation".

The verdicts mean Brain has now been convicted of a total of 22 sexual offences against 13 women.

Following his latest convictions, South Yorkshire Police said Brain was a "devious and arrogant sexual predator who caused lasting harm to these women".

News.title: Dolly Parton sings Jolene in Welsh in recording released after her death
News.content:
A new version of Dolly Parton's Jolene is set to be released, with parts of the song sung in Welsh by the legendary country artist.

The song was recorded before her death on 25 August, and is a collaboration with Welsh singer-songwriter Bronwen Lewis as well as Parton's niece, Jada Star.

In a seven-decade career, Parton won 10 Grammy awards, sold more than 100 million records worldwide, and wrote more than 3,000 songs.

The single will come out on 9 October, and is the second posthumous release from Parton - who was of Welsh descent.

In a teaser video released on social media, Star and Lewis explained how the song came to light.

As a proud Welsh speaker, Lewis, from Neath, had started translating some of her favourite tunes, and soon landed on the Parton classic, Jolene.

"Two years ago I posted a video of me singing the Dolly Parton classic Jolene in Welsh, external," said Lewis.

"I never expected it would go viral and definitely didn't expect it to attract the attention of Dolly's family - especially her niece Jada."

A woman who says she was gang-raped at a Cornell University fraternity told the school's investigators last year that she “felt like bait” as the attackers were “like lions around me,” according to records from the school’s disciplinary investigation.

The documents, reviewed Friday by The Associated Press, include excerpts of interviews Cornell's investigators did with the woman and the men she accused and shed more light on the university's handling of the case.

While heavily redacted, the records offer a fuller but sometimes conflicting timeline of events and a glimpse at how the men responded to the allegations. Some disputed the woman’s account and said they weren’t involved in any assault.

The woman, identified in court papers only as Jane Doe, sued Cornell and seven former students last month, alleging she was given ketamine and repeatedly assaulted at a fraternity house in October 2024.

She went to campus police three weeks after the encounter and gave a detailed account of what happened, but the local district attorney decided not to file criminal charges or push for more investigation after reviewing a police summary of her interview.

Only the school’s investigation, under the federal Title IX law, persisted, with a goal of deciding discipline for the students involved.

Lawsuit by one of the accused men reveals details on investigation

This week, a lawyer for one of the accused men filed documents from the school’s investigation in a lawsuit that seeks to overturn the university’s punishment and remove it from his academic record. They include a 99-page report on a campus hearing panel’s disciplinary findings and a summary of events submitted by the university's lawyers.

Though only a fraction of the thousands of pages amassed in the investigation, the records show the breadth of the university’s inquiry — including 50 interviews with 32 witnesses and 12 days of hearings.

Late Thursday, Gov. Kathy Hochul appointed Attorney General Letitia James as a special prosecutor to lead a renewed criminal investigation, saying she had lost faith in Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten.

According to the Title IX documents filed in court, which are only a portion of the entire investigation, the woman and several of the men gave investigators similar accounts of drug use and sexual activity that took place at the Chi Phi fraternity house — but differed sharply in how much of it was consensual.

Snapchat messages drew other men

The woman had been invited there by a fraternity member for whom she had long held strong romantic feelings and sexual interest, according to the disciplinary panel’s findings. The panel found that she initially consented to sex with that man and one of his friends, though she later alleged in her lawsuit that she had been pressured into taking ketamine, marijuana and alcohol and was too intoxicated to consent.

Then other men began showing up in the room, some drawn by a message one of the fraternity brothers sent to a Snapchat group at 1:42 a.m. using a vulgar term to advertise that a woman's body was freely available. Later, another person in the chat asked if the “shop” was still open.

The woman told investigators that her intoxication had rendered her partly defenseless. She said she remembered smoking marijuana and said she knew she took ketamine, her first time doing so, but didn’t have an independent memory of it. The drug, she said, left her in a state of “vague consciousness."

“You look like an operating human being," she told school investigators at a hearing in May of 2025. "You don’t look dead or asleep necessarily. So, lights are on, but nobody’s home. Your brain is not functioning at its proper level.”

She said some of the men inhaled drugs off her unclothed body.

“I felt like bait. I felt like lions around me. It just was a totally debilitating place to be in," she told investigators.

Accused student says he only entered room for a wellness check

One of the men the woman accused of snorting drugs off her body — but not participating in other elements of the assault — denied her account.

He told investigators he was in the room for no more than five minutes, and didn’t go there for sex.

“That was not our intentions at all. We were just checking out to see if everything” was OK, he said.

He insisted that he did not see the woman naked at any time — she was under bed coverings, he said — and did not partake in drug use. He said he sat on a couch and chatted for a few minutes, then left after the woman and another man there both indicated they were all right.

A Cornell disciplinary panel later cleared him of sexual assault or exploitation allegations, but found him responsible for attempted sexual exploitation because it didn't believe his claim to have gone to the room for altruistic reasons.

The fraternity member, who is challenging Cornell’s disciplinary process in court, also posted in the Snapchat conversation, saying what was happening in the room was not a joke, adding: “Firsthand pov not a bit.” The student later told investigators he did not remember sending the message, according to Cornell’s account.

Woman's lawsuit seeks tougher penalties

In her lawsuit, Jane Doe accused two of the other men who entered the room of performing sex acts on her without her consent, while she was partially incapacitated. She accused another man of kissing her without her consent. According to the Title IX documents, Jane Doe told investigators two other men stood at the foot of the bed acting “more like voyeurs than anything."

The lawsuit seeks to hold all seven men liable for rape. She is asking for unspecified damages.

Cornell hasn’t detailed the results of its investigation, but said it resulted in some students being expelled.

The man who filed the lawsuit challenging his punishment was allowed to stay at Cornell, but he was ordered to stay away from the woman, take a class on sexual harassment and bystander intervention, and write a paper reflecting on the circumstances for which he was found responsible and include a proposal to train other students on preventing sexual harassment.
