The Arsenal Supporters’ Trust said it had been given guarantees the club had “no current plans” to reduce ordinary seating or move fans to increase corporate numbers.

Christos Tzolis is to return to Arsenal for assessment after sustaining a suspected muscle injury with Greece. Germany’s Kai Havertz pulled out of international duty after picking up an injury against the Netherlands but Arsenal are believed to be hopeful he could feature against Leeds next Saturday.

Sports.title: Manchester City whistleblower Rui Pinto to leave Portugal over safety fears
Sports.content:
Rui Pinto has revealed he is preparing to leave Portugal because he fears for his safety after being informed that his participation in the country’s witness protection programme has been terminated.

The Football Leaks founder claimed he has received “multiple death threats” and is facing “the serious risk of an assassination attempt against me” after being informed of the decision by Portuguese authorities on Wednesday. That came two days after Manchester City were found guilty of 115 charges by an independent commission – an investigation that was prompted by Pinto’s leaks of thousands of private documents.

He said in a statement on Friday that the timing and circumstances of the decision to end his witness protection had left him facing a serious threat to his safety. “On 30 September 2026, just hours after the verdict officially confirming Manchester City’s guilt, the commission responsible for Portugal’s witness protection programme informed me of its decision to terminate my participation in the programme and withdraw my police protection, thereby knowingly placing me in a life-threatening situation,” he wrote on X.

“Given these circumstances, I have no alternative but to relocate, within the next few days, to an undisclosed location for an indefinite period of time, due to the multiple death threats I have received and the serious risk of an assassination attempt against me. For this reason, I have just set up a GoFundMe campaign and I am asking for everyone’s support to help me survive this serious situation created by the Portuguese state, which, as I have already stated, has knowingly decided to place my life at risk.”

The GoFundMe campaign’s target has been set at €3m (£2.55m) and had received €4,000 in the first half-hour after it was posted. “I would like to take this opportunity to extend a special thanks to everyone who continues to support Football Leaks, and I can give everyone one guarantee: the fight will most certainly continue,” Pinto added.

Earlier, the 37-year-old’s lawyers confirmed that they will appeal against the decision that was taken by the Portuguese authorities and said ending his protection would leave him “more vulnerable than at any point since 2020”. They argued that it was taken without giving him an opportunity to be heard and have described the circumstances surrounding it as a “failure to respect the rule of law”.

In a request to Portugal’s Ministry of Justice, the lawyers asked the government to reconsider the decision, disclose the material on which the latest risk assessment was based and ensure that his protection continues.

“His situation is now critical,” said his lawyers in a statement. “The threats against him are not merely theoretical: last April, he was assaulted in Lisbon. His revelations implicated powerful individuals with substantial resources, and many of the resulting legal proceedings are still ongoing, as demonstrated by the decision issued just a few days ago by the Premier League’s independent commission concerning Manchester City. Abruptly deprived of his protected residence and placed in a situation of extreme precariousness, Rui Pinto will now be more vulnerable than at any point since 2020.”

Pinto entered Portugal’s protection programme after cooperating with the country’s justice authorities. His revelations have subsequently been used by judicial, tax and sporting authorities across Europe, including the Premier League’s investigation into City’s alleged financial irregularities. Pinto’s lawyers argue that the authorities should take into account both his cooperation with the justice system and the continuing risks associated with his disclosures before ending his protection.

“This decision, and the manner in which it was taken, regrettably fail to respect the rule of law and constitute an act of state terrorism. We cannot accept this,” they added.

Sports.title: Slegers feels support from Arsenal hierarchy despite dismal run but biggest test looms
Sports.content:
Renée Slegers says she has felt the full support of Arsenal’s board and praised her senior players for showing “monumental leadership” this week as she vows to find solutions to recent poor form before Sunday’s pivotal trip to Manchester City.

One win in five matches has put Slegers under mounting pressure. Arsenal let slip a two-goal lead to draw at Paris FC in the Women’s ­Champions League on Wednesday and in the WSL they have slipped seven points behind City, the ­leaders and defending champions, having scored only twice in their four league games.

Slegers was in a determined mood on Friday, speaking of a “strong togetherness” at the club. Asked whether she felt the full support of the board, she replied: “Yes, that’s what I felt. That’s been positive and that’s helped me. The club’s leadership has been really good and positive for me in this moment because everyone thinks this is a difficult time and this is not something that we want for the team and for the club.

“But the leadership from Clare [Wheatley, the director of football], Rich [Garlick, CEO], James [King, director of football operations], Jodie [Taylor, technical director] has been superb. So I want to give everything back to the club.

“There’s been a lot of contact, of course. There’s a strong ­togetherness and I’ve really felt their support and they’re here with us, which I’m very grateful for, of course, because I care so much for the team, for the club. I believe in the potential that we ­possess. I believe we can come out of this.”

The 37-year-old Dutchwoman began with an apology to the media for her no-show after Wednesday’s game, when Arsenal conceded a bizarre penalty after Leah Williamson was penalised for handling the ball in the area when she thought she was taking a goal-kick. Slegers’s assistant Aaron D’Antino stepped in.

“After the game there was emotion from my end,” Slegers said. “[I] make the decision to be with the team instead.” She said that had felt important but added: “I will be there next time. I said to the team: ‘I’m angry, I’m really angry, and let’s try to use the emotions that we’re feeling and let it fuel us moving forward, so that’s definitely part of what I hope [to see] and what I believe is going to help us in the right direction.”

Sunday presents a huge challenge against a side who have a 100% record in the WSL this season and have won all their home league matches since Andrée Jeglertz took over as head coach in the summer of 2025.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Slegers praised her squad for their response since Wednesday, saying her “players have been brilliant – I’ve seen the best sides of them”.

“What the group has shown, it’s something I haven’t seen before,” she said. “The captains in the team they’ve been monumental; it’s the strongest leadership I’ve seen so far working within football, they’ve been amazing. They’re very calm, composed, solution-orientated and laser-focused. It was a great moment and I think vital for us moving forward.

“It’s strange because I have to be finding a solution, so I have to be calm, I have to give direction, I have to lead now. But at the same time, what I also feel is gratitude for how everyone is responding and how together we are and how the session on the pitch was today. It was really, really good.”

Sports.title: Robbie Savage steps up to take Peterborough job: ‘All I want is a chance’
Sports.content:
Robbie Savage has been confirmed as the new manager of League One strugglers Peterborough.

Savage has left his role at National League side Forest Green Rovers and signed a long-term contract at Posh, who are currently second from bottom and sacked Luke Williams last month. His appointment marks his first Football League role since retiring as a player in 2011, and Savage said he is relishing the opportunity to prove any doubters wrong.

“Everyone’s entitled to their opinion but all I want is a chance. I’ve done it all my life,” Savage said. “When I was released by Manchester United I was told I wasn’t good enough, when I moved to Leicester I wasn’t in the team and had to battle. Nobody’s given me anything in this world, I’ve earned it and I’ve worked hard for it.

“Judge me when we start playing football – that’s what I love. I’m passionate and emotional and I just want to watch this young team give me everything, play that explosive style of football.”

Savage started his managerial career at Macclesfield, whom he steered to promotion to National League North before moving to Forest Green in 2025. He is expected to meet the players for the first time on Sunday before taking charge for in Tuesday’s Football League Trophy tie against Ipswich Under-21s.

Quick Guide How do I 

The Peterborough chair, Darragh MacAnthony, said: “Excitement is the word I can use to describe the appointment of Robbie Savage as our new manager – a word I personally haven’t used about our football club for too long. His personality, character and mindset is something we need top to bottom. Nobody will work harder to get us up and running again than Robbie. The board were blown away by him in an extensive interview, and his hunger to fix our issues and get confidence back into our talented squad is what I am most excited by.”

Sports.title: Unai Emery makes shock claim over Premier League rivals after Man City verdict
Sports.content:
Unai Emery appears to have hinted that other Premier League clubs inflate their budgets following the guilty verdict on Manchester City.

In one of football's biggest-ever stories, City have been found guilty by an independent commission on all of their charges in relation to Premier League financial rule breaches.



3 City have officially launched an appeal after being found guilty on all charges over Premier League finance rule breaches Credit: AFP

They are said to have arranged 'sham contracts' to artificially inflate revenue and reduce costs between the 2009/10 and 2017/18 seasons, with other charges being for noncooperation in the investigation.

City announced on Friday that they have launched an appeal against the verdict as they face the prospect of huge sanctions, which remain undecided, including a heavy points deduction and stripped titles.

It's a monumental case that could affect the past, present and future of the English top flight, as well as the reputations of managers and players involved at the club during the investigated period of time.



However, Aston Villa boss Emery has suggested that City are not the only club that have gone against financial regulations.

Speaking to Diario de Sevilla on the verdict, via Mundo Deportivo, he said: "It's an issue that was already known.



"Because we all have our restrictions, we have to sell players to comply with Financial Fair Play; we have to figure out how to draw up contracts with new players.

"Fair Play seeks financial balance so that what is generated is spent, and there is no inflation.



"Yes, many other clubs have inflated their budgets, and now it's coming to light, and naturally there's a decline."

Emery added: "That's something the courts and those in charge will have to decide.

"I feel sorry for how that team played. With (Pep) Guardiola, there were times when they were unbeatable."

3 Emery has suggested that other clubs have inflated budgets in what is a shock claim amid the recent verdict Credit: Getty



What is the latest on City and their charges?

Now that City have appealed, an appeal process is set to follow, and as per Premier League rules, a hearing must be held within 12 weeks.

This can only last five days, and then a decision will be due within 30 days of its conclusion.

As talkSPORT reported, City will argue that the so-called 'tagged sponsorship payments', which totalled £830million, came from the Abu Dhabi Government, not owners Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG).

This applies to state-controlled entities such as Etihad Airways and Etisalat, yet the former previously refuted funding from the Abu Dhabi Government as "false".



But this defence has been contradicted by their title sponsor, Etihad.

In 2015, a lobbying coalition formed by American Airlines, Delta Air Lines and United Airlines called the 'Partnership for Open and Fair Skies' wrote to the United States departments of Commerce, Transportation and State.

3 City face serious sanctions for the charges that span across a period of nine seasons Credit: Getty

They argued that Etihad had gained a competitive advantage by receiving huge sums from the Abu Dhabi Government.



A 2010 internal report that was written for Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahya, the Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi, is cited, which does in fact claim that the Abu Dhabi Government, which was phrased as 'Executive Council', did cover the sponsorship of City.

City may be able to use this to their advantage during their appeal, but Etihad's response was to flatly deny any government funding in relation to their deal with the club.

"The assertion that the Abu Dhabi Government paid for Etihad's sponsorship of English Premier League football club Manchester City is equally false," Etihad argued.

"In 2011 Etihad and Manchester City entered into a 10-year sponsorship agreement, which included naming rights for Manchester City's stadium. Etihad funded this sponsorship from its own liquidity. It is not uncommon for airlines to have sponsorships with sports teams and their venues…



"We are government-owned and have been since our founding. We are and have always been clear that we do not receive any subsidies from the Abu Dhabi government, and that we are financed through a combination of equity, shareholder and commercial loans.

"Our shareholders' equity and loans are not subsidies under any applicable definition; they are the means by which the Abu Dhabi government has sensibly invested in a successful business model."

Sports.title: Son of Ballon d’Or winner joins non-league club after spells with Chelsea and Tottenham
Sports.content:
Son of Ballon d’Or winner joins non-league club after spells with Chelsea and Tottenham

Andriy Shevchenko’s son Kristian has joined non-league side Sholing FC ahead of their FA Cup third-round qualifying match this weekend.

The 19-year-old, who was born and raised in London, has spent his youth career in the academies of Chelsea, Tottenham, and Watford.



3 Andriy Shevchenko's son Kristian could make his FA Cup debut this weekend Credit: Getty

The teenager, who is the second of the 2004 Ballon d'Or winner's four sons, is eligible to play for England at international level.

However, the right winger is already following in his father's footsteps by being capped at Under-19 and Under-20 level with Ukraine.

Kristian Shevchenko joins Sholing FC

The attacker began his football journey in Chelsea’s academy, the club where his dad, Andriy, spent three years from 2006 until 2009.



He then joined their London rivals, Tottenham, in December 2022, where he worked under ex-Manchester City midfielder Yaya Touré.

Eight months later, Shevchenko moved to Watford, where he spent the next two years progressing through the Hornets' youth ranks.



The Ukrainian signed a professional contract with the Championship outfit in July 2025 but never made a senior appearance.

He has now taken the next step in his career by joining Sholing, who currently sit 16th in the Southern League Premier Division South.



The Boatmen are only five points above the bottom of the table, having won just three of their eight league fixtures this season.

Shevchenko's Sholing debut, however, could come in FA Cup third-round qualifying action this Saturday.

3 Shevchenko was involved in FA Youth Cup action for Watford but never made a senior appearance Credit: Getty

3 He also represented Ukraine at the 2025 FIFA U20 World Cup Credit: Getty



Paul Doswell's men beat Tiverton Town and Andover New Street to earn a match-up with National League South side Ebbsfleet United.

Should Sholing shock the team one step above them in the pyramid, then they will receive £5,625 from the competition’s prize fund.

The Boatmen, who would still bag £1,875 with a defeat, have only ever reached the Fourth Qualifying Round once before in their history.

Sholing, who won three of their last five games across all competitions, lost at that stage to Torquay United in 2020/21.



Shevchenko is not the only new face in the door at the Mortgage Decisions Stadium, with Jonas Mukuna also joining the club.

His famous father, Andriy, meanwhile, won the FA Cup as a player during his time at Chelsea, scoring 22 goals in 77 appearances.

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel reveals Bukayo Saka role in deciding competition between two England stars
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel has explained how his decision over who plays right-back for England involves how they can support Bukayo Saka.

Since starting as the Three Lions head coach in January 2025, Tuchel has selected numerous right-backs in his teams.



3 Saka is a regular for England, and Tuchel says he plays a role in who he chooses at right-back, with Quansah (right) one option Credit: Getty

Djed Spence has made the most such appearances in all competitions with 14, whilst Reece James is close behind on 13.

However, both players missed out on the latest England squad amid their respective fitness issues, whilst Tino Livramento withdrew with an injury.

Instead, Real Madrid target Jarell Quansah and Trent Alexander-Arnold have played in the role against Spain and the Czech Republic during the new Nations League campaign so far.



They have started one game each, with the latter appearing from the off for the first time under Tuchel against Czechia earlier this week.

Ahead of the trip to Croatia on Saturday, live on talkSPORT, Tuchel was asked about his thought process behind who he plays in the defensive role for England.



He then revealed that Saka, who has started in both matches during the international break, is someone who plays into this thinking in a bid to get the best out of him at right wing.

Saka role in England right-back selection

"It's easy, it's a competition between Trent and Jarell," Tuchel said to talkSPORT. "It's not isolated; it's just them under the microscope.



"It's also how we want to play: what strengths does the opponent have? Where do we want to implement ourselves?

"And how's the connection, for example, with Bukayo? What is a good addition to Bukayo that makes life for Bukayo easier, and helps him?

"So, a lot of things to consider, and it's an easy choice because we cannot get it wrong between the two; they're two good right-backs."

3 Alexander-Arnold (right) is another player who can support Saka from right-back for England with his pace and passing Credit: Getty



3 Tuchel has spoken on the importance of naming a right-sided defender that can get the best out of Saka Credit: Getty

Who could start at right-back against Croatia?

Alexander-Arnold had only played one match under Tuchel before he featured in the 2-0 win away to Czechia.

The Madrid full-back repaid the trust shown in him by assisting Anthony Gordon with an excellent cross for the opening goal.

In fact, Alexander-Arnold played the full 90 minutes in Prague in a performance that could grant him another start against Croatia.



Alongside Quansah, Trevoh Chalobah and Ezri Konsa are two other players who could play at right-back if needed.

However, the pair are more likely to feature at centre-back if they were to play.

Tuchel therefore has plenty of options to choose from, but has made it clear that Quansah and Alexander-Arnold are his competing duo.

Sports.title: Jordan Pickford details Thomas Tuchel message before being dropped for England matches
Sports.content:
Jordan Pickford has cited competition as the reason for his recent England omissions by Thomas Tuchel.

Pickford was benched in both Nations League matches against Spain and the Czech Republic, with James Trafford the chosen goalkeeper.



3 Trafford (left) only had two caps before this camp but has played in both England matches ahead of Pickford Credit: Getty

The decision to drop the Everton star from each starting XI came as a surprise given that he has been the long-term no. 1 for England since his debut in 2017.

Pickford also won his 19th World Cup appearance during the summer, which is the all-time Three Lions record, and has 91 caps overall.

Speaking to the media, he all but confirmed that he will start in goal for England when they face Croatia on Saturday, live on talkSPORT, as Trafford has now met his international break quota of two matches.



And during an interview with talkSPORT's Faye Carruthers, he revealed what head coach Tuchel told him ahead of the camp about his team absences.

What did Tuchel say to Pickford?

"He said I've done nothing wrong. New competition after the World Cup; he wanted to give Trafford a go to see how he is.



"He's started well at Leeds, so I think he wants to have competition against me, and that's great. He's the manager, a top manager, and you've got to respect that.

"Then it's about me - what do I need to do more? How can I keep pushing my boundaries and break that ceiling again? That's what I love to do, that's why I love football."



On the competition with other goalkeepers, he added: "I won't be looking over my shoulder; I'll be focusing on myself, how I can improve, how I can keep developing.

"We've had good competition over the years... Harty (Joe Hart), Jack Butland, we've always had good 'keepers coming through and a lot of 'keepers playing in the Prem (Premier League).

"So the competition is always there, and it's about me focusing on me, being the best version of myself. I think that's what every 'keeper would do and, as long as I focus on me, I'll keep improving."

3 Pickford has explained that Tuchel wanted to give Trafford a chance in goal against Spain and Czechia, so that's why he was benched Credit: Getty



Pickford reveals next ambition

The legendary Peter Shilton has made the most appearances in goal for England, with his 125 caps also the country's overall leading tally.

With starts against Croatia and Czechia now on the horizon for Pickford, he is set to end the international break on a total of 93 caps.

It means he is closing in on the landmark figure of 100 appearances for England, something that only ten players have managed to hit.

Now 32-years-old, Pickford has plenty more years left in the tank at international level, with goalkeepers typically among the last players to retire from football.



So when asked about his future goals with England, he explained: "My ambition is just to focus on me, being who I want to be and who I'm striving to be.

"Just keep improving day in, day out, always setting goals. There's not many people who've got 100 caps, so that's my first ambition.

3 Pickford is set to return to the starting XI, and is setting his sights on reaching 100 caps for England Credit: Getty

"I want to keep playing at World Cups, I want to keep being at the Euros, I want to play at major tournaments.



"That's the ambition, so the hard work never stops, and I'll always push those boundaries to keep improving."

Sports.title: Key Man City defence in appeal on guilty verdict contradicted by club’s own sponsors
Sports.content:
Key Man City defence in appeal on guilty verdict contradicted by club’s own sponsors

One of Manchester City’s key defences in their appeal against the Premier League has been contradicted by title sponsor Etihad Airways.

City will argue commercial revenue totalling £830million was paid by the Abu Dhabi Government.

3 Man City's 61,000-capacity stadium is named after principal sponsor Etihad Airways Credit: PA

The independent Commission concluded Sheikh Mansour's Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG) instead made the payments over a nine-year period spanning from 2009 to 2018.

City are therefore guilty of disguising equity as commercial revenue, but have lodged an appeal.

City also maintain Abu Dhabi government funding is within the Premier League rules because Etihad, and fellow sponsor Etisalat, are State-controlled.

Yet the club's arguments are undermined by Etihad as well as Man City's own arguments to the Court of Arbitration for Sport in July 2020.

Evidence that undermines Man City’s defence

In 2015, the 'Partnership for Open and Fair Skies' - a lobbying coalition formed by American Airlines, Delta Air Lines, and United Airlines - wrote to the US departments of Commerce, Transportation and State, arguing Etihad gained a competitive advantage due to receiving huge sums from the Abu Dhabi Government.

A 2010 internal report written for the Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi, Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahya, is cited, which does indeed claim the Abu Dhabi Government, or 'Executive Council' as it is phrased, did cover the sponsorship of Manchester City. City may be able to use this to their advantage in their appeal.

Yet Etihad's response was to flatly deny any government funding in relation to their deal with Manchester City.

“The assertion that the Abu Dhabi Government paid for Etihad’s sponsorship of English Premier League football club Manchester City is equally false," Etihad argued.

“In 2011 Etihad and Manchester City entered into a 10-year sponsorship agreement, which included naming rights for Manchester City’s stadium. Etihad funded this sponsorship from its own liquidity. It is not uncommon for airlines to have sponsorships with sports teams and their venues…

3 City won three Premier League titles during the nine-year period in which their offences took place Credit: Getty

"We are government-owned and have been since our founding. We are and have always been clear that we do not receive any subsidies from the Abu Dhabi government, and that we are financed through a combination of equity, shareholder and commercial loans.

"Our shareholders’ equity and loans are not subsidies under any applicable definition; they are the means by which the Abu Dhabi government has sensibly invested in a successful business model.”

Etihad's comments go firmly against City's argument, as stated in the verdict, that 'AD Sponsors had from time to time applied for financial assistance from the AD Government towards their liability to pay the Recorded Sponsorship Fees.'

Due to redacted names, multiple sponsors being involved, and the phrase 'from time to time', City could make a case for other sponsors, but Etihad's on-record denial doesn't help the club's position, according to multiple legal sources talkSPORT has spoken to.

Man City sources do not believe Etihad’s statement undermines their appeal.

They will argue Etihad got funding from the Crown Prince Court for the purpose of promoting Abu Dhabi and that this became part of the airline’s liquidity.

3 Etihad Airways made a statement in 2015 that undermines Man City's current appeal Credit: Getty

However, City have also changed their argument made to the Court of Arbitration for Sport in 2020.

A CAS witness statement from former Etihad chief executive James Hogan makes clear, "Neither [Sheikh Mansour] nor his private investment vehicle ADUG, nor any entity on their behalf, has funded or reimbursed the sponsorship obligations of Etihad under the sponsorship agreements. The sponsorship obligations were paid out of Etihad's own funds."

Man City maintains a "firm position, on multiple grounds, [that] the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact and is unsafe.

"The Club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case."

However, the fact that their title sponsor refutes one of their leading arguments, and the club offered a different explanation to CAS in successfully overturning their UEFA charges, all provide clear inconsistencies.

The independent Panel, which considered the explanation that so-called 'sham' commercial deals were paid by the Abu Dhabi Government, not ADUG, concluded the argument was "concocted well after the event".

Sports.title: Robbie Savage reveals talkSPORT influence before taking new EFL job
Sports.content:
Robbie Savage has revealed Darragh MacAnthony was a driving factor in his decision to take the Peterborough job.

Savage was named as the new man in charge at London Road on Friday, leaving Forest Green Rovers to land his first managerial role in the EFL.



5 After days of speculation, Robbie Savage has been confirmed as Peterborough's new manager Credit: Getty

talkSPORT previously reported the Welshman was close to being appointed, after he missed Forest Green’s 1-1 draw with Wealdstone on Tuesday night as he neared an agreement with Posh.

He succeeds Luke Williams as manager after the 45-year-old was sacked last month, with the role remaining vacant until now.

Savage's new team are 23rd in League One, having won just once in eight games so far this season.



The 51-year-old is tasked with transforming Peterborough's fortunes, having earned his stripes as a coach at Forest Green and Macclesfield before then.

His time in Nailsworth saw his side finish seventh in the National League last term, where they missed out on EFL promotion in the play-offs, while Savage guided Macclesfield to the Northern Premier League Premier Division title in 2025.



Savage savouring MacAnthony partnership

After his appointment at London Road was confirmed, Savage joined talkSPORT's Max Scott and Andy Jacobs to discuss his new role.

And the former Premier League midfielder revealed that Peterborough chairman MacAnthony was a major influence in his decision to take charge of the League One side.



MacAnthony is a friend of talkSPORT, having hosted several shows this summer, and has held his position at the Posh since 2006, during which time he has overseen four promotions and three EFL trophy glories.

On his new chairman, Savage told talkSPORT: “That's one of the reasons why I've accepted the opportunity - to work with Darragh.

“Because I know how passionate he is about his football club and how much it means to him, not just him, but all the staff.

5 MacAnthony was the youngest chairman in the football league when he took over at Peterborough in 2006, aged 30 Credit: Alamy



“So, it's a brilliant football club. I've studied my managerial career and my sporting directorship when I was at Macclesfield on this model of attacking football, of assets - selling them on.

“So when this opportunity came about, I think it came about because of the way my teams have played.

“I think we've got to go back to the DNA of Peterborough and I've got an owner in Darragh who's so passionate.

"I know people say we're both spiky characters - listen, Dale Vince [the owner] at Forest Green was amazing with me. People said the same thing there, but we became very, very good friends because we're both honest, transparent people who care.



“And Darragh's certainly of that mould, so I can't wait to work with everybody.”

With Savage now getting a chance to prove himself in the Football League, he shared his goals to push Peterborough up the table after back-to-back 18th place finishes in League One.

5 Savage has climbed from English football's seventh tier to League One in three years since starting his managerial career Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

He continued: “The last three years - 18th, 18th, 23rd as it stands - it's a good time to come in. It's a reset.



"I'm going to try and hit the ground running, but it might take time. I just want a chance to show people what I can do.

"A lot of people might be thinking, ‘Wow, he's come from non-league to a massive club in League One’, but I've earned the right. I've not been a manager who's gone into the top level straight away; I wanted to earn it.

“I started at Step 5. Built a football club, given a community their football club back in Macclesfield. Broke records.

"People might say, 'Well, he should have done that. He had the biggest budget' That's nonsense. You've still got to beat what’s in front of you because Macclesfield was everybody's cup final at those levels.



Moving on to his biggest club yet, Savage shared his excitement ahead of starting work with MacAnthony at Peterborough, especially given that the pair have never actually met in person.

5 MacAnthony is among the EFL's most recognisable chairmen Credit: Getty

While they are yet to speak in the flesh, the ex-Wales international revealed he had previously sought out the advice of both MacAnthony and talkSPORT's Simon Jordan when starting out as a manager.

He said: “Now I'm at Peterborough. There's an added pressure now with a high-profile owner who's brilliant, by the way. Can't wait to work with him. Never met him in person, which is incredible.



“So I hear all this about our friendship, and that friendship's been built on phone calls because I've seen him on the TV, heard him on talkSPORT.

“My friendship with Simon Jordan come about that way also. I get people's number, because when I was at Macclesfield building a club, I wanted to tap into Darragh and to Simon.

“They'd run football clubs so I could get out and gain knowledge and speak to people who were better than me at what they do. So, that's how our friendship came about, because Darragh knew I loved the model.

“So, again, our relationship formed through me wanting to learn, but we've never met in person."



5 Posh have not scored in three of their past five League One matches Credit: Getty

MacAnthony and Jordan are not the only talkSPORT favourites Savage has been listening to, with our chief football commentator Adrian Durham previously outlining what he wanted to see from the new manager of his beloved Posh.

"I spoke to Ade when I was given permission to speak to the Football Club. He told me about the history, which I knew anyway.

"Chris Turner has got a statue outside the stadium. I think his Cambridge United side came here and won 5-1. We're playing them on November 28th, which will be huge for our fans.



"Tommy Robson, also there's a statue going up near Future, the winger, who was brilliant. He told me all about that, told me everything about the club.

"I think this club has never won a league since 1973-74. I think, listening to lots of fans, they would like to be the best team in the league one day. Yes, they've gone up through the play-offs.

"It might be a lot to do this season, but can we produce a team where the fans can say they're the best team in the league?

"I think that's what Ade said to me. He's a passionate fan, Andy, as you know. I'm sure that he'll want his side to get back to what the club's built its history on."

Sports.title: Dutch doctor suggests Brian Brobbey has ‘very serious’ injury in angry rant
Sports.content:
Brian Brobbey has returned to Sunderland, and the club have been warned that his injury is more serious than they originally thought.

The Dutchman has started strongly in the Premier League this season, scoring a hat-trick for the Black Cats against Manchester City in his last top-flight outing.



2 Brian Brobbey suffered a significant hamstring injury Credit: Getty

He had started all five league games for the Wearsiders before joining his national team squad for the international break.

In the Netherlands 1-1 draw against Germany, Brobbey was on the pitch for 35 minutes until an injury forced him off.

Brian Brobbey injury update

The former Ajax star lasted a little over half an hour in Xavi's first match as a manager, and suffered a hamstring issue which has seen him replaced by Joshua Zirkzee.



However, former PSV doctor Cees-Rein van den Hoogenband revealed the issue is more than a little problem for Sunderland.

He said: "That has a huge medical impact. Everyone can see that from the large number of injuries, both nationally and internationally.



"However, I have no illusion that anyone will ever listen. The commercial interests are so incredibly high.

"I hold my breath. I fear that many more will follow. It is like trying to mop up water with the tap still running, because players simply do not get the rest they need.



"Of course, it remains a contact sport. If something happens during a tackle, like with Cody [Gakpo], that’s all part of the game.

"But if you look at Brobbey, he has a very serious hamstring injury. That’s a typical example of overuse.

2 Brobbey has scored 10 goals for Sunderland since joining the club last year Credit: AFP

"The Premier League is already so tough with two matches a week, and then they throw in a Nations League period like this with four matches in two weeks. Incomprehensible.



"In my time as club doctor at PSV, I actually had it very easy. It has really become much tougher."

Additionally, Liverpool’s Cody Gakpo, Tottenham Hotspur’s Jan Paul van Hecke and PSV Eindhoven’s Lutsharel Geertruida have left the national team because of injuries.

The Black Cats signed the striker from Ajax in September 2025 for around €20million (£17m).

Brobbey, who is the ninth-most-owned striker in Fantasy Premier League, played 32 games for Sunderland last season and registered seven goals and an assist.



Sunderland boss Regis Le Bris will be desperate for the injury not to be long-term as the Black Cats also have Europa League fixtures to compete in - including against AC Milan at the San Siro.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta plays influential role in Arsenal decision on Emirates Stadium expansion
Sports.content:
Arsenal have decided against a ‘huge-scale masterplan’ to expand the Emirates Stadium.

The Gunners had considered various ways to increase the stadium’s capacity for around two years.

4 Arsenal have opted against increasing the capacity of the Emirates Stadium Credit: Getty

The Emirates, which opened in 2006, has a capacity of 60,700; however, the club hoped to increase the numbers to beyond 70,000.

It was previously revealed by talkSPORT that the project could potentially cost up to £500million, with the stadium having cost £390m to build two decades ago.

Club chiefs considered moving to an alternative venue whilst work was carried out, with Wembley Stadium identified as a possible makeshift stadium.

However, plans have now been scrapped with boss Mikel Arteta preferring not to disrupt his side’s success by playing home matches elsewhere.

North London rivals Tottenham played their home games at Wembley after they left White Hart Lane.

Arsenal have now committed to a ‘continued evolution’ of the Emirates Stadium.

At the recent Arsenal Advisory Board meeting, co-chairman Josh Kroenke and chief executive officer Richard Garlick outlined the club’s plan regarding the stadium.

Plans for Emirates expansion aborted

A club statement read: "The discussion covered investment in player talent, the longer-term plans for our men’s and women’s training ground, Sobha Realty Training Centre and developments such as the appointment of Pascal De Maesschalck as part of our ambitions for a world-class Academy.

"Richard also pointed towards the need to balance competitiveness with financial discipline.

"We updated members on the continued evolution of Emirates Stadium, our plans for retail growth and transformation and our continued focus on partnerships.

“We also discussed steps we will take to deepen our connection with supporters even further, wherever they are in the world.

4 Gunners boss Mikel Arteta was a driving force behind the decision Credit: Getty

4 The Tottenham Hotspur Stadium will remain as London's biggest club stadium Credit: Getty

"We are currently recruiting a Chief Marketing Officer to drive this.

"We shared a commitment to continued evolution of Emirates Stadium, rather than a huge-scale masterplan, building on improvements we’ve made to date in partnership with our catering partner, Legends, the introduction of safe standing (this season in the Clock End, and next season in the North Bank), improving hospitality and retail experiences, and upgrading visitor experiences."

Arsenal reportedly looked into the idea of making the Emirates Stadium the biggest Premier League stadium in London.

As it stands, the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium holds that honour with 63,000 fans able to pack into the state-of-the-art arena.

However, Arsenal say they will continue to improve the matchday experience for fans.

That includes improving 5G mobile connectivity inside the stadium, with progress expected on that front before the end of the season.

4 Arsenal have instead planned to enhance the matchday experience for all supporters Credit: Getty

Arsenal Supporters Trust statement

On hearing the news that the stadium will not be renovated, Arsenal Supporters’ Trust said: "No capacity changes at the Emirates. Focus will be on facilities behind the scenes.

"Expect more hospitality offerings. Once again, we secured a commitment from the club that they have no current plans to move or reduce any general admission places.

“But all supporters must be vigilant to this and repeat the importance of custodianship."

Sports.title: Controversial NBA star JR Smith accused of 'hitting, grabbing or pushing' a woman in shocking court filing
Sports.content:
Controversial NBA star JR Smith accused of 'hitting, grabbing or pushing' a woman in shocking court filing

JR Smith 'intentionally, knowingly, or recklessly' caused 'bodily injury' to a member of his family or household or someone with whom he was dating, according to excerpts of the criminal complaint filed against the retired NBA star on Friday.

As previously reported by The Daily Mail, Smith was arrested Monday in Hunt County, Texas on a warrant out of Southlake and subsequently booked on a misdemeanor count of 'assault caused bodily injury family violence.' The 41-year-old has denied the allegations through his attorney in a statement provided to The Daily Mail earlier this week.

Now, The California Post has obtained a copy of the criminal complaint out of Tarrant County that accuses Smith of 'hitting, grabbing or pushing' a woman 'with [his] hand.'

The Daily Mail has sought the criminal complaint from authorities in Tarrant County, Texas.

Smith was released from jail Tuesday on a $5,000 bond.

The arrest took place Monday afternoon when Royse City Police received an alert about a suspect traveling eastbound on Interstate 30. An officer observed the vehicle and checked the license plate before pulling over the suspect. Smith was with his brother at the time of his arrest and the younger sibling took possession of his car, according to the Royse City police press release.

JR Smith 'intentionally, knowingly, or recklessly' caused 'bodily injury' to a member of his family or household or someone with whom he was dating, according to a criminal complaint

As previously reported by The Daily Mail, Smith was arrested Monday in Hunt County, Texas on a warrant out of Southlake and subsequently booked on a misdemeanor assault charge

'The wanted person was Earl Joseph [JR] Smith III and the charge was for Family Violence Assault Causing Bodily Injury,' read Tuesday's press release out of Royse City. 'A traffic stop was conducted and the driver of the vehicle was identified as Earl Joseph Smith III. The warrant was confirmed and Mr. Smith was taken into custody.'

His attorney has since issued a denial on Smith's behalf.

'JR is eager to see this matter resolved and has full confidence in the legal process,' attorney Justin A. Moore told The Daily Mail in an email. 'He is presumed innocent, and we will address this matter in Court. We ask that everyone respect the privacy of all involved throughout the process.'

The 16-year NBA veteran won two titles alongside LeBron James – one with the Cleveland Cavaliers in 2016 and another with the Los Angeles Lakers in 2020 – before retiring and briefly becoming a college golfer at North Carolina A&T State University. He graduated last spring with a bachelor's degree in Liberal Studies.

Smith does have a non-violent criminal history that includes a conviction for reckless driving over a car accident that killed his friend. Smith would later serve 24 days in prison.

Smith (right) won two titles alongside LeBron James (left) – one with the Cleveland Cavaliers in 2016 and another with the Los Angeles Lakers in 2020 – before retiring and focusing on golf

Smith of the North Carolina A&T Aggies greets playing partner Pedro Rabadan of the Elon Phoenix before the start of the Phoenix Invitational at Alamance Country Club in 2021

And in 2018, he ultimately paid $600 after throwing a fan's cell phone into a Manhattan construction site.

Smith's basketball career is largely remembered for his frequent run-ins with coaches and the league.

Not only was he fined twice for untying opponents' shoes during a game, but he seemingly referenced gangs in a 2009 Twitter post and in 2012 he was arrested for failing to appear in court after being cited for operating a motor-scooter without a valid license.

He also once threw a bowl of hot chicken tortilla soup on Cavs assistant coach Damon Jones in 2018.

Smith also raised eyebrows by going shirtless for several consecutive days while celebrating the Cavs' 2016 title, prompting then-president Barack Obama to ask head coach Tyronn Lue to intervene.

'Tell JR Smith to put on a shirt, though,' Obama told Lue. 'He can't just be walking around without a shirt for the [inaudible].'

A former Sixth Man of the Year, Smith averaged 12.4 points a game for his career with the Charlotte Hornets, Denver Nuggets, New York Knicks, Cavs and Lakers.
