World.title: Police bodycam shows Luigi Mangione arrest at Pennsylvania McDonald’s
World.content:
NewsFeed Police bodycam shows Luigi Mangione arrest at Pennsylvania McDonald’s

Newly released bodycam footage shows police arresting and searching Luigi Mangione at a McDonald’s in Altoona, Pennsylvania, on December 9, 2024. Officers found a weapon in his backpack during the arrest.

World.title: Israel could’ve ended Gaza war, freed captives sooner: Israel ex-negotiator
World.content:
Retired General Nitzan Alon says more captives could have been returned alive and a deal was possible ‘maybe a year earlier’.

A former Israeli general who was the army’s point person for hostage negotiations at the beginning of the Gaza war says that a deal to return all Israeli captives could have been achieved “much earlier” than October 2025 but it was prolonged unnecessarily.

“I think that we could [have gotten to] this point much earlier, maybe a year earlier or so, without any major implication on the other strategic goals of the war,” Major General Nitzan Alon said on Friday. “We missed it, actually. The war was too long.”

He was speaking during a Washington Institute for Near East Policy webcast marking three years since the October 7, 2023 Hamas attack on Israel preceding the genocidal war that has killed over 74,000 Palestinians.

Alon referred to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s claim that Israel must achieve “total victory” before signing a deal as “false”.

He called the October 2025 “ceasefire” a “strategic achievement” that has since curbed Hamas’s military power. But he said it could have been secured much sooner with “maybe some hostages that got killed or murdered during their captivity [coming] back home alive.”

Hamas and Israel carried out a prisoner exchange deal in October 2025 under a ceasefire agreement that saw the release of nearly 2,000 Palestinians imprisoned in Israeli jails and 20 Israeli captives held in the Gaza Strip.

“We could have – and we should have – shortened the war, brought all the hostages back, maybe a year earlier, and moved forward and maybe, you know, saved thousands of lives on both sides,” Alon told the panel discussion organised by the United States think-tank.



Alon had made similar comments in July, when he also criticised Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, saying Smotrich had opposed some of the agreements put forward at various stages and therefore could not take credit for the return of all the captives.

‘Not just a missed opportunity, it’s tragic’

Speaking to Al Jazeera on Friday, former Israeli diplomat Alan Pinkas said Netanyahu had stalled the end of the war.

“A deal was possible very soon after the Hamas attack in October 2023,” he said.

“It took almost two years before the hostages were returned, so it’s not just a missed opportunity, it’s tragic.”

Earlier this week, Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani said Israeli officials “rejected to entertain the idea” of a Hamas proposal to release all captives in exchange for a limited ceasefire soon after the attacks.

Al-Thani said Doha reached out to Israeli officials “on day one … Our message was very clear. They [Hamas leaders] are asking for a window of ceasefire to get the civilians out,” Sheikh Mohammed said in an interview with Piers Morgan. “And basically, they [the Israelis] were not interested to engage in the idea.”

Alon’s latest comments come less than a month before Israel’s October 27 legislative election, with polls showing the political battle remains at knife-edge.

Pinkas said Alon’s comments were unlikely to influence the outcome of the vote as polls already “reflect public anger” over the Netanyahu government’s failure to prevent the Hamas attacks.

A report by Israeli newspaper Haaretz claiming that United Arab Emirates President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan had warned Netanyahu about a possible attack also sparked outrage across Israel last month.

Netanyahu said he would sue the outlet over its report, which he described as “fabricated” and “false”.

World.title: France held 1-1 by Italy in Zidane home debut after Olise stunner
World.content:
Michael Olise scored another superb goal but France were held to a 1-1 draw by Italy on Friday in Zinedine Zidane’s first home game since being appointed coach of Les Bleus.

Four days after coming off the bench to score a stunning solo effort to give France a 1-0 win in Belgium, Bayern Munich star Olise again showcased his spectacular talent by smashing a shot in off the crossbar from a free kick early in the second half.

However, Inter Milan defender Alessandro Bastoni equalised for Italy midway through the second half to prevent Zidane from making it three wins out of three in charge of his country.

France, who had defender Dayot Upamecano sent off late on, lead UEFA Nations League Group A1 with seven points, with Belgium just behind on six points after a 3-0 win over Turkiye.

France and Belgium meet on Monday in their last match of this two-week international window. Italy have four points before hosting Turkiye next.

Zidane was the focus of attention as his home debut, before a packed crowd of 77,118 at the Stade de France just outside Paris, came against the same opponents as in his final game as a player.

The now 54-year-old icon and former Ballon d’Or winner never played again after being sent off for an infamous headbutt on Marco Materazzi in the 2006 World Cup final in Berlin, which Italy won on penalties.

It was a first appearance for the former Real Madrid playmaker at France’s national stadium since he played in a friendly against Mexico in May 2006, winning his 100th cap in the process.



Beyond the spotlight on his past, Zidane is trying to stamp his mark on the France team in this Nations League campaign, with one eye on the next major tournament, Euro 2028.

He was again without captain Kylian Mbappe here with the Real striker having returned to his club after suffering a knee injury while scoring the winner in Turkiye last week.

Olise returned to the starting lineup in one of six changes from the Belgium game, but new faces Jeremy Jacquet, the Liverpool defender, and Como midfielder Lucas Da Cunha again played.

Italy are rebuilding under Roberto Mancini, who has returned for a second spell as coach of a nation who have failed to qualify for the last three World Cups.

They will be the happier of the two teams with the draw in this game, although they had goalkeeper and captain Gianluigi Donnarumma to thank for keeping them in it with a host of saves in the second half.

Moise Kean should have given Italy an early lead after a sweeping move, only for his disappointing finish to be saved by Mike Maignan.

Davide Frattesi also came close in the first half while Kean had a goal disallowed for offside, as an Olise cross that landed on the bar was as close as France came.

The hosts turned up the volume after the break and Donnarumma saved from Desire Doue, Ousmane Dembele and Olise before the latter crashed in the opener on 55 minutes when Rayan Cherki laid off a dead ball.

However, Bastoni caught Da Cunha in possession just outside the France box and was left with an easy finish to pull the visitors level.

Donnarumma, formerly of Paris Saint-Germain, then produced more magic to save from Adrien Rabiot and twice from Eduardo Camavinga, before Upamecano walked for a second yellow on 85 minutes.

World.title: Bosnia’s elections explained
World.content:
NewsFeed Bosnia’s elections explained

Bosnia and Herzegovina votes on October 4 in an election that may determine whether the country breaks its political deadlock, strengthens its path towards the European Union or faces fresh divisions that could reverberate across the Balkans. Al Jazeera’s Nafisa Latić explains.

World.title: Israeli general: Gaza captives could have been freed a year earlier
World.content:
Israeli general: Gaza captives could have been freed a year earlier

NewsFeed Israeli general: Gaza captives could have been freed a year earlier

Israeli Maj. Gen. Nitzan Alon told a Washington Institute forum that all captives in Gaza could have been freed a year earlier without changing the war’s outcome. The former hostage negotiator also called for new “realistic” Israeli leadership.

World.title: India Faces Fresh Protests, This Time Over Voter Rolls
World.content:
The government deployed thousands of security personnel to prevent people from reaching Jantar Mantar, the only spot in New Delhi where protests have been authorized in recent years. Nearly a dozen metro stations were locked up, and roads were closed to prevent vehicles from reaching the area.

Those who managed to get close to the site faced large numbers of police and security forces in riot gear, who took them away on buses.

“Who doesn't allow protest? Those who know they have done something wrong,” said Banishree Das, 70, a retired educator who was among the protesters. “They have done something wrong — depriving so many people of their votes. A vote is not just a piece of paper for us.”

Much of the day was a game of cat-and-mouse. Hundreds of demonstrators were taken to police stations and holding areas, while others were driven away from the protest site and released. Then, they made their way back.

“In the past hour, they have detained us three times,” Neha Bora, the president of the All India Students’ Association, said from a bus as the police took her away. “They think by detaining us they can finish this protest?”

World.title: Iran Jails Hard-Line Lawmaker, Exposing Deep Rifts in Its Leadership
World.content:
In public comments and interviews with state television, Mr. Rasaei had regularly accused President Masoud Pezeshkian’s government of “a coup.” In one televised interview he said the negotiating team was defying the new supreme leader, Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, and forcing him to accept Washington’s conditions to end the war.

“This coup exists; this coup cannot be denied,” Mr. Rasaei said.

The case has become the latest flashpoint in divisions tearing at Iran’s leadership over the war with the United States. Officials are fighting over whether to concede and reach a deal or continue the war. Mr. Ghalibaf represents the pragmatic side favoring negotiations, and Mr. Rasaei is the face of the opposition to a deal.

The judiciary’s decision to prosecute Mr. Rasaei is largely viewed as an attempt to rein in the rowdy, and sometimes violent, hard-liners and their support base, analysts say. The hard-line supporters physically assaulted Mr. Pezeshkian and the foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, at the funeral of Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, the supreme leader who was killed in February at the start of the war.

“By prosecuting one of the most prominent critics of engagement with the U.S., the system wants to send a domestic message to the rest of the critics that it will not tolerate dissent if a deal comes through,” said Sina Azodi, the director of the Middle East studies program at George Washington University.

World.title: Investigators Seek Motive for FlyDubai Cockpit Attack
World.content:
Investigators on Thursday were trying to determine what motivated the co-pilot on a flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv to stab the pilot, a midair cockpit attack that nearly resulted in catastrophe.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of Israel suggested in a television interview on Thursday that the co-pilot, who Israeli officials have identified as an Omani citizen, was ideologically motivated.

“We know that he underwent Islamist radical indoctrination,” Mr. Netanyahu told Fox News, saying that investigators had learned this from the man’s “personal information.” He did not provide further details, and the man’s identity has not been made public.

In a video released by Mr. Netanyahu’s office on Thursday, Yaniv Hayoun, an Israeli passenger said to be the first to grab the co-pilot, recounted him saying “Kill me! Kill me!” in English. Mr. Hayoun said he took that to mean that “he had failed in his mission and preferred to die.”

World.title: UK-Iranian Man Arrested in Connection to RAF Fairford Air Base Incident
World.content:
The new arrest came just days after the police arrested five men who had been traveling early Sunday morning in white vans near the air base, called R.A.F. Fairford, which has been used by American bombers in the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran. The men were released on bail a day later after the authorities did not discover explosives in the vans.

But the police have repeatedly said the men remain under investigation. Prime Minister Andy Burnham said this week that the British government believes Iran played a part in planning the events that unfolded on Sunday.

Iran has denied the accusations. Abbas Araghchi, Iran’s foreign minister, wrote on social media on Wednesday: “I can confirm Iran’s belief that releasing supposed terrorists working for foreign states really says it all. You’re barking up the wrong tree.”

The incident near the air base began at 12:45 a.m. on Sunday when one of the men in the vans called 999, the local emergency number. The authorities have not said why he called, but they quickly stopped the vans and arrested the man and four associates. All five were British nationals from London in their early 20s, the police said.

The events rattled residents of the small villages around the air base, which is about 90 miles west of London. After the men were arrested, the police evacuated about 85 families from nearby homes while a bomb disposal robot searched the vehicles.

World.title: G7 to release 100 million barrels of oil and diesel after Trump export ban threat
World.content:
The G7 has agreed to release 100 million barrels of oil and diesel in a bid to ease supply pressures that have caused prices to skyrocket.

The group of advanced economies, including the US, said the move would include a "substantial release" of diesel in the coming days.

President Donald Trump had threatened to ban diesel exports in a move which would have eased pressure on prices for US consumers ahead of November's midterm elections, but pushed up prices elsewhere.

In a joint statement, the G7 said member countries had now agreed to "refrain from export restrictions on energy and energy products" on one another.

The G7 includes the US, UK, Canada, Japan, Germany, Italy and France, with the EU also represented at its meetings.

Trump had warned he would ban diesel exports from the US if European countries did not agree to put more of their own stocks onto the market.

On Friday, he said on social media: "Europe has just agreed to release a massive amount of their heavily stocked Diesel Oil. The process will begin immediately."

His Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent had argued US farmers, truckers, and businesses "should not be left carrying the burden" as prices soar.

Diesel is used heavily by the haulage industry and in agriculture, meaning rises in the cost of the fuel feed through into essentials such as food.

But, following a meeting of G7 leaders, French President Emmanuel Macron said the bloc had agreed to release reserves of "up to 100 million barrels" within four months under the coordination of the International Energy Agency (IEA).

The UK was represented at the meeting by Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband, who said the measures would "stabilise energy supplies, build resilience in supply chains and shield households and businesses from price shocks".

Macron said the coordinated action would "bring down the prices of petroleum products, particularly diesel". Highlighting the agreement not to pursue export bans, Macron said "President Trump, in particular, was very clear on this point".

Speaking at the White House, Trump later said an export ban on diesel was "never really on the table".

In the joint statement, G7 leaders said: "We will implement our commitments with a coordinated release through the IEA of 100 million barrels to begin immediately over four months, including a frontloaded substantial diesel release within the first 20 days by G7 members and partners."

It is not yet clear which partner countries will release stocks, nor how quickly.

The 100 million barrels will comprise a mix of diesel and crude oil. The price of global benchmark Brent crude oil briefly dropped below $100 a barrel, but rose back to around $102 by Friday evening. Before the US and Israel invaded Iran, it was trading at around $73.

Matt Smith, director of commodities research at Kpler, said oil had risen again due to renewed strikes between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis in Yemen.

"Oil prices were selling off strongly due to the announcement of strategic stock releases in Europe, but they reversed course on rumours of Saudi Arabia planning an offensive into Yemen as it looks to re-establish a safe path via Bab-Al Mandeb," he said.

European countries had pushed back against US threats to turn off American diesel, against a backdrop of the US-led war in the Middle East and reduced supplies from Russia and China.

The G7 leaders said they will also coordinate maintenance schedules to avoid multiple refineries being shut down at the same time, while encouraging countries with the capacity to do so to ramp up refining of diesel in particular.

World.title: Riot police clash with students as education protests rage in France
World.content:
Darmanin said that 735 of France's 3,700 schools were now affected "one way or another" by the violent protests.

Announcing the arrests late on Friday, NuÃ±ez told France's TF1 television network: "We are sliding into riot and urban violence, and we are using all intermediate means to put an end to it."

Meanwhile, Education Minister Ãdouard Geffray said the movement had been hijacked by non-students.

He told French broadcaster BFMTV that teachers had said "the people in front of me were not my students".

Earlier on Friday, a 17-year-old was arrested on suspicion of attempted homicide after protests in Belfort, north-eastern France, where a police officer was targeted.

BBC Verify has now authenticated two videos that show the man, who was later identified as an officer by a minister, being beaten up.

In the graphic footage, a group of young men are seen chasing him. The officer falls to the ground, and is subsequently punched and kicked multiple times in the head.

At least 65 staff members have been injured in the unrest, the education ministry said.

In the Paris suburb of Pantin police charged at protesters and made arrests after projectiles where thrown at officers.

Meanwhile, in Strasbourg tear gas was deployed as police feared conditions would become more hostile, according to the Reuters news agency.

Rubbish bins have also been set on fire in Rennes and Paris.

"As far as we're concerned, we've won - our school is closed this morning," Lola, a 16-year-old protester, told the AFP news agency on Friday.

She said police actions had made things worse.

"It makes us even angrier - the police have no right to hit us or use tear gas on us," she added.

World.title: US murderer Christa Pike unconscious and on ventilator after failed execution, lawyers say
World.content:
Pike's lawyers filed an emergency motion on Friday to preserve "any and all evidence" related to her botched execution.

Hospital staff are working to save her life and clear the drug used, pentobarbital, from her system, the filing states.

During the execution attempt, prison officials tried to start intravenous (IV) lines by using at least seven needles on Pike, according to her lawyers.

At one point, Pike herself offered guidance of where they could try.

"One needle was bent in a 90-degree angle when it was removed," the filing states.

While receiving the two doses, "she could be heard crying, whimpering, and breathing loudly throughout the procedure", her lawyers said.

Tennessee Governor Bill Lee ordered an independent review into Pike's botched execution and he halted all executions in the state for the year.

The state's department of correction has defended the method it used, saying "the protocol does not allow for additional procedures beyond what was carried out".

Authorities are yet to say whether they will try again to execute Pike. They have not not offered any explanations about what went wrong.

World.title: Woman at centre of Cornell rape inquiry was 'failed' by officials, says New York governor
World.content:
New York Governor Kathy Hochul has said the woman at the centre of the Cornell University rape case was "failed" at "every turn".

The woman, known as Jane Doe in legal documents, alleges she was drugged and raped by several men at a fraternity house in 2024.

The case was investigated at the time but no charges were laid. It recently reopened after the woman filed a civil lawsuit last month that thrust the allegations into the national spotlight.

At a news conference on Friday, Hochul said she was "deeply disturbed" by how the investigation was handled. She has now appointed New York Attorney General Letitia James to lead the case.

This appointment was made after Hochul said she "lost faith" in the local prosecutor's ability to oversee the investigation.

Expressing outrage that local prosecutors did not interview the accuser themselves, Hochul on Friday said: "This young woman had already endured something that is utterly unspeakable, and then at every turn she was failed by people and institutions with an obligation to protect her."

She has also vowed to close a "loophole" that prevents prosecutors from pursuing rape charges in cases when the victim has voluntarily consumed drugs or alcohol. Jane Doe is believed to have voluntarily taken drugs and alcohol on the night of the alleged gang rape.

"If someone is too intoxicated to consent it should not matter if they chose to use drugs or alcohol," said Hochul, adding: "Voluntary intoxication is not a licence for gang rape."

James, who is the state's chief legal officer, appeared alongside Hochul at Friday's news conference, pledging to "lead a process guided by the facts and the law".

She said her office would interview witnesses and pursue prosecutions if warranted.

District Attorney Matthew Van Houten, who previously led the investigation, has defended his office's previous decision not to file charges in the case, arguing they were not given enough evidence to meet the legal threshold.

Van Houten said much of the information released in recent weeks about the case was not passed to his office.

In a statement on Friday, he said he supported James' investigation, adding: "It has become clear that we were not provided the full picture by the university."

Cornell has said it provided evidence to the district attorney's office from its own investigation, including a Snapchat group chat in which fraternity members discussed a "free" sexual encounter with Doe on the night of the alleged assault.

World.title: Intensified Russian strikes are tearing Kyiv apart, warns mayor
World.content:
"We're talking about survival," Klitschko said at Friday's defence council meeting with Kyiv's top military, security, emergencies and police officials.

Russia's aim was to "sow panic", he said, stressing that the capital would "prevail - but only through the joint efforts of those who love it and care for it".

The mayor was speaking just hours after Kyiv's key Pivdennyi (Southern) bridge was hit in an overnight Russian drone attack. On Friday evening it was struck again - the fourth time in two days.

The bridge is one of the main transport arteries across the Dnipro River dividing western and eastern parts of Kyiv.

All metro and automobile traffic is now suspended across the bridge, causing major delays across the city. Restrictions are also in place on Kyiv's two other key bridges.

Kyiv's current population is estimated to be about three million, and many residents rely heavily on the city's metro network.

One person was killed in the capital when a multi-storey residential building was hit overnight, Ukraine's state emergencies service DSNS said.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Putin had decided in early September that "there are no rules now" when attacking Ukraine.

In a published excerpt from his interview with the Financial Times, Zelensky said: "The Russians have failed to occupy us. So now they are carrying out massive attacks and mass killings.

"They want to destroy our bridges... our data centres, the internet, mobile networks, hospitals, kindergartens, schools, universities - everything. They want people to flee their cities."

Putin insisted that Russia's attacks on Ukrainian economic targets were a direct response to Ukraine's strikes on Russia's oil refineries and its ships in the Black Sea.

"Now from every direction we're receiving calls 'let's stop'. But they started it," Putin said after a wide-ranging speech at the Valdai foreign policy forum on Thursday.

Putin admitted Kyiv had "got some results" from its refinery attacks and Russia had lost about 1% of its GDP. Ukraine maintains it began attacking Russian oil infrastructure because it helps the Kremlin finance the war.

Russia has targeted Ukrainian energy infrastructure, ramping up attacks every winter since Putin launched a full-scale invasion in 2022.

World.title: 'I was not going to let others die' - pilot of Flydubai flight describes cockpit attack by co-pilot
World.content:
The Indian pilot of the Flydubai plane who was stabbed by his co-pilot and opened the cockpit door to let others in has said he was determined not to let others die.

Capt Smit Machchhar said he was on the floor and still being attacked when he realised the plane carrying more than 170 passengers was sinking and he had to do something.

"I was lying on the floor injured but I told myself to go for one last push to open the door from inside," he said in a video call with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

"Others came in and also played a role [in controlling the situation]. I was of course fighting for my own life but at the same time I knew I was not going to let others die," he added.

Flydubai's flight FZ1073, which was bound for Tel Aviv from Dubai early on Wednesday morning, plunged more than 17,000ft (5,200m) two and a half hours into its journey.

It first sent an emergency signal to air traffic controllers before switching to code squawk 7500, which indicates hijacking.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu later told the media that one pilot had stabbed the other before "apparently trying to crash" the plane.

After fellow passengers overpowered the attacker, two reserve pilots, who were onboard, safely landed the plane at Tabuk Airport in north-western Saudi Arabia at 06:58 local time.

Machchhar, who has been hailed as a "true hero" by Netanyahu, was taken to hospital in Tabuk before being airlifted to Abu Dhabi, where he is reported to be in a stable condition.

Netanyahu told Fox News the attacker was an Omani national and said investigations suggested he had undergone "Islamist radical indoctrination".

He said that once the attacker had been subdued and tied up by passengers and crew, he was "calling out to the aircrew 'kill me, kill me', so it's clear he was suicidal - that's not a question".

The United Arab Emirates has begun investigating "whether the incident was linked to any terrorist activity or purpose", according to the country's state news agency.

World.title: Spanish PM Sánchez loses key housing crisis vote after eviction of woman, 87
World.content:
The Sindicato de Inquilinas (Tenants' Union) activist association which has been co-ordinating protests, announced during the congressional debate that it was abandoning the tent protest in central Madrid. It said it wanted to "take the struggle to all the neighbourhoods, residential blocks and homes of Madrid, wherever there are rental increases, expulsions and abuses each day, and turn the energy of the last few days into a permanent organisation".

Protesters are also calling for a general strike over the housing crisis.

The left-wing coalition government responded to the social anger by hurriedly drawing up the two decree-laws in an effort to defuse the protests.

The first decree included the suspension of evictions of vulnerable tenants until 2030, a two-year extension to rental leases due to expire before 2028, tax increases for tourist apartments, and a restriction on the purchase of residential properties by what the government calls "vulture funds".

The second decree was more controversial, because it included the automatic renewal of rental contracts, a major demand of many on the left and the Sindicato de Inquilinas.

The conservative People's Party (PP) and far-right Vox had already said they would vote against both initiatives, leaving the minority government depending on the support of smaller nationalist parties in Catalonia and the Basque Country.

However, by the eve of the parliamentary session, the centre-right, pro-independence Together for Catalonia (JxCat) had signalled its opposition to both laws, condemning them to failure.

Friday's debate was fierce and at times angry, as supporters and opponents of the decrees clashed in Congress.

"I don't ask you, I beg you to be brave and consistent," SÃ¡nchez said, moments before the two votes took place. "Because they are not just ambitious measures, they are necessary".

He appealed to lawmakers "to put order and humanity into [the housing] market, because if we don't, it will bring down our society".

Social Affairs minister Pablo Bustinduy, of the Sumar alliance, the junior partner in the governing coalition, presented the debate in dramatic terms.

"Today is about defending an international oligarchy which is extracting the rent from salaries earned with the effort of working classes of this country in order to share it out with dividends and they don't even pay taxes in Spain," he said.

"Voting against these decrees today means defending the interests of this oligarchy and turning your back on your own people."

However, Miriam Nogueras, of JxCat, said the decrees had been hastily drawn up and lacked rigour.

She said the decrees "will allow [vulture] funds to keep buying, keep speculating and evictions to keep happeningâ¦ these two decrees would provoke the opposite effect of what they aim to achieve."

The political right has argued that the government's attempts to intervene will frighten homeowners, causing them not to put their properties on the rental market and pushing prices up further.

Juan Bravo of the PP said "housing doesn't get cheaper with decrees, it gets cheaper with more homes".

World.title: Hawaii's iconic 550-year-old Hōlei Sea Arch collapses
World.content:
Hawaii's famous HÅlei Sea Arch, a 90-foot-tall (27.4m) lava rock structure that formed about 550 years ago, has collapsed into the Pacific Ocean.

The collapse's exact time is not known. The arch was still projecting into the water from the coast of Volcanoes National Park on 23 September, but was gone by 27 September, the National Park Service (NPS) said.

"The coastline flanking the sea arch has shown signs of instability for years," NPS, which warned in 2021 that the arch would eventually crumble, said in a statement.

Located at the end of Chain of Craters Road on the island of Hawaii, also called "the big island", the formation was a popular - and heavily photographed - tourist destination.

The arch is believed to have fallen when the park was temporarily closed during Tropical Storm Nolo last weekend.

The park service said earthquakes during the 2018 KÄ«lauea volcano eruption and summit collapse had damaged the cliffs near the arch.

Its ultimate collapse marks "the latest transformation of the park's remote and rugged coastline".

In January 2020, new cracks and instability in the cliffs led the park to close the original arch viewing area, and a few months later, a new viewing area opened at a safer distance, NPS said.

Waves from a tropical storm later that year broke off a chunk of rock from the bottom of the arch.

"This formation is beautiful, but temporary, and has a limited life span," the park service said in 2021. "The sea arch will eventually crumble into the sea. However, others will replace it as the cliff slowly migrates inland."

Thousands of people have liked and commented on the NPS social media post about the arch's collapse, including sharing their memories of visiting the arch and posting photos of it.

"Nothing and no one is here forever," one Facebook user commented. "Millions of years from now the sun will die. Appreciate the good, the beauty, now."

World.title: Jigawa recruits additional 2,000 secondary school teachers
World.content:
The Jigawa State Government has expanded its teaching workforce with the formal presentation of appointment letters to over 2,000 newly recruited secondary school teachers, adding to the thousands of teaching staff recruited over the past three years as part of its efforts to strengthen the education sector in the state.

The event featured the presentation of appointment letters to 2,020 newly recruited teachers, comprising 1,100 appointed on permanent and pensionable terms and 920 engaged under the J-Teach programme.

Governor Umar Namadi, who presided over the presentation at the Banquet Hall of Government House, Dutse, said the intervention was aimed at addressing shortages of qualified teachers and improving pupil–teacher and student–teacher ratios across the state, particularly in underserved rural communities.

“Barely a month ago, we provided school uniforms, bags, and writing materials to thousands of learners across the state to improve access and strengthen learning conditions. Today, we complement that investment by expanding the teaching workforce and directing qualified teachers to schools where shortages are most acute, particularly in underserved rural communities. This occasion therefore marks another purposeful step towards better teaching, improved learning outcomes, and a stronger future for every child in Jigawa State.”

The governor said the appointments represented another stage of the administration’s effort to strengthen the teaching workforce while creating employment opportunities for qualified young people.

Governor Namadi said the government’s investment in education must go beyond infrastructure and learning materials, stating that the importance of having sufficient numbers of qualified and motivated teachers in schools cannot be overemphasized.

“More than ever, in a rapidly changing world powered by information and communication technology, people need the knowledge, skills, and tools that quality education provides to thrive the knowledge, skills, and tools that quality education provides. This enduring reality explains why we continue to commit a significant proportion of our annual budget to education. It also means our investments in classrooms, furniture, instructional materials, technology, and school governance must be matched by enough qualified, motivated, and properly supported teachers.”

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He said the state government would continue to give attention to teacher development, including induction, continuous training and retraining, improved teaching methods, and professional development through the Teacher Development Agency.

“This intervention fulfils a commitment made at the inception of our administration: to improve unfavourable pupil–teacher and student–teacher ratios through the recruitment of qualified teachers, sustained training and retraining, and a more balanced deployment policy. The objective is not simply to increase staff numbers but to ensure that every school—particularly those in underserved rural communities—has the right mix of personnel to deliver effective teaching and meaningful learning.”

The governor said the latest appointments were part of a broader expansion of the teaching workforce since the beginning of his administration.

“Since 2023, the J-TEACH pathway has brought 7,500 personnel into basic education, with 3,000 subsequently converted to permanent and pensionable appointments after training and a competitive selection process. At the post-basic level, nearly 2,000 personnel entered through the same programme, and 1,000 later secured permanent status. These efforts were reinforced by deploying more than 2,100 graduate teachers and employing about 600 teaching and non-teaching staff for mega schools and other boarding senior secondary schools across the state.”

He assured the new appointees that the government would provide the necessary support while urging them to demonstrate professionalism, discipline, and commitment to the interests of learners.

“Government will support you with effective induction, mentoring, supervision, and fair performance assessment,” he said.

The governor also commended Guaranty Trust Bank for donating 450 bicycles to pupils and students who travel long distances to schools in hard-to-reach communities, saying the intervention would help ease the burden of daily travel and improve access, punctuality, attendance, and retention among affected learners.

World.title: Nigeria @ 66 : Uba Sani grants clemency to 27 prisoners
World.content:
Governor Uba Sani has granted clemency to 27 inmates in correctional facilities across Kaduna State to mark Nigeria’s 66th Independence anniversary, in an effort to give deserving inmates the opportunity to rebuild their lives.

A statement issued by the Commissioner for Information and Culture, Ahmed Maiyaki, on Friday, stated that the latest clemency brings the number of beneficiaries to more than 500 since the Governor assumed office.

Maiyaki added that the intervention included the release of eligible inmates as well as the payment of fines and compensation of over N300 million for victims since 2023.

The statement quoted the State Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice, Sir James Kanyip, as saying that the latest exercise is part of the Governor’s practice of extending mercy to deserving inmates on national occasions.

According to the Chief Law Officer of Kaduna State, previous exercises were carried out on New Year’s Day, during Democracy Day and Independence Day celebrations.

He said the prerogative of mercy was exercised through established processes, taking into consideration accountability, rehabilitation and the responsibilities that come with freedom.

Kanyip said the beneficiaries were expected to return to society with a renewed sense of responsibility and appreciation of their obligations to others.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The statement said the payment of fines and compensation is also intended to give the clemency a restorative justice dimension by addressing barriers to the release of deserving inmates while recognising the interests of victims.

It said the interventions were based on the belief that public safety, human dignity, rehabilitation and the possibility of redemption should form part of the administration of justice.

The statement added that clemency goes beyond freeing inmates from custody, as it also provides an opportunity for beneficiaries to reconnect with their families and communities.

The statement further said the administration would continue to support rehabilitation, reconciliation and the reintegration of deserving inmates into society.

According to the statement, the government remains committed to a justice system that protects society, respects victims’ interests and gives deserving individuals an opportunity to become responsible and productive members of their communities.

World.title: Zamfara @ 30: Gov Lawal commissions infrastructure projects, declares his rescue mission a success
World.content:
Governor Dauda Lawal has declared that his administration’s rescue mission is transforming Zamfara State across critical sectors. On Thursday, the governor began a series of events and project commissioning to mark Zamfara State’s 30th Anniversary.

The 30th Anniversary and commissioning were attended by the Pioneer Military Administrator of Zamfara State, Colonel Jibril Bala Yakubu (rtd), former governors Ahmed Sani Yarima and Mahmud Aliyu Shinkafi, and other dignitaries.

During his speech at the National Independence Day parade and Zamfara’s 30th Anniversary at the Trade Fair Complex in Gusau, Governor Lawal said Zamfara has moved from despair to an era of clear execution, transparency, and sustainable development.

He said, “Today, we join Nigerians in celebrating Independence Day and mark three decades since Zamfara State was created on October 1, 1996. Alhamdulillah for Allah’s grace, mercy, and protection that have guided us through trials and triumphs, uniting us in a shared destiny.

“As we watched our gallant security forces, paramilitary agencies, vibrant students and youth march in unity on this parade ground, we were reminded of the resilience that defines the Nigerian spirit and, most specifically, the strength of character of our people.

“We must reflect intentionally on the profound sacrifices of our founding fathers, who fought tirelessly to break the chains of colonial rule and give birth to a free, sovereign nation. We owe them an eternal debt of gratitude for protecting this country’s unity, peace, and territorial integrity.

“As we look forward to the next decade, we must understand that true independence demands collective responsibility. Government alone can’t do this. I call on traditional rulers, religious scholars, civil servants, traders, and our resilient youth to unite. We must set aside divisions—ethnic, political, sectarian—and protect the peace we fought for.”

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

On Friday, Governor Lawal commissioned phase III of the renovated and modernised J B Yakubu Secretariat in Gusau as part of his effort to rebuild government institutions and create a modern, efficient, technology-enabled, results-oriented Public Service for Zamfara State.

The J B Yakubu Secretariat houses critical Ministries, Departments, and Agencies whose responsibilities span virtually every aspect of governance and service delivery.

Governor Lawal said modernising the Secretariat will deepen coordination among MDAs, strengthen communication, promote institutional synergy, and support faster, more effective implementation of government decisions.

“Today’s occasion is significant as we welcome His Excellency, Colonel Jibril Bala Yakubu (rtd), Zamfara’s pioneer Military Administrator, after whom this Secretariat is named. As Zamfara marks thirty years since its creation, it’s fitting that a leader from our foundation is here to witness this milestone.”

Earlier, the pioneer Military Administrator of Zamfara State, Colonel J B Yakubu (rtd) lauded Governor Lawal’s giant strides, particularly in infrastructure, education, and health.

On the same Friday, His Eminence, the Sultan of Sokoto, Alhaji Muhammadu Sa’ad Abubakar III, commissioned the reconstructed and remodelled Jumu’at Mosque (Yardole) and its attached shopping complex.

The mosque, named after Malam Sambo Dan Ashafa, a renowned Islamic scholar and companion of the great (MUJADDADI) and leader of the 1st Sokoto Jihad, Sheikh Uthman Ibn Fodiyo, will also serve as an Islamic and research learning centre.

World.title: 2027: Makinde appoints campaign spokesperson
World.content:
Governor Seyi Makinde of Oyo State has appointed a veteran journalist, Amos Dunia, as special adviser on public affairs for his 2027 campaign.

Mr Makinde,​‌‍‍‍⁠⁠‌⁠⁠‌‍⁠‌‍​‌​ the presidential candidate of Allied People’s Movement (APM), disclosed this in a statement in Abuja by the Director, Strategic Communications for the Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation, Richard Ihediwa.

Mr Dunia is a former chairman of the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ), FCT Council.

”Dunia, a former Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ) chieftain brings decades of extensive print and broadcast media experience from prominent outlets, including the Nigerian Television Authority (NTA) and The Sun, to strengthen the Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation’s communications team.

”The appointment took immediate effect as the campaign pushed its ‘Reset Nigeria’ message ahead of the upcoming election.

”As a key spokesperson, Dunia would help drive the campaign’s central ‘Reset Nigeria’ message, working alongside other media professionals to secure victory for the party in the upcoming 2027 presidential election.”

According to him, Mr Dunia brings his experience, capacity, skills and connections as a seasoned journalist, public commentator, communication expert and publisher to the Makinde-Daura presidential campaign organisation.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

”As a spokesperson, Dunia joins other professionals in the campaign in driving the Makinde-Daura reset Nigeria message towards ensuring the victory of the APM in the 2027 presidential election,” he said.

He said following the announcement, Makinde urged all campaign members, party leaders, supporters, and citizens across the nation to remain steadfast in achieving economic prosperity, national cohesion, and political stability together.

“I charge all members of the Makinde/Daura Presidential Campaign, leaders, teeming members, supporters of the APM and indeed all Nigerians to remain steadfast in the collective quest to use the 2027 Presidential election to reset and put our nation back on the path of stability, national cohesion and economic prosperity,” the campaign organisation stated.

(NAN)

World.title: Independence: Nigerian governor pardons 13 convicts, gives reasons
World.content:
Governor Peter Mbah of Enugu State has approved the pardon, release, and commutation of sentences of 13 inmates at the Nigerian Correctional Centre in the state.

Mr Mbah’s media aide, Uche Anichukwu, disclosed this in a statement on Thursday.

Mr Anichukwu said the governor pardoned the convicts in commemoration of Nigeria’s 66th independence anniversary.

“This is in the exercise of his power of Prerogative of Mercy under Section 212 of the 1999 Constitution (as amended) and in consultation with the Advisory Council on Prerogative of Mercy, Enugu State,” he said.

The media aide said the approval was conveyed to the Comptroller, Nigerian Correctional Service, Enugu State Command, by the state’s Attorney General and Commissioner for Justice, Osinachi Nnajieze.

Mr Anichukwu listed the beneficiary inmates to include Kenneth Ozioko, Moses Saliyat, Promise Olung, Chijioke Ugwu, Samuel Ani, and Eugene Odo.

Others are Celsus Emeachi, Caleb Jatto, Calistus Eze, Gabriel Onu, Timothy Ani, Ernest Okeke, and Ejike Nwodo.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The official said some of the inmates were pardoned and released, while others had their death sentence commuted to life imprisonment.

He explained that Mr Mbah’s decision was predicated on reports of ill-health and/or proven reform in character, and following a recommendation by the Correctional Services to the Advisory Council on Prerogative of Mercy, chaired by the state’s attorney-general.

Mr Anichukwu said other members of the council include representatives of the Nigerian Correctional Service, Carmelite Prisoners Interest Organisation, and the Catholic Institute for Development, Justice and Peace, among other reputable bodies in the justice sector.

ALSO READ: PDP appoints replacement for Gov Peter Mbah as convention secretary

The media aide noted that the governor’s action was backed by Section 212 of the Nigerian Constitution.

He acknowledged that Subsection 2 of the Section provides that the powers of the governor shall be exercised after consultation with an advisory council of the state on the prerogative of mercy as may be established by law of the state.

World.title: CAN marks 50th anniversary, warns politicians against weaponising religion, ethnicity, regional sentiments
World.content:
The Christian Association of Nigeria (CAN) has warned political parties and politicians against weaponising religion, ethnicity and regional sentiments ahead of the 2027 general elections.

CAN President, Daniel Okoh, an archbishop, gave the warning on Friday in Abuja at a press conference to mark the 50th anniversary of the association with the theme: “CAN at 50: Walking Together in Faith.”

CAN was founded in 1976.

Mr Okoh said as Nigeria approached the 2027 general elections, the association was calling on all political actors to place Nigeria above political ambition.

“We expect political campaigns to be issue-based and focused on competing ideas about how to improve the lives of Nigerians.

“Political parties and candidates must resist the temptation to weaponise religion, ethnicity and regional sentiments, as Nigerians have witnessed enough bloodshed and division during election periods.

“We do not want another generation of Nigerian youths sacrificed on the altar of political ambition,” he said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The CAN president said political leaders must take responsibility for the conduct of their supporters.

“They must discourage incitement, hate speech, violence and intimidation. Every Nigerian must be free to vote according to his or her conscience, without coercion, intimidation or manipulation.

“Elections should be a contest of ideas, not a contest of violence; a competition for public service, not a licence for personal destruction,” he said.

Mr Okoh said CAN would continue to support credible democratic processes, civic education, peaceful elections and electoral integrity.

On CAN’s 50 years journey, he said the anniversary was not merely a description of an anniversary, but a statement of who the association was, where it had come from and how it intended to journey into the future.

“For 50 years, Christians from different traditions, denominations, theological backgrounds and cultural contexts have chosen to walk together under the umbrella of the Christian Association of Nigeria.

“We have not always agreed. We have had our differences. We have experienced difficult moments, disagreements and leadership challenges.

“There have been times when denominational interests appeared to compete with our collective interests. Yet, through all these seasons, we have remained together,” he said.

Mr Okoh said CAN’s unity had never meant uniformity, but recognition that there were issues bigger than denominational differences.

He said the association was established in 1976 because its forebears understood that there were moments when the Church must rise above denominational boundaries.

He explained that on 27 August, 1976, church leaders were summoned by the then Head of State, Olusegun Obasanjo, at the instance of the then Chief of General Staff Supreme Headquarters, Shehu Yar’Adua, to seek their endorsement of the National Pledge and Flag Salutation in schools, a meeting that eventually led to the formation of CAN at the Catholic Secretariat, Race Course, Lagos.

The cleric paid tribute to founding fathers and past presidents of the association, saying their labour was not in vain.

On insecurity, Mr Okoh said for more than a decade, Nigerians had suffered from terrorism, banditry, kidnapping and communal violence, with places of worship attacked and communities displaced.

“CAN therefore repeats its call to government that the primary responsibility of government is to protect life and property. Citizens should never have to negotiate with terrorists, bandits or kidnappers simply to remain alive.

“Early warning must lead to early response. We cannot continue to wait until people are killed before action is taken,” he said.

He acknowledged efforts of President Bola Tinubu to reduce insecurity, but said more needed to be done.

On alleged persecution of Christians, Mr Okoh said CAN would continue to defend the rights and welfare of Christians, but clarified that defending Christians did not mean fighting government or hating Muslims.

“CAN does not support religious hatred, and neither are we opposed to government simply for the sake of opposition.

“When a Christian is attacked because of his faith, we will speak. When a Muslim is attacked because of his faith, we should speak. When an innocent Nigerian is killed by terrorists, bandits or criminals, we must all speak,” he said.

He appealed to the media to resist reducing every Nigerian conflict to a simplistic Christian-versus-Muslim narrative, noting that some conflicts involved ethnicity, land, political power and criminality.

On CAN-Government relations, Mr Okoh said the association was neither an opposition party nor a praise-singing organisation.

“Where government policies promote the welfare of Nigerians, we will support them. Where government makes progress, we will acknowledge it. Where government fails to protect citizens, we will say so. Where injustice occurs, we will speak,” he said.

He also expressed concern over economic hardship, saying rising cost of living had placed enormous pressure on families.

“The Church sees these realities every day. People come into our churches not only with spiritual needs but with hunger, unemployment, medical bills, school fees, housing challenges and uncertainty about the future.

“Every economic policy must ultimately be judged by its impact on the people. Economic reform cannot become an abstract exercise divorced from the realities of ordinary families,” Mr Okoh said.

He listed achievements under his leadership to include strengthened national and international partnerships, advocacy for vulnerable communities, electoral observation, the Airport Chapel and Pilgrims Centre at Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja, and partnership with Oasis International on the Africa Study Bible.

Mr Okoh announced that activities for CAN at 50 would include road walk on Saturday anniversary crusade on Sunday, with Paul Enenche, the senior pastor of the Dunamis International Gospel Centre, football competition between 7 and 9 October.

Other activities include ecumenical workshop on 10 October, Bible quiz and charity visit on 13 October, women and youth assembly on 14 October, jubilee colloquium on 15 October, music cantata on 16 October, awards and presentation of CAN history book on 17 October, and thanksgiving service on 18 October.

(NAN)

World.title: Court remands man over alleged impersonation of JAMB registrar
World.content:
The Federal High Court in Abuja has remanded Arinze Nwogba in prison over alleged impersonation of the Registrar of the Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB), Segun Aina.

Mr Aina, a professor of computer engineering, was appointed JAMB registrar by President Bola Tinubu in May, succeeding Is-haq Oloyede, who served as registrar for 10 years.

Judge Salim Ibrahim ordered defendant Mr Nwogba’s remand in Kuje Correctional Centre in Abuja on Friday, pending ruling on the defendant’s bail application.

The judge fixed 7 October for the ruling and adjourned the case until 19 October for commencement of trial.

The Nigerian police charged Mr Nwogba with six counts, accusing the adefendant and others still at large of impersonating Mr Aina and used his name and photograph on WhatsApp and Truecaller.

The prosecution alleged that Mr Nwogba used telephone number 08139433155 to impersonate the JAMB registrar with the intention of gaining financial advantage.

The alleged offences contravene Section 22(3)(a), (b) and (4) of the Cybercrimes (Prohibition, Prevention, Etc.) Act, 2015, as amended in 2024.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

But the defendant denied the charges, pleading not guilty.

Bail application

After the defendant entered his plea, police lawyer Nonso Eleodimuo asked the court to fix a date for trial.

Defence lawyer Christian Ejike did not oppose the request for a trial date but informed the court that he had filed a bail application on 23 September.

Mr Ejike said the prosecution had been served and had responded to the bail application.

Mr Eleodimuo confirmed receipt of the application and told the court that the prosecution had filed and served a counter-affidavit dated 2 October.

After Mr Ejike moved the bail application, he urged the court to grant Mr Nwogba bail on liberal terms. But Mr Eleodimuo urged the court to dismiss the application.

Gregory Woje, a clerk at the Directorate of Legal Services, Force Headquarters, Abuja, who swore to the counter-affidavt filed in opposition to the bail application that the police, described the major planks of the defendant’s application as speculative and extraneous to the case.

He told the court that if granted bail, Mr Nwogba was likely to evade justice and might not appear for trial.

“Assuming the court is minded to grant bail, it is for the court to do so considering the punishment upon conviction and upon terms that will ensure the defendant/applicant attend his trial,” Mr Woje wrote.

He also stated that the conditions of bail were within the discretion of the court and not for the defendant to determine.

He said the police were ready “to prosecute the case expeditiously as all the exhibits and witnesses are ready for the trial.”

He further argued that if Mr Nwogba was granted bail and absconded, it would affect the proceedings and prejudice the prosecution.

Alleged impersonation

According to the case summary filed by the prosecution, the charges stemmed from the JAMB registrar’s petition to the Inspector-General of Police.

Mr Aina reported in the petition suspicions activities of suspected criminal gangs who allegedly registered and used telephone number 08139433155 as well as his name and photographs without his knowledge or authority.

The police alleged that the suspects used the registrar’s identity to deceive members of the public.

They said the suspects also published the telephone number on LinkedIn and directed members of the public to contact them through WhatsApp.

According to the police, investigators subsequently engaged the suspects through the WhatsApp number which had Mr Aina’s image as the profile picture. They also said the Truecaller profile of the number had Mr Aina’s image. The Whatsapp number, according to the police, was advertised on LinkedIn as the suspects offered unsuspecting members of the public phoney contracts.

The prosecution alleged that the suspect claimed to have obtained approval from the Minister of Education for the supply of 200 HP laptops as part of the ministry’s digitisation programme.

The suspect also provided the contact of a purported personal assistant, identified as Dr Stephen Igwe, who would allegedly handle arrangements for the contract, the police said.

The prosecution alleged that the suspect directed the payment of N900,000 as a “handshake” and demanded another N3 million for the Permanent Secretary and Minister of Education.

It also alleged that an Access Bank account bearing the name Edeh Chimezie Benedict was provided for the payment.

But the prosecution said Mr Nwogba, whose operational name was allegedly Dr Stephen Igwe, was subsequently arrested in Abakaliki, Ebonyi State.

According to the police, Mr Nwogba told investigators that the account details belonged to his late nephew, who died in April 2026 and was buried on 31 July.

The police also alleged that he admitted forwarding the account details to his cousin, Nnabuife Nwekpa of Onitsha, Anambra State, for use in the alleged fraudulent activity.

The police said Mr Nwekpa, whom they identified as the alleged fake JAMB registrar, was still at large and that efforts were ongoing to arrest him.

Judge Ibrahim, after hearing the arguments on the bail application, fixed 7 October for ruling and 19 October for commencement of trial.

World.title: Appeal court affirms nullification of CAMA provisions on CAC powers over religious, others
World.content:
The Court of Appeal in Abuja has upheld a Federal High Court judgement that nullified several provisions of the Companies and Allied Matters Act (CAMA), 2020, which gave the Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC) powers over incorporated trustees, including religious and other associations.

A three-member panel, in a unanimous judgement, held that sections 839, 842, 843, 844, 845, 846, 847 and 848 of CAMA infringed upon constitutionally protected rights to freedom of thought, conscience, religion, association, and peaceful assembly.

The court also affirmed that Emmanuel Ekpenyong, a constitutional lawyer with Fred Young & Evans LP, had the legal standing to challenge the provisions after he argued that they infringed on his fundamental rights.

The three-member bench delivered the judgement on 17 September. But PREMIUM TIMES obtained a copy of the judgement on Friday.

The dispute

The controversy over the amended CAMA began almost immediately after the late President Muhammadu Buhari signed it into law in August 2020.

Although the Act introduced several reforms to Nigeria’s corporate environment, its provisions on incorporated trustees, which cover churches, mosques, charities, NGOs and other associations, drew strong objections from religious organisations and civil society groups.

At the centre of the controversy was Section 839, which gave the CAC powers to suspend trustees and appoint interim managers where certain conditions existed, including alleged misconduct or mismanagement, fraud or where intervention was considered necessary in the public interest.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Religious organisations feared the provision could give the government excessive control over their internal affairs.

The Christian Association of Nigeria (CAN) called for the law to be amended, while the CAC maintained that it would not arbitrarily suspend trustees and that its actions remained subject to judicial review.

Amid the ensuing controversies, Mr Ekpenyong instituted the suit on 31 August 2020 at the Federal High Court in Abuja.

He sued the National Assembly, the CAC and the Attorney General of the Federation (AGF), over provisions of CAMA which he argued violated his constitutional rights.

In his suit, Mr Ekpenyong challenged the sections in dispute, urging the court to rule that the disputed provisions infringed upon his freedom of thought, conscience and religion, freedom of association and peaceful assembly, as well as his right of access to court.

He relied on Sections 38 and 40, among other provisions, of the Nigerian constitution.

What the Federal High Court ruled

Judge James Omotosho agreed with Mr Ekpenyong in his judgement delivered in April 2023, ruling that the powers granted to the CAC to regulate and administer incorporated trustees under sections 839 to 848 were excessive and infringed on his constitutional rights.

The judge also held that Mr Ekpenyong had the legal standing to challenge the provisions and declared the affected sections unconstitutional, null and void.

Judge Omotosho further held that Section 851, which empowered the Administrative Proceedings Committee to determine matters arising under CAMA, was inconsistent with Section 251(1)(e) of the Constitution, which confers relevant jurisdiction on the Federal High Court.

The CAC was dissatisfied with the decision and appealed to the Court of Appeal through its lawyer, Jibrin Okutepa, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN).

CAC’s appeal

On appeal, the CAC argued that the Federal High Court erred in assuming jurisdiction over Mr Ekpenyong’s fundamental rights suit. The agency argued that Mr Ekpenyong lacked the legal standing to institute the suit.

But Mr Ekpenyong opposed the appeal and maintained that the rights to freedom of thought, conscience and religion and freedom of association and peaceful assembly were fundamental to a democratic society.

He argued that the Nigerian constitution protected his right to practise his faith and associate with other members of his religious community.

He also argued that the powers given to the CAC under the disputed provisions could allow the commission to interfere with the leadership and affairs of religious associations by suspending trustees, appointing interim managers and managing their accounts.

Court of Appeal’s decision

The Court of Appeal substantially agreed with the Federal High Court.

Judge Okorowo, who read the Court of Appeal’s judgement, held that voluntary associations are generally supreme in managing their internal affairs and that courts should not interfere unless an association acts contrary to its own constitution.

The appellate court held that the trial court was right to invalidate the provisions that interfered with the constitutional freedoms protected under Sections 38 and 40 of the Constitution.

The court also rejected the argument that the restrictions imposed by the provisions could be justified under Section 45(1) of the Constitution.

Judge Okorowo held that the disputed provisions infringed the rights guaranteed by Sections 38 and 40 and were not reasonably justifiable within the meaning of Section 45(1).

The court consequently affirmed the Federal High Court’s decision striking down Sections 839, 842, 843, 844, 845, 846, 847 and 848 of CAMA.

The Court of Appeal, however, did not uphold the Federal High Court’s wholesale nullification of Section 851.

The appellate court held that the section was unconstitutional only to the extent that it purported to give the Administrative Proceedings Committee power to determine, at first instance and to the exclusion of the Federal High Court, justiciable disputes arising under CAMA and impose penalties in the manner of a court.

“The remaining administrative and regulatory functions of the committee subsist, subject to the supervisory jurisdiction of the Federal High Court,” the court held.

The court therefore modified the Federal High Court’s decision on Section 851 while affirming the nullification of Sections 839 and 842 to 848.

On Mr Ekpenyong’s standing, the Court of Appeal affirmed the finding of the lower court, holding that he had the legal standing to institute the action on the narrow basis of his personal interest and membership of a registered religious association.

“The finding that the 1st respondent possessed locus standi to institute the action is affirmed, on the narrow basis of his personal interest and membership of a registered religious association,” the court held.

The court consequently dismissed the CAC’s appeal in substantial part.

Judge Abba Mohammed and Judge Eberechi Nyesom Wike concurred with the judgment.

What the ruling means

The judgement has now placed limits on the extent to which the CAC can exercise regulatory powers over incorporated trustees where those powers conflict with constitutionally protected freedoms.

The Court of Appeal’s decision therefore preserves the regulatory role of the CAC but draws a boundary around powers that could interfere with freedom of religion and association.

However, the aggrieved party can still appeal the Court of Appeal’s decision at the Supreme Court, whose decision is final on legal disputes in the country.

World.title: Three injured as gunmen disrupt PDP meetings in Calabar
World.content:
By Ike Uchechukwu, Calabar

CALABAR — Three persons were reportedly injured on Friday after gunmen disrupted two consultative meetings organised by the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Calabar South Local Government Area of Cross River State.

The incident also resulted in damage to several vehicles belonging to members and supporters of the party, according to the PDP governorship candidate in the state, Sir Arthur Javis Archibong.

Archibong, who spoke with journalists after the incidents, said the first attack occurred at the palace of the Paramount Ruler of Calabar South, Etubom Nyong Edet Okon I, where the party was holding a consultative meeting.

He said three persons were injured and taken to hospital for treatment.

According to him, the situation later escalated at the African Club along Calabar Road, venue of a second consultation, where vehicles belonging to members of the party’s consultative team were damaged.

Archibong also alleged that gunmen opened fire on the party’s convoy and vandalised vehicles belonging to some supporters.

He said about 3,000 supporters attended the consultation, adding that the police had been notified of the meetings and that the party expected adequate security arrangements.

The candidate said the party restrained its supporters from retaliating and instead moved its convoy to the office of the Commissioner of Police for protection.

He added that the PDP would petition the Inspector-General of Police, the Department of State Services (DSS) and other relevant security agencies over the incidents.

Archibong warned that continued disruption of political activities could undermine peaceful political participation ahead of the 2027 elections.

“Let the party not be held accountable when such disruptions lead to a total breakdown of law and order,” he said.

In a separate statement, the PDP State Publicity Secretary, Mike Ojisi, described the incidents as attacks on the party’s consultative engagements.

Ojisi said the matter had been reported to the Commissioner of Police, Cross River State Command, CP Ajo Geoffrey Ordue, and urged security agencies to identify and prosecute those responsible in accordance with the law.

The PDP also appealed to its members and supporters to remain calm and shun reprisals, stressing that political consultations should not become an avenue for violence.

APC denies involvement

Reacting, the state chapter of the All Progressives Congress (APC) denied involvement in the incidents.

The APC Publicity Secretary, Emmanuel Inyang, said the party was focused on its own political activities and advised the PDP to look elsewhere for those responsible.

Police commence verification

Confirming the incident, the Cross River State Police Command said it had deployed personnel to the affected areas and that the situation was under control.

The command’s spokesman, ASP Sunday Eitokpah, said police were verifying reports of gunfire, injuries and damage to property.

“The Cross River State Police Command is aware of reported incidents during political activities in Calabar South today, 2nd October 2026.

“Police personnel have been deployed to the affected locations, and the situation is presently under control.

“The Command is verifying the circumstances surrounding the incidents, including reports of gunfire, injuries, and damage to property,” he said.

Eitokpah urged residents to remain calm, avoid affected areas where necessary and refrain from circulating unverified information.

He added that police presence and monitoring had been strengthened to maintain peace and public order.

As of the time of filing this report, the police had not attributed responsibility for the incidents to any political party or group.

World.title: Cleric critises appointing clinicians as administrators in health institutions
World.content:
By Ozioruva Aliu

BENIN CITY – A cleric, Engineer Osaze Egbenusi has criticized the increasing appointment of clinicians to head hospitals across Nigeria while professional health administrators exist.

Speaking at a public lecture organised by the Institute of Health Service Administrators of Nigeria (IHSAN), University of Benin Teaching Hospital (UBTH) Chapter, with the title “Still Diligent: The mindset of the public servant in a healthcare system in flux” Egbenusi also criticised the government for inadequate funding for government health institutions which he said is responsible Nigerian political leaders to always run abroad for every slight health challenge that they have.

In his lecture, Eng. Egbenusi spelt out the roles of Administrators which has been shifted to Clinicians.

He maintained that “Clinicians are not administrators and cannot be” lamenting that administrators in health facilities are largely relegated to file recorders to even the cleaners yet “there can be no smooth clinical activities in their absence”.

He said that if this misappropriation of duties continues, it would lead to dearth of resources and advised that doctors should be made to face their primary assignments because they presently are in short supply in the country.

The speaker who is also a lawyer defined the distinct line between working by motivation and working by diligence and postulated that understanding these conditions is key to advancing the health sector in Nigeria.

He therefore encouraged administrators to have a mindset of resilience without bitterness and do their works with dedication despite the lacuna in the system.

He appealed to the Federal government to properly fund the health sector to build trust in the country’s services and bid farewell to the constant “health pilgrimage.”

Earlier in his remarks, Chairman of the IHSAN UBTH, Joshua Uwaila Esq, said the lecture was the first organised by the association.

“It is the visionary prospect of the union that has ensured the inclusion of various unions and public servants in today’s public lecture to educate all on responsive roles and commitments towards the smooth running of health institutions on particular” he said.

World.title: Activist raises concern on judiciary under military and current democratic dispensation
World.content:
Richard Akinnola

By Ozioruva Aliu

BENIN CITY – PROMINENT journalist, activist and lawyer, Richard Akinnola, on Friday expressed concern about the current state of the judiciary in Nigeria and said that it was more independent and fearless under the military era than under the democratic dispensation.

He said that even though there are a number of judges who are hardworking and independent-minded, a few of them who have been politically compromised seem to be the face of the current judiciary.

Akinnola stated this shortly after he participated in the Health of Mother Health Foundation, HOMEF,’s Book Day which involved book reading and sharing of knowledge for the protection of the environment and protection of human rights.

He said many Nigerians have lost confidence in the current judiciary because of those of them who have been exposed politically.

According to him, “When there is a perception that a public officer seems to have control over the judiciary, and cases are assigned in a particular judicial division in Abuja to a certain number of judges, when we have about 12 judges, and when you assign such sensitive cases to just about 3 or 4 such judges, it engenders suspicion.

“For example, why should one particular judge be assigned with 4 major cases by DSS? It doesn’t make any sense. It couldn’t have been by happenstance. So even when the judge rules by fact and by law in favour of the government, people will say, what do we expect? So it’s a matter of perception, which has to change.

He said: “I tried to make some comparison between the judiciary under the military and the judiciary under the current dispensation, unfortunately, I came to the painful conclusion that the judiciary under the military seems to be much more independent and fearless than what we have currently, which is most unfortunate. And you see, perception is critical.

“Justice is rooted in public confidence. And when you have an institution in which the public has that kind of impression that certain judicial decisions are politically motivated, it brings the whole institution to ridicule. Don’t get me wrong, we have quite a number of fantastic judges on the bench. Independent-minded, brilliant. But unfortunately, the few ones who are politically compromised seem to be the face of the current judiciary.

He urged the “judiciary to reinvent itself and assert its independence, fearlessness and instill public confidence.”

On his part the Executive Director of HOMEF, Nnimmo Bassey, said the group wanted all to be involved in knowledge sharing for the protection of the environment for the protection of human rights.
