World.title: One feared dead in Aguleri, Umuoba Anam clash
World.content:
By Vincent Ujumadu

AWKA — One person was feared dead and several others injured following a fresh communal clash between Amaeze Aguleri and Umuoba Anam communities in Anambra East Local Government Area of Anambra State.

Several buildings, including a microfinance bank in Aguleri, were reportedly set ablaze during the violence.

The latest incident is believed to be linked to a longstanding land dispute between the two communities, which dates back to 1999 and had previously attracted the intervention of the administration of former President Olusegun Obasanjo.

Accounts surrounding the dispute indicate that Amaeze Aguleri had decades ago given a portion of its land to Umuoba Anam on trust. The ownership of the disputed area later became a source of disagreement between the communities.

The Anambra State Police Command confirmed the death of one person and said it had deployed personnel to the affected communities to restore peace and maintain law and order.

The Commissioner of Police, CP Nnanna Oji Ama, led the state Deputy Governor, Dr Onyekachukwu Ibezim, other government officials, security agencies and community stakeholders on an on-the-spot assessment of the affected areas.

The visit was aimed at assessing the security situation, safeguarding lives and property and preventing further escalation of the conflict.

The delegation assessed the extent of the reported destruction and the impact of the violence on residents and the affected communities.

The stakeholders also reviewed immediate measures to restore peace and strengthen security, while exploring longer-term steps to prevent a recurrence.

During the assessment, Oji Ama reiterated the commitment of the Police Command to protecting lives and property and ensuring that residents could carry out their legitimate activities without fear.

He urged residents of Aguleri and Umuoba Anam to remain calm and refrain from actions capable of escalating the situation.

The police commissioner also appealed to residents to cooperate with security agencies by providing credible and timely information that could assist ongoing investigations and peace-building efforts.

Speaking during the visit, Deputy Governor Ibezim urged traditional rulers, community leaders, youth organisations, town unions and other stakeholders to work with the government and security agencies towards finding a lasting solution to the dispute.

He said security was a shared responsibility requiring the cooperation and commitment of all stakeholders.

The Police Command assured residents of Aguleri and Umuoba Anam that security measures were being strengthened in the affected areas to prevent further breaches of peace.

It added that efforts were ongoing to address the underlying issues through dialogue and other lawful channels.

World.title: My experience with EFCC after my tenure as CBN governor – Soludo
World.content:
By Vincent Ujumadu

AWKA — Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, has recounted his experience with the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) following the end of his tenure as Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), saying the commission eventually cleared him of any wrongdoing in an investigation involving the Nigeria Security Printing and Minting Plc.

Soludo spoke on Friday during the commissioning of the EFCC Awka Zonal Directorate Complex, which will serve Anambra and Imo states.

The governor said he was invited for questioning after his name was mentioned in connection with an EFCC investigation into the activities of the Mint, where he had served as chairman of the board.

He said he appeared before the commission after receiving a month’s notice of the investigation but did not hear from the EFCC for about a year.

According to Soludo, he subsequently wrote to the commission seeking an update and was informed that the investigation had not established any corrupt conduct on his part.

“My personal testimonies about the professionalism of this Commission is that when I left office as CBN Governor, EFCC was investigating Nigeria Printing and Minting Company, the Mint, an agency within the bank.

“I was chairman of board of the Mint and was given one month notice of investigation and I showed up. After about a year, I didn’t hear from them, so I wrote them and they said that the investigation didn’t show any corrupt action about me,” he said.

Soludo further said the then EFCC chairman had clarified that he was not the subject of the investigation after his name was mentioned in connection with the matter.

He said the commission subsequently wrote to him confirming that its investigation had not established any wrongdoing on his part.

“When my name was mentioned in connection with the investigation, the former chairman of EFCC told them that I was not the subject of the investigation.

“Subsequently, the Commission wrote me a beautiful letter and said the investigation showed I didn’t have anything to do with the matter,” Soludo said.

The governor said his experience had reinforced his appreciation of the commission’s work, particularly the need for investigators to formally communicate the outcome of inquiries to persons who were invited but not found culpable.

“So I deeply appreciate the professionalism of the Commission. I want to urge that if you invite someone and later fail to find him complicit, you must write and say so, especially in this part of the world where, if you invite people, it finds its way into the pages of newspapers because they see invitation as an indictment,” he said.

On the establishment of the EFCC’s Awka Zonal Directorate, Soludo said the state was pleased to host the facility, saying its presence would facilitate faster investigation of financial crimes in the region.

“Some people might be asking why we are so excited about having the zonal office in our state. The reason for our excitement is that it will enhance quicker investigation,” he said.

The governor said the EFCC’s staffing constraints made it difficult for the commission to establish offices in all 774 local government areas, adding that the Awka directorate would, in the meantime, serve Anambra and Imo states.

“Ideally, EFCC should have offices in the 774 local government areas of the country, but with only about 6,000 staff, it is difficult to have offices in all LGAs. So this regional office will serve in the meantime and we will cooperate with you to serve the two states,” he said.

Soludo said the Anambra State Government would seek the commission’s assistance in areas relating to revenue and taxation, while also working to improve knowledge of financial crime prevention among civil servants and local government officials.

“We will not just be waiting for you to come from Abuja; we will be visiting you because it’s in our own interest that we should minimise financial crimes to the barest minimum. We assure EFCC of our fullest co-operation,” he said.

He said the fight against economic and financial crimes required collective responsibility, assuring the commission that Anambra would cooperate with it in every possible way.

According to him, the work of the EFCC was important to national development and required cooperation among government institutions and citizens.

World.title: EFCC secures 1,370 convictions, recovers N1.23trn
World.content:
EFCC

By Vincent Ujumadu

AWKA — The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) secured 1,370 convictions from 1,889 cases filed in court during the first half of 2026, the commission’s Executive Chairman, Ola Olukoyede, has said.

Olukoyede disclosed this on Thursday while speaking at the commissioning of the EFCC Awka Zonal Directorate Complex, which will serve Anambra and Imo states.

He said the commission also recovered ₦1,233,612,040,411.11, $684,478,457.32, £373,905.78 and €9,343,803.66 during the period, in addition to recoveries in other currencies.

Giving a broader account of the commission’s activities, Olukoyede said that between October 2023 and July 2026, the EFCC received 49,673 petitions, investigated 39,615 cases, filed 14,476 cases in court and secured 10,872 convictions.

He said the figures represented a conviction-to-filing ratio of 75.1 per cent.

According to him, the commission had introduced reforms aimed at improving its operations, including changes to its processes and procedures, which he said had contributed to its performance across various law-enforcement indicators.

On the new Awka directorate, Olukoyede said its establishment was part of the EFCC’s expansion programme, supported by appropriations from the National Assembly and interventions by the Federal Government.

He said Anambra and Imo required effective institutional presence because of their economic activities, describing the states as centres of enterprise, commerce and industry.

Olukoyede said the EFCC’s mandate went beyond arrests and prosecution to include prevention and coordination in the fight against economic and financial crimes.

“The EFCC exists not merely to arrest and prosecute. Our official mission encompasses prevention, enforcement and coordination in the effort to eradicate economic and financial crimes,” he said.

He said preventing financial crimes before they occurred could help reduce the economic and social costs associated with fraud and diversion of public resources.

“If we can identify vulnerabilities before billions of naira are lost, prevent fraudulent transactions before citizens lose their savings, strengthen procurement systems before public resources are diverted and interrupt criminal financial flows before they mature, then we would have saved the nation enormous economic and social costs,” he said.

The EFCC chairman said the Awka directorate would place emphasis on corruption prevention and engagement with government institutions, businesses, financial institutions, professional bodies, schools, markets, civil society organisations, traditional institutions, religious bodies and communities.

He urged members of the public to provide credible information about suspected economic and financial crimes, while cautioning against using whistleblowing to settle personal scores.

“Whistleblowing must become an act of responsible citizenship,” Olukoyede said.

“However, whistleblowing must be responsible and based on fact. It must not become an instrument for settling scores.”

He called on traditional rulers, religious leaders, town unions, market associations, professional bodies, youth and women’s groups, civil society organisations and the media to support efforts to prevent corruption.

Olukoyede also urged the new directorate to build sustained relationships with state and local governments, tertiary institutions, the organised private sector and community structures in Anambra and Imo.

Speaking on behalf of President Bola Tinubu, the Speaker of the House of Representatives, Tajudeen Abbas, said the commissioning reflected the Federal Government’s efforts to strengthen the capacity of anti-corruption agencies.

The President said his administration had, since assuming office, worked to improve the institutional capacity of anti-corruption agencies to carry out their mandates.

He said the Awka directorate would strengthen the EFCC’s presence in Anambra and Imo, particularly in major commercial and industrial centres.

“From the industrial towns of Onitsha and Nnewi, to the oil and gas town of Egbema and the rapidly growing economic city of Owerri, Imo State, the presence of EFCC will improve the ease of doing business,” Tinubu said.

He said the government would continue to provide an enabling environment for anti-corruption agencies to carry out their responsibilities.

Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, assured the commission of the state government’s cooperation in carrying out its duties.

Soludo said reducing financial crimes was in the interest of the state and expressed satisfaction that Anambra would host the regional directorate.

“Some people might be asking why we’re so excited about having the zonal office in our state. The reason for our excitement is that it will enhance quicker investigation,” he said.

The governor, however, observed that the EFCC’s staffing capacity made it difficult for the commission to establish offices in every local government area.

“Ideally, EFCC should have offices in the 774 local government areas of the country, but with only about 6,000 staff, it is difficult to have offices in all LGAs,” he said.

Imo State Governor, Hope Uzodinma, commended the EFCC for bringing its services closer to residents of the two states.

Uzodinma also appealed to the commission to establish a dedicated state office in Imo to enhance its coverage and operations in the state.

World.title: Abducted Corps Members: NANS raises alarm over ₦50m ransom
World.content:
Demands review of long-distance NYSC postings

By Adeola Badru

IBADAN — The National Association of Nigerian Students (NANS), Southwest Zone D, has raised concern over alleged ransom demands of up to ₦50 million for some prospective National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) members abducted while travelling from Ibadan to their orientation camps.

The association also called on the Federal Government to review compulsory long-distance postings and introduce safer deployment and transportation arrangements for prospective corps members.

The demand followed the attack on two buses conveying prospective corps members and other passengers along the Owerri-Onitsha Road near Umunoha in Mbaitoli Local Government Area of Imo State.

The Imo State Police Command confirmed that the buses were travelling from Ibadan to Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, and Bende, Abia State, when they were attacked by suspected armed men.

The police said 10 victims were rescued and both buses recovered, while the exact number of persons abducted was still being verified as security agencies continued search-and-rescue operations.

In a statement jointly signed on Friday by NANS Southwest Zone D Coordinator, Adeyemo Josiah; General Secretary, Ojetola Babatunde; and Public Relations Officer, Olugbemi Timothy, the association described the incident as a serious security concern requiring urgent government action.

NANS said information available to its leadership indicated that graduates from institutions in the South-West, including the Federal Polytechnic, Ede, and Osun State Polytechnic, Iree, were among those affected.

The association expressed concern that the victims were travelling to comply with the compulsory national service programme, arguing that the government should take greater responsibility for the safety of graduates required to travel long distances for the programme.

“A country cannot summon its youths and abandon their security,” the association said.

On the alleged ransom demands, NANS said it had received reports and seen fundraising appeals suggesting that as much as ₦50 million was being demanded for each victim.

It, however, urged security agencies and NYSC authorities to verify the reports and establish direct communication with the affected families before any conclusion was reached on the amounts allegedly being demanded.

“If confirmed, it would be completely unacceptable for families whose children were kidnapped while travelling for national service to be left to crowd-fund tens of millions of naira to secure their freedom,” the association said.

NANS also called for the immediate implementation of the risk-sensitive deployment framework approved by the Federal Executive Council in June 2026 as part of comprehensive reforms of the NYSC.

The reforms approved by the FEC include a technology-driven call-up process, risk-sensitive deployment to improve the safety of corps members, a redesigned six-week orientation programme, skills-based primary assignments and improved orientation camp standards.

The association argued that the latest incident underscored the need to move from policy approval to practical implementation of the safety measures.

It also called for a review of compulsory long-distance interstate deployment and proposed state-based or zonal service options, particularly where security conditions make interstate travel difficult.

“Until Nigeria’s security situation substantially improves, the Federal Government must seriously consider state-based and zonal service options, while making long-distance interstate deployment voluntary where circumstances justify it,” NANS said.

“National integration remains important, but patriotism should never require a graduate to gamble with his or her life.”

The students’ body further demanded organised and secured transportation arrangements for prospective corps members travelling to orientation camps.

It proposed the use of accredited transport operators, designated travel corridors, vehicle-tracking systems and closer coordination between NYSC and security agencies during mobilisation periods.

NANS also urged the authorities to review deployments to remote and high-risk communities and establish stronger emergency-response mechanisms for corps members serving across the country.

The association disclosed that its Southwest leadership was reviewing more than 500 complaints and reports from students and graduates concerning the NYSC process.

According to NANS, the complaints cover issues including delayed mobilisation, omissions from Senate and Academic Board lists, Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB) and institutional-record challenges, accreditation issues, registration and call-up difficulties, relocation, transportation, accommodation and reports concerning conditions in some orientation camps.

It said the latest abduction had added an urgent security dimension to the administrative and welfare concerns surrounding the NYSC scheme.

NANS called on the Federal Government, the Federal Ministry of Youth Development, NYSC management and security agencies to intensify rescue efforts until all remaining abducted persons were safely recovered.

It also demanded verification of the reported ransom claims, direct official liaison with affected families and implementation of the approved risk-sensitive deployment framework.

Other demands included a review of compulsory interstate deployment, consideration of state-based and zonal service options where necessary, secured transportation for prospective corps members and attention to outstanding mobilisation and welfare complaints.

The association urged the Ministry of Youth Development, NYSC management and student representatives to convene an engagement on the security and welfare of prospective and serving corps members.

Appealing to President Bola Tinubu, NANS called for urgent intervention in the incident, saying the government should ensure the safe recovery of the victims and take steps to prevent similar incidents.

“When young Nigerians answering a compulsory Federal Government call are abducted on their way to orientation camp, while their families reportedly begin searching for enormous sums of money for their release, government cannot afford silence or delayed intervention,” it said.

The association said the incident had generated anxiety among students, graduates and affected families, urging the government to provide clear updates on rescue efforts.

NANS clarified, however, that while its Southwest leadership was responsible for raising concerns and escalating issues through the appropriate structures, any broader national decision or course of action remained the responsibility of the national leadership of the association.

Reiterating its call for a comprehensive review of the NYSC scheme, the association said the security, economic and technological circumstances facing Nigerian graduates had changed considerably since the programme was established in 1973.

“Nigeria in 2026 is not Nigeria in 1973 when NYSC was established. The country’s security realities, economy, technology and circumstances confronting graduates have changed, and NYSC must evolve accordingly,” it said.

“We will not accept kidnapping as an unavoidable price of national service. We will not accept preventable danger as patriotism, and we will not normalise administrative hardship simply because the scheme has existed for decades.”

The association expressed solidarity with the families of the affected prospective corps members and urged security agencies to sustain search-and-rescue operations until all victims were reunited with their families.

“National service must never become national endangerment,” NANS said.

World.title: Over 250 PDP, Accord members defect to APC in Oyo
World.content:
By Adeola Badru

IBADAN — More than 250 members and chieftains of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) and Accord Party have defected to the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Oyo State ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The defectors were received by the Oyo State leadership of the APC, led by its chairman and former Deputy Governor, Moses Alake Adeyemo, during a reception held at Watershed, Old Ife Road, Ibadan, on Friday.

Addressing the new members, Adeyemo assured them of full integration into the party, saying they would not be discriminated against or denied equal participation in the affairs of the party.

He said the APC was gaining support in the state amid what he described as dissatisfaction with the administration of the state government, adding that the party was positioned to provide an alternative in the 2027 election.

According to him, “The people of Oyo State are tired of the maladministration of the APM, hence their desire for a change.”

“APC remains the only party that can produce the required change in 2027. You have made the right decision. I am assuring you that you will not regret your action.”

Also speaking, the APC governorship candidate, Sharafadeen Alli, outlined some of the policies he said his administration would pursue if elected governor in 2027.

Alli said his proposed administration would prioritise education and healthcare, as well as review the state’s security architecture to address kidnapping, banditry and other security challenges.

He said, “Our government will revamp the education, health and other sectors of the economy.

“We are going to rejig the security architecture to bring an end to the reported cases of kidnapping, banditry and other vices in the past seven and half years.

“There will also be a civil service reform with the training and retraining of workers.

“Also, our administration will revisit the issue of the Circular Road that has left thousands of people homeless.

“The local government autonomy will be the topmost priority of our administration.”

Alli also pledged to pursue civil service reforms through continuous training and retraining of workers and review issues surrounding the Circular Road project.

He identified local government autonomy as another priority of his proposed administration.

Speaking on behalf of the defectors, Hon. Olamiposi Ojo, popularly known as Bibire Forum, who led members from Accord, said their decision to join the APC was based on what he described as the party’s commitment to internal democracy.

Ojo also cited the leadership of President Bola Tinubu and what he described as the President’s impact on the country as factors behind their decision.

He said, “Our decision is based on the leadership quality of President Bola Tinubu and the way he has been able to transform the country.”

Similarly, Taoheed Ademola Lucky described the defection as a “homecoming” and expressed confidence in the APC’s prospects ahead of the 2027 elections.

He pledged that his supporters would mobilise and work for the success of the APC at both the state and federal levels in the forthcoming elections.

World.title: Cyberbullying: Sowore’s DSS Subpoena U-turn Absurd, Unprecedented, Prosecution Tells Court
World.content:
Counsel to the Department of State Services (DSS), Akinlolu Kehinde, SAN, on Friday described as “absurd and unprecedented” the alleged volte-face by the presidential candidate of the African Action Congress (AAC), Omoyele Sowore, over the appearance of a witness subpoenaed to testify in his defence.

Sowore is currently defending allegations of cyberbullying arising from posts he published on X and Facebook in August 2025, in which he described President Bola Tinubu as a “criminal” and accused him of misrepresenting the level of corruption in the country.

The controversy over the subpoena arose following the appearance of the Attorney-General of the Federation (AGF), Lateef Fagbemi, SAN, in connection with a subpoena requiring the Director-General of the DSS, Tosin Ajayi, to appear in court.

At an earlier proceeding, Sowore’s counsel, Adeyinka Olumide-Fusika, SAN, agreed with the AGF that the appearance of another senior official of the DSS would suffice.

However, at Friday’s proceedings, Olumide-Fusika reportedly reversed his position, insisting that the DSS Director-General must personally appear in court to testify as a defence witness.

Responding to the development, Kehinde argued that it was wrong for Sowore’s counsel to insist on the personal appearance of the DSS Director-General in compliance with the subpoena issued to him.

The prosecution counsel cited the Supreme Court decision in Ishaq v. Soniyi (2002) ALL FWLR (Pt. 498) 347 at 373, where the court held that where a subpoena is directed to a named public officer, it would be absurd to insist that only the named officer must appear in due compliance with the subpoena.

Kehinde also recalled that the AGF, who led the prosecution team on July 28, 2026, had made the same submission, arguing that the defence could not insist on the personal appearance of the DSS Director-General where another appropriate official could represent him.

Kehinde said it was on the basis of that understanding that the parties agreed that an official of the DSS would be nominated to represent the Director General.

He told the court that, in keeping with the understanding, a DSS official had been designated and was present in court, ready to testify.

The prosecution further argued that the DSS Director General had no personal interest in the case, having acted only in his official capacity.

Kehinde said it would be impracticable for the Director General to personally attend every proceeding involving the DSS, particularly as the Service has cases pending before different divisions of the Federal High Court.

He said: “This is a case that is over a year old. The prosecution closed its case since March 16, 2026. It is not an act of charity on the part of the defence to argue that, at a point, it agreed that an official of the DSS should come, but now it is insisting on the DG alone.”

“The decision as to who should attend court is at the discretion of the court, not that of the defence. An official of the DSS is competent to give evidence in place of the DG,” he added.

Following the arguments by both parties, Justice Mohammed Umar adjourned the matter until October 6, 2026, for ruling on whether the DSS Director General can be compelled to personally appear and testify as a defence witness in relation to actions taken by the Service.

World.title: 2027: Kogi Central Stands Still For Yahaya Bello’s Homecoming as Major Stakeholders Vow Support
World.content:
*’Your victory already sealed’, constituents assure ex-gov

Kogi Central Senatorial District on Friday erupted in a wave of excitement as former Kogi State Governor, Alhaji Yahaya Adoza Bello, returned home to a massive reception by indigenes of the region and the supporters of All Progressives Congress (APC) ahead of the 2027 Kogi Central Senatorial election.

The homecoming, which attracted a huge crowd across the district, was marked by colourful displays, chants and enthusiastic supporters who trooped out in large numbers to welcome the former governor and APC senatorial candidate.

Yahaya Bello, who governed Kogi State from 2016 to 2024, emerged as the APC candidate for the Kogi Central Senate seat after winning the party’s May 2026 senatorial primary.

They enumerated some of the legacy projects of Bello when he governed the state, declaring that the senatorial hopeful is naturally loved by the entire residents of Kogi, even years after meritoriously completing his two term of office.

Many stakeholders and residents across Kogi Central who led constituents to welcome Bello vowed to further demonstrate their gratitude for the “good works” of the former governor by voting him massively next year.

Speaking during the homecoming, former Kogi State APC Chairman and Commissioner for Local Government and Chieftaincy, Hon. Abdullahi Bello, described the reception as a demonstration of the affection and confidence the people of Kogi Central have for the former governor.

“This is the homecoming of a leader that liberated the whole Ebiraland, and we all trooped out to welcome him. It is not an easy thing. We love him and we have to demonstrate that,” Abdullahi Bello said.

He declared that the APC structure in Kogi Central was fully prepared for the forthcoming election, stressing that the district remained a stronghold of the party.

“I will not flatter you with words, but obviously, as you can see for yourself, Ebiraland, Kogi Central, is the home of the All Progressives Congress. APC is here. APC lives here. We preach APC,” he said.

According to him, the massive crowd witnessed during the homecoming was not merely a political gathering but an indication of the level of acceptance he said Bello enjoys among the people.

He expressed confidence that APC members and supporters across the five local government areas of Kogi Central would mobilise behind Bello at the polls, saying, “APC is 100 per cent prepared to vote Alhaji Yahaya Adoza Bello to the Red Chamber come next year.”

Bello’s emergence as the APC flag bearer followed a direct primary in which he was declared winner with 72,399 votes across the district.

He said: “The era of using professional influence or advantage, I think, is over. The law will put an end to that when you beat a candidate mercilessly with a very clear margin. Then I think you’ll learn some lessons, and that is going to happen in this election.”

Addressing the overwhelming crowd that welcomed the former governor, the former APC chairman said he was not surprised by the turnout, insisting that Bello’s political appeal cuts across age and gender.

“I am not surprised because Alhaji Yahaya Bello has done so much to the extent that every Ebira, both young and old, man and woman, they so much believe in him. Even if you hear his name, you just have to join the queue,” he said.

He further claimed that the message of the APC campaign was already resonating with party members and supporters across the district.

The former chairman also linked the reception to what he described as the security situation in Kogi Central during Bello’s tenure as governor, recalling that the area had previously experienced episodes of violence and insecurity.

“Before now, especially 2007 and 2008, this Central used to be a battlefield, burning of houses and killing of innocent people. But the coming of Alhaji Yahaya Bello put an end to all that,” he said.

According to him, the relative peace in the area has enabled residents to move freely and participate in political and economic activities without the level of fear associated with previous years.

Other constituents who spoke hailed the track records of Bello, promising to mobilise support for him to win with wide margin.

Responding, the former governor expressed happiness at the show of love by his people, describing the massive crowd who came to honour him as “organic” and proof that sense of appreciation of the people of the state, especially in Kogi Central is “inborn”.

Addressing journalists at the palace of the Ohinoyi of Ebira Land, Belo emphatically stated that the all the APC candidates for the 2027 general elections would emerge victorious at the polls, saying, “I have never doubted that my people are with me 100%. I have never doubted that my people are supporting APC 100%. I have never doubted that my people will support and vote for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu 100%. I have never doubted that my people are with my governor, Governor Ahmed Usman Ododo 100%.”

He further expressed assurance that he enjoys the total support of the people of Kogi Central ahead of the Senatorial polls.

“I have never doubted that my people are going to vote myself as the senator representing Kogi Central and all of our other candidates on the platform of All Progressives Congress because they know very well what this party has done to liberate our people and bringing

infrastructure to the people and ensuring that dividend of democracy is

delivered to our people and is still being delivered to our people,” Bello pointed out.

While appreciating the people for the show of love and support, he said “Kogi State is 100% APC and APC is Kogi State 100%.”

“So, I sincerely appreciate my people for displaying this love and affection. It is organic, it is inborn, it is inherent, it’s in our DNA, and I sincerely appreciate them, I appreciate. Let me appreciate God Almighty, and I appreciate our party, and I appreciate the leader of our party President Bola Ahmed Tinubu; I appreciate my governor, Governor Ahmed Usman Ododo and all the party members from top down.

“I want to assure Mr President that Kogi State election is done and Kogi Central in particular is as good as done 100% for APC,” he maintained.

The Friday’s homecoming, according to stakeholders, provided a striking display of the mobilisation surrounding the former governor, with supporters turning out in large numbers to receive him as he formally reconnects with his political base ahead of the 2027 National Assembly election.

World.title: Ekiti Moves To Cut Transport Fare By 50%, Rolls Out 15 CNG Buses
World.content:
Ekiti State government on Thursday commenced moves aimed at reducing transport fares by 50 percent across the State, with the deployment of Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) buses to cushion the effect of transportation cost on residents.

The State Governor, Mr Biodun Oyebanji, said the deployment of the CNG buses, which conicided with the Indeoendence Day and 30th anniversary celebrations, marked a major step in government’s move to reduce transport cost for the citizens in line with President Bola Ahmed Tinubu directives.

He added that the state has commenced the process of cutting transport fare by 59 percent through the rollout of 15 CNG buses donated to the state by the Federal Government as part of efforts to promote affordable and accessible public transportation, adding that the State would expand the fleet of vehicles in order to serve the residents better.

Governor Oyebanji who was accompanied by the Senate Leader, Senator Opeyemi Bamidele, at the official flag off of the vehicles at the premises of Ekiti State Transportation Agency in Ado Ekiti on Thursday, said government would continue to explore avenues to reduce the burden of the citizens.

Speaking with journalists shortly after inspecting the fleet of vehicles, Governor Oyebanji expressed appreciation to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu for the intervention, noting that the provision of the buses would contribute significantly to reducing the burden of transportation on the people. He added that the initiative demonstrates the commitment of both the state and federal government to improving the welfare of the people.

The Governor added that the CNG buses would provide a more affordable means of transpiration for residents across the state, urging the drivers union to ensure that the gains are transmitted to the commuters.

Governor Oyebanji who also inspected ongoing projects in different parts of the state after inspecting the CNG buses, hailed President Tinubu’s economic policies, which he said had allowed more recourses to carry our programme and projects that have direct impact on the people.

“No matter how visionary a leader is, if there are no resources to work with, it will just stay in the realm of a vision. But the President has been helping and supporting us not only Ekiti State but all the states in the country to translate our vision into action and impacts for the people.

“The President charged all state Governors that by October first, we should find a way of reducing transportation cost because most of the implications we are witnessing, transportation contributes a lot to it and what we have done today is just the pilot, 15 CNG buses which is going to be distributed to the unions and the agency will manage it.

“My appeal is to the Unions, they should allow the gains to translate to the commuters because this will reduce transportation cost by 50 percent.

Speaking on the deployment of the buses, the Director General of the Ekiti State Transportation Agency, Hon. Tajudeen Akingbolu, said routes had been mapped out for the CNG buses to operate from Ado Ekiti to Lagos, Ibadan, Onitsha and Abuja, adding that the initiative would provide residents with more affordable and reliable interstate transportation while reducing the burden of high transport fare.

World.title: 184.5kg Cocaine: Court Rejects KC Luxury, Two Others’ Bail
World.content:
Wale Igbintade

Justice Musa Kakaki of the Federal High Court, Lagos, has dismissed the bail applications filed by businessman Afolabi Michael Kazeem, popularly known as KC Luxury, and his alleged co-conspirators, Boniface Freeman Ochoche Sule and Ikechukwu Ekugo Patriarch.

The three defendants were arraigned by the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) on a second amended 22-count charge bordering on alleged conspiracy, cocaine trafficking and money laundering.

They pleaded not guilty to all the charges.

Following their pleas, their lawyers, including Abdulakeem Labi-Lawal, SAN, Uche Okoronkwo and Chief Benson Ndakara, urged the court to admit them to bail. The applications were opposed by the NDLEA’s counsel, Abu Ibrahim.

In a ruling dismissing the applications, Justice Kakaki said he declined to exercise his discretion in favour of the defendants because of the gravity of the alleged offences, the severity of the punishment prescribed for them upon conviction and the likelihood that the defendants might abscond if granted bail.

The judge also noted the prevalence of hard-drug trafficking in the society, stressing that the case involved a large quantity of narcotics allegedly destined for an international market.

Consequently, Justice Kakaki dismissed the bail applications and ordered an accelerated hearing of the charges.

He adjourned the case to November 2, 3, 4 and 5 for trial and ordered that KC Luxury and the two other defendants be remanded in the custody of the Nigerian Correctional Service (NCoS) pending the determination of the case.

The defendants are accused of conspiring to export 184.5 kilogrammes of cocaine concealed in five consignments through a Lagos-based courier logistics company to London, United Kingdom.

According to the charge, Kazeem, also known as Yemi Ejide and Kee Cee Luxury, allegedly conspired with Sule and Patriarch, as well as Atandare Oladipupo Oluwarotimi and Latifat Yusuf, who the NDLEA said had been arrested in London in connection with the case.

The five consignments allegedly bore Airway Bill Numbers 2079998314, 8224082370, 2079973571, 7181131742 and 2211893902, with Yemi Ejide listed as the shipper.

Count one of the charge, marked FHC/LAG/CR/755/2026, alleged that the defendants conspired between July 28 and August 1, 2026, to export the 184.5kg of cocaine, contrary to Section 14(b) of the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency Act, Cap N30, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria, 2004.

Other counts alleged that Sule procured Patriarch to facilitate the export of the cocaine, while Kazeem allegedly procured a staff member of BOT Express Logistics, Lagos Island, to process the consignments.

Kazeem was also accused of unlawfully possessing the cocaine in preparation for its export.

The NDLEA further alleged that Kazeem paid N13.2 million from a Mallamawa Ventures Zenith Bank account to BOT Express Logistics as consideration for the shipment.

The remaining counts largely concern alleged money laundering.

The agency alleged that Kazeem funnelled several billions of naira through various companies and personal accounts, including Mallamawa Ventures, Fateey Man Multi-Purpose Nigeria Limited, Patonifa Limited, Ade-Lak Resources, Holmestas Global Services Limited and La Capital Enterprises.

The prosecution alleged that some of the funds were used to acquire motor vehicles and landed properties in an attempt to conceal the alleged illicit origin of the proceeds.

He was also accused of failing to declare his assets to the NDLEA as required by law.

Kazeem, who allegedly portrayed himself online as a luxury goods dealer and lifestyle influencer, was arrested by NDLEA operatives on August 13, 2026, at the Murtala Muhammed International Airport, Lagos, while allegedly attempting to leave the country on a business-class flight to Paris.

His arrest followed the interception of the 184.5kg cocaine consignment, which the agency said was worth about N39 billion.

The NDLEA also alleged that a subsequent search of Kazeem and his Banana Island residence led to the recovery of exotic vehicles, foreign currencies and jewellery believed to be proceeds of illicit activities.

The defendants have pleaded not guilty to the allegations, and the prosecution is expected to present evidence as the trial begins in November.

World.title: Nigeria at 66: Our Problems Stem From Failure of Values, Principles, Says Dan Kanu
World.content:
*Faults 3-day warning strike by civil servants

Chuks Okocha in Abuja

Chairman of the New Deal Organization, Prince Daniel Kanu, has blamed Nigeria’s persistent challenges on the failure of good values and principles across society, saying the country’s problems cannot be solved through politics, strikes and constant finger-pointing.

Kanu said Nigerians must look beyond government for solutions and accept their own responsibility for rebuilding the country, especially by putting national interest above ethnic, religious and political considerations.

In an Independence Day message signed by him, Kanu described President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s 66th anniversary address as sincere and progressive, urging Nigerians to support legitimate institutions and leadership while playing their part in fixing the country.

“Nigeria is where it is today because Nigerians have failed themselves at virtually every level—both those in government and those outside government. We must learn to tell ourselves the truth and stop indulging in self-deception,” he said.

Kanu also questioned the three-day warning strike announced by the Joint National Public Service Negotiating Council, JNPSNC, over demands it said the government had failed to meet by September 30, 2026.

“It is rather ironic that some of the people who should be working within the system to help fix our systemic problems are going on strike to compel someone else to fix problems that are, in part, within their own areas of responsibility,” he said.

He said Nigeria’s development was being undermined by the absence of values, including integrity, honesty, competence, accountability, compassion and respect for rules.

“The solution to Nigeria’s problems therefore depends on the deliberate inculcation and practice of values and principles such as integrity, honesty, respect, competence, compassion, empathy, accountability, and customer service,” Kanu said.

While acknowledging the hardship facing Nigerians, particularly the less privileged, Kanu said the country’s problems did not begin with the present administration and would not be solved by politics or industrial action.

He urged Nigerians to take responsibility for building the country, quoting former United States President John F. Kennedy: “Ask not what your country can do for you—ask what you can do for your country.”

Kanu said Nigeria’s abundant natural and human resources would remain insufficient without responsible citizens and institutions, urging Nigerians to put the country first and rally around the Constitution in the interest of present and future generations. ‎

World.title: Maryam Abacha: Court Orders Takeover of Disputed Victoria Island Property
World.content:
Restrains firm from selling, transferring property pending suit

Wale Igbintade

The Federal High Court in Lagos has appointed a Receiver/Manager to take possession and control of a disputed property at No. 68 Molade Okoya Thomas Street, off Ajose Adeogun Street, Victoria Island, Lagos, in a suit filed by Mrs Maryam Sani Abacha against Levitikal Realties & Construction Limited.

Justice Ambrose Lewis-Allagoa, in an interim order issued on September 29, 2026, restrained Levitikal Realties, its directors, agents, representatives, servants and persons acting through it from selling, transferring, assigning, mortgaging, leasing, charging, alienating or otherwise encumbering the property pending the hearing and determination of the applicant’s Motion on Notice for interlocutory injunction.

The order was made in Suit No. FHC/LAG/CS/1245/2026, in which Abacha is the Plaintiff/Applicant and Levitikal Realties & Construction Limited is the Defendant/Respondent.

The property is covered by a Certificate of Occupancy dated July 4, 1988, and registered as No. 32 at Page 32 in Volume 1988B of the Lands Registry Office, Lagos State.

The court’s intervention followed an ex-parte application filed by Abacha on September 10, 2026, through her counsel, Adedayo Adesina, SAN.

In addition to restraining the defendant from dealing with the property, Justice Lewis-Allagoa barred it from taking any step or carrying out any act calculated to interfere with, overreach, dissipate, assign, transfer, sell, alienate, encumber or otherwise prejudice the subject matter of the originating summons.

In a significant aspect of the order, the judge appointed the Deputy Chief Registrar of the Federal High Court, or any officer of the court serving as Official Receiver, as Receiver/Manager to take possession, custody and control of the disputed property pending the hearing and final determination of the Motion on Notice.

Alternatively, the court approved the appointment of the property management company of Bola Adebule & Company, Estate Surveyors & Valuers, or any other fit and reputable property management firm registered with the Lagos State Real Estate Regulatory Agency, LASRERA, to take possession and control of the property.

Justice Lewis-Allagoa further restrained Levitikal Realties from representing or holding itself out to any third party as the owner of the property with the capacity to sell, transfer, mortgage, lease, alienate or otherwise encumber it.

The order arose against the backdrop of a Notice of Dispute and Request for Mediation and/or Arbitration dated September 7, 2026, concerning the property.

The dispute reportedly originated from a joint venture arrangement for the development of a high-rise property on the site.

According to the account contained in the court processes, the landowner subsequently terminated the joint venture agreement over alleged fundamental breaches by the developer, Levitikal Realties & Construction Limited.

The court processes further indicate that the dispute has generated parallel legal and alternative dispute-resolution proceedings, including the Federal High Court action and arbitration proceedings.

Levitikal Group identifies Samuel Mawuyon Ajose as its Chairman and Chief Executive Officer and describes the group as having interests including construction and real estate.

Ajose also publicly described himself in January 2026 as the Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Levitikal Group while declaring his interest in the 2027 Lagos governorship race.

The property has also previously attracted the attention of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission, EFCC.

Media reports in August 2026 said EFCC operatives had marked the Victoria Island development with a warning directing persons to keep off amid an alleged investigation.

Those reports, however, did not establish a final finding of wrongdoing against any party.

Against that background, the latest Federal High Court order places further restrictions on dealings involving the property while the substantive dispute remains pending.

Justice Lewis-Allagoa also authorised Abacha to publish the court’s orders in national newspapers and online media circulating in Nigeria to notify members of the public, prospective purchasers, lenders, investors and other interested parties of the pending proceedings and her interest in the property.

The judge further directed the Nigeria Police Force, including the Inspector General of Police, the Assistant Inspector General of Police, Zone 2, and the Commissioner of Police, Lagos State, as well as the EFCC and other relevant law-enforcement agencies, to provide adequate security and assistance to the applicant and the Deputy Sheriff of the Federal High Court for the implementation and enforcement of the orders.

The court reached its decision after considering the affidavit filed in support of the application, sworn to by Sadiq Mohammed Abacha, as well as the submissions of Adesina, SAN, on behalf of the applicant.

The matter has been adjourned until November 9, 2026.

World.title: Fertility Specialist, Musician Daramola Marks 40, Keeps Dreams Alive
World.content:
Founder and Medical Director of Greenleaf Fertility Clinic and Wellness Centre, Ikorodu, Dr. Adeleke Daramola Luke, has marked his 40th birthday, celebrating a career highlighted by over 300 successful live births through in-vitro fertilisation (IVF) alongside an active pursuit in the Nigerian music industry.

Widely known as ‘Dr. Global’ on social media, Daramola has built his medical career around reproductive medicine and assisted conception, helping couples achieve parenthood after years of fertility challenges.

Born into the royal family of Oba Adewumi Daramola, the Onigbemo of Igbemo-Ekiti, Dr. Daramola earned his medical degree from the University of Lagos.

He subsequently undertook specialized postgraduate training in reproductive medicine across Germany and the United Kingdom before returning to Nigeria to establish his medical practice.

Alongside his medical practice, Daramola has maintained a longstanding passion for music.

In 2015, he emerged as a runner-up in an MTN music talent competition, where he performed on stage alongside established Nigerian artists including Humblesmith and Harrysong.

He has continued to write and record music, with his latest artistic venture being a collaboration with Afro-fusion artiste, Qdot.

Those close to his work described his dual path as a reflection of his drive to build a career on his own terms.

In a tribute, scientific consultant and long-time friend, Dr. Adetokunbo Soyoye, said Adeleke’s rare blend of medicine and creative arts is a testament to what happens when vision meets relentless drive.

​”Adeleke is a goal-getter, completely unashamed about pursuing his dreams,” he said.

World.title: Ogun PDP Deputy Gov Candidate, Sowunmi-Kolapo, Installed as Muslim Council Grand Matron
World.content:
Ĥ.Urges Ogun indigenes to shun money politics, protect their heritage

The Ogun State Muslim Council has installed the Peoples Democratic Party’s deputy governorship candidate for the 2027 election, Hajia Lateefat ‘Yemi Sowunmi-Kolapo, as its Grand Matron (Egba Zone).

Sowunmi-Kolapo, who is the Iya Sunnah of Egbaland and Ameerah of Ogun State, was installed and decorated at the Ake Palace, Abeokuta, on Thursday, October 1, 2026.

The ceremony, which attracted Muslim leaders, political stakeholders, traditional figures and other members of the community, was held under the theme, “Socio-Economic Stability: A Fortress for Global Security.”

The installation has assumed political significance, coming ahead of the 2027 governorship election, with Sowunmi-Kolapo using the occasion to call for increased civic participation among Muslims and urging voters to reject electoral violence, vote-buying and political apathy.

She also urged Muslims across the state to take an active role in determining the political leadership of the country.

Speaking in an interview after her installation, the new Grand Matron described the honour as a demonstration of confidence and support from the Muslim community.

She said, “It’s a great honour for me because when people appreciate you and they show it, you can only be thankful to God and them.

“I thank the Ogun State Muslim Council for this great honour. As we were told, the Iya Sunnah of Egbaland is expected to be decorated OMC Grand Matron (Egba Zone). Our late revered mother, late Chief Khadijah Adebisi Edionseri, was the Iya Sunnah of Egbaland and OMC Grand Matron.”

“Stepping into her shoes is a big deal for me. I pray Almighty Allah guides my steps and makes the journey fruitful,” the deputy governorship candidate added.

She also expressed appreciation to members of the Muslim community for the support she had received, from the beginning of her political journey, and throughout the process leading to her installation.

“To the Muslim community, I can only say thank you to them because the shower of love and support that I got from them from the beginning of this journey is unprecedented and I don’t take it for granted,” she said.

She, however, used the occasion to broaden her message from religious leadership to civic and political participation, urging Muslims to recognise the importance of political power in protecting their interests and heritage.

The new Grand Matron said the Muslim community must not remain passive in matters concerning its future.

“An elder statesman was telling me something when I went to visit him. He said religious leaders should not sit back and think that they will hand over everything they seek to them on a platter of gold.

“If you don’t struggle for power, some oppressors will use the same power to destroy you, which is why we say our power is in our votes.”

The PDP candidate urged Muslim parents, leaders and community stakeholders to educate their children and wards on responsible democratic participation.

She said electoral participation should be peaceful and driven by citizens’ choices rather than inducements.

Earlier at the ceremony, the OMC, Egba Zone, used the occasion to draw attention to the connection between socio-economic conditions, education, security and global stability.

Earlier at the ceremony, the OMC, Egba Zone, used the occasion to draw attention to the connection between socio-economic conditions, education, security and global stability.

The guest lecturer, Sheikh Sulaimon Faruq Onikijipa, OON, who spoke on the theme, “Socio-Economic Stability: A Fortress for Global Security,” urged governments to give greater priority to security, education and the economic wellbeing of citizens.

Onikijipa said a stable society could not be achieved when citizens were denied access to quality education, security and the basic socio-economic conditions necessary for dignified living.

Also speaking at the ceremony, Senator Prof. Iyabo Obasanjo commended the Ogun State Muslim Community for honouring Sowunmi-Kolapo and giving her the blessing to serve as the PDP deputy governorship candidate.

Obasanjo described the new Grand Matron as humble, faithful and kind, while acknowledging her contributions to the Muslim community.

World.title: ‘Dad is back’: Sarah Langa and Sacha show off PDA
World.content:
Sarah Langa and Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu have continued to flaunt their romance on their social media platforms. The model and businesswoman and the Springbok have been romantically linked since late 2024.

SARAH LANGA AND SACHA FLAUNT ROMANCE

On his IG Story, Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu posted a picture of his day out with his girlfriend, Sarah Langa, who had flown to Cape Town to spend time with him.

On her account, Sarah posted her POV, walking arm in arm with the handsome young rugby player. In another post, Sarah, Sacha and their pet dog lay sprawled across a sofa.



In the video clip, Sarah revealed that the Dachshund preferred her partner to her.

She jokingly captured the clip: “I’m not allowed to touch his ball. Now that his dad is back, I’m not fun to play with anymore.

‘MY MISSUS’

Without naming him, Sarah Langa confirmed she was in a relationship during an IG Q&A in March.



A month earlier, Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu teased that he had a “missus” during a public event. The famous flyhalf was speaking at a media conference, where he was unveiled as the first-ever male ambassador for Garnier in Sub-Saharan Africa.

The post was liked by Sacha himself, as well as rugby WAGS, Layla Kolbe and Busisiwe Dayimani.

World.title: 7de Laan stars show love to Carina Nel after breast cancer reveal
World.content:
Carina Nel has received an outpouring of love after sharing her breast cancer diagnosis on her social media platforms. The actress is known for her portrayal of the medical doctor Alexa Welman on 7de Laan.

The SABC 2 soapie came to a halt in 2023.

CARINA NEL RECEIVES WELL WISHES FROM 7DE LAAN FAMILY

Earlier this week, Carina Nel shared the disturbing news that she had been diagnosed with breast cancer earlier this year.



The 38-year-old actress revealed that she had had a biopsy and had started gruelling treatment.

She thanked her support system of family and friends, as well as her Christian faith, for encouraging her.

In the comments section, the mom-of-two received an outpouring of well-wishes from the public, particularly from her 7de Laan colleagues.



TV dad David Rees, who played Chris Welman, commented: “Stay strong. We love you very much, and I will stand on my knees and pray. May our Lord bring you through this.”

TV mom, Deidre Wolhuter, who played Mariaan Welman, praised the actress for her beauty while screen sibling Andre Lotter, who played Rikus Welman, added: “All my love for you, sis”

Here’s what others had to say to Carina Nel…

Christo David (Errol Pieterse): “Darling Carina, I’ll keep you in my prayers. Lots of love”.



Jacques Blignaut (Vince Meintjies): “My Dearest Girlfriend. I am keeping you and your family in prayer.

Beata Green (Shady Vermeulen): “Sending you so much love”.

Dirk Stoltz (DeWet Basson): “My dear Carina… oh boy.. You were always in my thoughts.. My prayers now too! Few of us can try to understand what you are now forced to walk through. I do care, we do care”.



Nobuhle Mahlasela (Aggie Ngwenya): “In my thoughts and prayers”

OCTOBER IS BREAST CANCER AWARENESS MONTH

October is National Breast Cancer Awareness Month, a month dedicated to bringing awareness about breast health and the importance of early detection.



Women are encouraged to practise self-awareness, have clinical breast exams, and have regular mammograms.

World.title: Leon Schuster: ‘I’m not scared to die’
World.content:
Leon Schuster has spoken about his thoughts on dying. Images via Facebook

Despite enduring excruciating physical pain, immobility, and severe depression, TV actor and comedian Leon Schuster has shared that he has no fear of dying.

The Oh Schuks, I’m GATVOL star has revealed that he is working on the script of a new Netflix-commissioned film project.

LEON SCHUSTER: ‘I’M SURE I’LL GO TO HEAVEN’

In a clip from his interview on online radio station Play ZN, Leon Schuster was asked about his thoughts on death and the afterlife.



Leon revealed that he had grown up in a conservative religious family and was taught to have a strong Christian faith.

Despite this, the 75-year-old joked about overindulging in alcohol and other “sins” during his film career.

He shared: “I’m on my knees every day thanking the Lord that I made it to 75. I only want to make it to 80 like Dolly Parton. I’m not scared to die. I’m sure I’ll go to heaven”

HEALTH WOES IN RECENT YEARS

In recent years, Leon Schuster has shared his health struggles with the public.

The actor and comedian injured himself in 2023 while filming Mr Bones 3, which was released a year later.

Since then, he has undergone extensive surgery and rehabilitation.



Leon – who shared that his chronic back pain had affected his mobility and left him reliant on pain medication – has also spoken about suffering from depression and loneliness.

In the 2025 KykNET docuseries Schuster, he said: “I don’t want to be alone anymore. I hope to meet a young thing in her 40s. I just hope she’ll understand my health problems, and has empathy and sympathy for them.”

The comedian revealed his “biggest fear” was “growing old alone”.

He said, “On Sunday evenings when the sun goes down, I get depressed. This is why I try as much as possible to have my kids visit me on a Sunday, having a braai that continues until I go to bed.

“You look for company, you don’t want to be alone. If no one visits me, I sit on my stoep and think about life, which is not a good thing. One should be busy.”

World.title: SA attracts more international tourists despite travel ‘warning’ list
World.content:
South Africa received an increase in international tourists this year. Image via Canva

South Africa is poised to break its record for international tourist arrivals in 2026, as revealed by figures released by the Department of Tourism.

Interestingly, two of the top three countries with the highest international visitors have also issued travel alerts warning their citizens to “exercise caution” when travelling to SA.

SOUTH AFRICA RECORDS SPIKE IN INTERNATIONAL TOURISTS

According to the Department of Tourism, South Africa received over one million international tourists in August 2026.



This marked a 7.4% increase compared to August 2025.

Between January and August 2026, South Africa recorded over 7,5 million international visitors, an 11.7% increase compared with the same period last year.

Last year, statistics showed that around nine million international tourists arrived in the country.

WHICH COUTRIES ARE INTERNATIONAL VISITORS FROM?

According to data, during the month of August, the Top 3 overseas visitors to South Africa included:

US – 37 134

United Kingdom – 25 749

Germany – 14 731

The same countries accounted for the largest share of international tourists throughout 2025.

Figures were as follows for January to December 2025:



US – 358 333

UK – 356 080

Germany – 256 878

TRAVEL ALERTS

Interestingly, both the UK and the US have issued travel alerts to their citizens to “exercise extreme caution” when visiting South Africa.

In May 2025, the US warned of crime, terrorism, unrest, and kidnapping in South Africa. The alert – which is still active – also warned US officials living and working in South Africa to travel in “armoured vehicles” when conducting missions in informal settlements.

The UK government has claimed that terrorist attacks – citing the Israel and Palestine conflict, political violence, as well as Cape Town’s N2 “Hell Run” – are some of the reasons not to visit South Africa.

Other countries that have added South Africa to their travel alert lists include Australia, Canada, New Zealand and France.

Several African governments issued safety warnings to their citizens in South Africa amid a wave of anti-foreigner/xenophobic violence in 2026, with Nigeria, Ghana and Zambia taking particularly visible measures.

World.title: SASSA reminder: Fourth payment date for October 2026
World.content:
SASSA has confirmed Wednesday, 7 October as its fourth payment date for October. The date appears on the agency’s official October payment schedule. It follows the Older Persons Grant on 2 October, the Disability Grant on 5 October and the Children’s Grants on 6 October.

SASSA lists 7 October as the payment date for all other grants not covered by the first three dates. It also serves as the final check for grant recipients across all grant types. SASSA has issued a clear warning: grant recipients who do not receive their money on 7 October should urgently visit their local office. The agency says its grant may have been suspended because it failed to complete a review.

Grant recipients who bank their grants should check their accounts on the day. Those who use payment cards can check their balance at an ATM or retail pay point before travelling to an office.



Why reviews matter

SASSA reviews grants regularly to confirm that recipients still qualify – recipients who ignore a review notice or fail to bring the required documents risk having their payments suspended. A suspended grant does not reflect on the payment date, which is why SASSA links a missed payment on 7 October to an incomplete review.

Grant recipients who visit an SASSA office should take their ID document and any review letter or SMS they received. Bringing proof of income and banking details can also help to speed up the process. SASSA also urges recipients to keep their cellphone numbers updated, since the agency sends review notices by SMS.

Understanding the means test

SASSA uses a means test to decide who qualifies for a grant. The agency describes it as a financial assessment that checks an individual’s or household’s income and assets against a set threshold. The aim is to make sure that only people who qualify receive a grant. The means test applies to all social grants except the Foster Child Grant.



Changes in income or assets can affect whether a recipient still qualifies, which is one reason SASSA carries out reviews. Grant recipients who are unsure whether a review affects them can contact SASSA’s toll-free line on 0800 60 10 11. SASSA also shares updates through its official social media pages, including SASSA News on Facebook and @OfficialSASSA on X.

If you receive a SASSA grant and want to share your story, we want to hear from you.

World.title: South African chef in the UK nominated for top award
World.content:
Cape Town chef Jean Delport (left) has been shortlisted for a prestigious UK restaurant award. Image: Jean Delport/ Facebook

A Capetonian is in the running for Hotel Restaurant Chef of the Year at the UK’s prestigious Hotel Cateys awards.

Jean Delport is the executive chef at Restaurant Interlude at Leonardslee Gardens near Horsham, West Sussex, England.

He is one of just four chefs shortlisted for the award. The category recognises talent in the hotel restaurant industry.



The Cateys, organised by The Caterer magazine, is a prestigious annual awards ceremony that honors the top people, teams, and properties in the UK hotel industry.

This year’s winners will be announced at a ceremony in London on 23 November.

South African chef combines two culinary traditions

Since moving to West Sussex, Delport has become known for combining classical French techniques with his South African heritage.

At Interlude, he uses seasonal ingredients from the Leonardslee estate and surrounding area to showcase Sussex produce.

Delport’s nomination adds to an impressive list of achievements since he arrived in the county from his native Cape Town.

The restaurant earned a Michelin star within its first year. It has since received a Michelin Green Star for its sustainable approach.



The restaurant’s team won Hotel Restaurant Team of the Year at last year’s Hotel Cateys, while Interlude’s 10 bedrooms have been awarded a Michelin Key.

Delport also represented London and the South East on BBC’s Great British Menu in 2025.

The South African chef reached the banquet final after winning both the fish and main-course heats.

Cape Town chef’s latest recognition

Delport said his focus remains on making the most of the ingredients available to him, while drawing on his South African roots.

“I use ingredients from across the estate and I love it when guests enjoy what we have set out to do,” he said.

His latest nomination adds another accolade to his growing list of achievements in the UK.

World.title: Second Durban High School Old Boy elected Lord Mayor of London
World.content:
Durban High School Old Boy Bronek Masojada is the incoming Lord Mayor of London. Images via X

The second Durban High School Old Boy has been elected as Lord Mayor of London. Bronek Masojada joins the school’s alumni, Gavyn Arthur, in his role as international ambassador for Britain’s financial and professional-services sector.

The position is not to be confused with the Mayor of London, who is Sadiq Khan.

DURBAN HIGH SCHOOL CELEBRATES SECOND ALUMNUS TO BECOME LORD MAYOR OF LONDON

On its social media platforms, Durban High School celebrated the news that its alumnus, Bronek Masojada, has been elected the 698th Lord Mayor of London.



Masojada succeeds Dame Susan Langley and will assume office on 13 November.

The 1978 alumnus is the second Old Boy, behind Gavyn Arthur, who served as Lord Mayor of London between 2002 and 2003.

DHS hailed the move as a “remarkable distinction for our school and its proud Old Boys fraternity”.



Bronek Masojada is a Durban-born businessman who studied Civil Engineering at the University of KwaZulu-Natal before winning a Rhodes Scholarship to Oxford.

He has worked in the insurance and financial sector over the past three decades and is active in civic life and community development.

His path to his new title was aided by his tenure as an Alderman of the City of London in 2019 and by his election as one of the City’s two Sheriffs, which he served between 2023 and 2024.



He then went through the City’s mayoral appraisal process, during which he was identified as a suitable candidate for progression to the mayoralty.

WHAT ARE THE RESPONSIBILITIES?

The Lord Mayor of the City of London is the ceremonial and civic head of the City of London Corporation, which governs the historic financial district known as the Square Mile.

The Lord Mayor is elected for a one-year term, with their role focused on serving as an international ambassador for Britain’s financial and professional services industries, promoting trade, investment and business links around the world.



It is not to be confused with the Mayor of London, who is Sadiq Khan, who governs Greater London.
