03 Why it moved: heavy banks, steady Safaricom

Safaricom drew the most trading. The company runs a mobile network and M-Pesa, the mobile-money service widely used in Kenya to pay and send money. The stock rose 0.41%, and 3.63 million shares changed hands.

Banks were among the gainers. Equity Group rose 0.48% to KES 105.50 (US$0.82), KCB Group 0.54% to KES 92.50 (US$0.72) and Co-operative Bank 0.41% to KES 37.05 (US$0.29). Equity was the most valuable trade of the day, at roughly KES 178 million (about US$1.4 million).

Diamond Trust Bank was unchanged at KES 189.00 (US$1.47), but about 519,000 shares traded, worth roughly KES 98 million (about US$0.8 million). Standard Chartered Bank Kenya slipped 0.78% to KES 319.50 (US$2.48), giving back part of Thursday’s gain, and NCBA fell 0.85%.

There was no clear policy trigger in the session. The Central Bank Rate stands at 8.75%, according to the CBK, and the next decision comes on Wednesday. Investors in bank shares watch that decision closely, because lending rates and funding costs follow it.

04 The data behind the day

Rates (CBK). The CBK’s Monetary Policy Committee last met on 11 August 2026 and kept the Central Bank Rate at 8.75%. Its next meeting is on Wednesday 7 October 2026. KESONIA, the overnight interbank rate, was 8.7505% on 1 October.

Inflation (KNBS), released Wednesday 30 September. The Kenya National Bureau of Statistics (KNBS) said annual inflation was 6.8% in September 2026, up from 6.6% in August. Food and non-alcoholic drinks rose 9.5% on the year and transport 15.6%. Firmer inflation can reduce the room for rate cuts, which is the question hanging over Wednesday’s meeting.

US jobs (BLS). The US Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that employers added 29,000 jobs in September and that unemployment was 4.2%. The report came at 8:30 a.m. New York time, which is 3:30 p.m. in Nairobi, after the NSE had closed at 3:00 p.m. Any reaction in Kenyan stocks comes on Monday at the earliest.

Kenya’s modest gain contrasts with Nigeria’s small fall. Each market moves largely on local factors, so a split of this size is not unusual.

The NASI’s close at 247.32 leaves it 0.50 points above Thursday’s level. The more useful signal is turnover: a rise backed by heavier trading is stronger than one on a quiet tape, and Friday’s KES 622.80 million (about US$4.8 million) is above Thursday’s KES 432.96 million (about US$3.4 million).

World.title: Mexican Peso Falls 4% as Speculators Cut Long Bets
World.content:
MEXICO · MARKETS

Key Facts — The country Mexico is Latin America’s second-largest economy and sends most of its exports to the United States. Its peso floats freely and is one of the most traded emerging-market currencies.

— The background Every Friday the CFTC, the US futures regulator, reports who holds currency futures traded in Chicago. Speculators have bet on a stronger peso every week since late January 2025.

— Why now The peso fell about 4% against the dollar in the week to 29 September and on 1 October touched its weakest level since December 2025.

— What happened On Friday 2 October, the CFTC said speculators held a net long position of 52,402 contracts in peso futures on Tuesday 29 September, down 22,765 from a week earlier.

— The numbers Each contract covers 500,000 pesos (about US$27,330). The net position is worth about 26.2 billion pesos (about US$1.43 billion).

— What it means for you A weaker peso gives dollar earners and families receiving remittances more pesos. It raises costs for importers and for anyone in Mexico paying dollar debts.

— Still open Whether funds keep trimming peso bets as US yields rise. Banco de México, the central bank, next decides on interest rates on 5 November.

Speculators’ net bets on a stronger Mexican peso stood at 52,402 futures contracts on Tuesday 29 September. That was 22,765 contracts fewer than a week earlier, the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) said on Friday 2 October.

The data cover a week in which the peso fell about 4% against the US dollar. Their net position has now fallen for three weeks in a row.

What the report shows

The CFTC’s weekly Commitments of Traders report counts open positions in US futures markets. They include currency contracts on the Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME).

The figures are taken on Tuesday and published on Friday. Traders are sorted into groups, and “non-commercial” traders, mostly hedge funds and other investment funds, are the usual gauge of speculative sentiment.

On Tuesday they held 115,431 contracts that gain if the peso strengthens and 63,029 that gain if it weakens. Over the week they cut 12,164 long contracts and added 10,601 short ones.

Open interest, the total of all open peso contracts held by every type of trader, was 274,821.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Why the peso is under pressure

A US dollar cost 17.2945 pesos per dollar on 22 September and 18.0465 on 29 September, according to RT live market data. It closed at 18.2965 on Thursday 1 October.

That took the peso to its weakest level since December 2025. Analysts quoted in Mexican media point mainly to the United States: US bond yields at their highest since 2007 and bets on another US rate rise.

The carry trade loses some pull

Funds have long held pesos for the interest. Banco de México kept its benchmark rate at 6.50% on 24 September, less than half Brazil’s 13.75%.

When US yields rise, the extra return from holding pesos shrinks. The bet sours if the peso falls by more than the interest earned.

The net long peaked at 109,301 contracts in early January and fell to 54,657 by 2 June. It rebuilt to 94,732 by 8 September.

The latest figure is 52% below the January peak and the lowest since July 2025.

What it means for foreign readers

For investors, the report shows how many funds are still positioned for a firmer peso. If they sell together, the currency can fall further and faster.

For visitors, retirees and businesses paid in dollars, a weaker peso stretches budgets in Mexico. Nothing in the report says where the currency will be next week.

What comes next

The next report, due on Friday 9 October, will show positions on Tuesday 6 October. The US Federal Reserve meets on 27 and 28 October, and Banco de México on 5 November.

A smaller net long does not mean funds have turned against the peso. They still hold more bets on a stronger currency than on a weaker one.

What is the CFTC Commitments of Traders report?

It is a weekly report by the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission, the US futures regulator, showing open positions in US futures markets by type of trader. Data are taken on Tuesday and published on Friday at 3:30 p.m. US Eastern time.

What does a net long position in the peso mean?

Speculators hold more contracts that gain if the peso strengthens against the dollar than contracts that gain if it weakens. Each Chicago peso contract covers 500,000 pesos (about US$27,330).

Why does the Mexican peso matter outside Mexico?

It is one of the most traded emerging-market currencies. Its value shapes remittances to Mexico, holiday budgets and the price of goods made there for the US market.

World.title: Brazilian Real Bets Rise to 60,538 Before the Vote
World.content:
BRAZIL · MARKETS

Key Facts — The country Brazil is Latin America’s largest economy. Its currency, the real, draws foreign money because Brazilian interest rates are far above those in the United States or Europe.

— The background Every Friday the CFTC, the US futures regulator, reports who holds currency futures traded in Chicago. Speculators have bet on a stronger real every week since February 2025.

— Why now Brazil votes for president, Congress and state governors on Sunday 4 October. In the three weeks to 22 September, speculators cut their net bets from a 2026 high of 72,813 contracts to 54,201.

— What happened On Friday 2 October, the CFTC said speculators held a net long position of 60,538 contracts in real futures on Tuesday 29 September, up 6,337 from a week earlier.

— The numbers Each contract covers 100,000 reais (about US$19,170). The net position is worth about 6.1 billion reais (about US$1.16 billion).

— What it means for you The data show how heavily funds lean on the real. When large one-way bets unwind, the currency can move sharply, which affects travel budgets, transfers and investments.

— Still open How funds positioned after Tuesday. The report is three days old when published and does not cover Sunday’s vote.

Speculators’ net bets on a stronger Brazilian real stood at 60,538 futures contracts on Tuesday 29 September. That was 6,337 contracts more than a week earlier, the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) said on Friday 2 October.

The figures cover the last full week before Brazilians vote for president, Congress and state governors on Sunday 4 October. Their net position rose for the first time after three weekly declines.

What the report shows

The CFTC’s weekly Commitments of Traders report counts open positions in US futures markets. They include currency contracts on the Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME).

The figures are taken on Tuesday and published on Friday. Traders are sorted into groups, and “non-commercial” traders, mostly hedge funds and other investment funds, are the usual gauge of speculative sentiment.

On Tuesday they held 96,067 contracts that gain if the real strengthens and 35,529 that gain if it weakens. Over the week they added 11,315 long contracts and 4,978 short ones.

Open interest, the total of all open real contracts held by every type of trader, was 146,704.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Why funds bet on the real

The main draw is interest. Brazil’s central bank has cut its Selic rate from 15% to 13.75% this year, still far above US and European rates.

Investors who borrow in dollars to hold reais pocket that gap, a strategy known as the carry trade. The bet sours if the real falls by more than the interest earned.

Positioning has swung widely in 2026. The net long fell to 17,617 contracts in early January, then climbed to a 2026 high of 72,813 on 1 September.

The latest figure is 17% below that peak.

An election-week market

The real weakened in the week the report covers. A US dollar cost 5.1006 reais per dollar on 22 September and 5.2019 on 29 September, according to RT live market data.

It closed at 5.2176 per dollar on Thursday 1 October. The Ibovespa, the main São Paulo stock index, rose 1.4% on 30 September as banks led a rebound.

What it means for foreign readers

For investors, the report shows how exposed funds are to the real going into the vote. If they sell in a hurry, the currency can drop quickly; if they add, it can firm.

For visitors and anyone sending money to Brazil, a weaker real means more reais per dollar. Nothing in the report says where the currency will be after Sunday.

What comes next

The next report, due on Friday 9 October, will show positions on Tuesday 6 October, two days after the first round. A run-off, if needed, is on 25 October.

A larger net long does not mean the real will rise. Crowded positions can unwind fast when news surprises.

Chicago futures are also only a slice of the market. Much more trading in the real happens elsewhere, including dollar futures on B3, the São Paulo exchange.

What is the CFTC Commitments of Traders report?

It is a weekly report by the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission, the US futures regulator, showing open positions in US futures markets by type of trader. Data are taken on Tuesday and published on Friday at 3:30 p.m. US Eastern time.

What does a net long position in the real mean?

Speculators hold more contracts that gain if the real strengthens against the dollar than contracts that gain if it weakens. Each Chicago real contract covers 100,000 reais (about US$19,170).

Does the report predict where the real will go?

No. It shows how funds are positioned, not where the currency will move. Large one-sided positions can amplify a move when they unwind.

POLITICS · MEXICO

Key Facts — The country Mexico, where former president Andrés Manuel López Obrador handed power to Claudia Sheinbaum in October 2024.

— What happened On 1 October 2026 Latinus reported that the UIF, the Finance Ministry’s anti-money-laundering unit, has been investigating businessman Amílcar Olán for weeks.

— The numbers The file reportedly shows a UBS investment account holding €72.04 million (about US$81 million at 0.887 euros per dollar, 2 October 2026).

— What it means for you An intelligence file is not a charge. Only the federal prosecutor (FGR) can bring a case, and it recently said it had no open inquiry into Olán.

— Still open Neither the UIF nor Olán has commented publicly. Whether the file reaches prosecutors, or Swiss authorities, is unknown.

Mexico’s Financial Intelligence Unit (UIF), the anti-money-laundering office of the Finance Ministry, is investigating Amílcar Olán, according to the news site Latinus. Olán is a Tabasco businessman and a close friend of former president López Obrador’s sons.

Published late on 1 October, the report says the UIF found a Swiss investment account holding about €72 million (about US$81 million). The UIF has not confirmed the file, and Olán has not responded.

What the Reported UIF File Contains

Reporter Mario Gutiérrez Vega wrote that Latinus had access to the inquiry, opened weeks ago. Its central finding is an active equity portfolio at UBS Switzerland AG.

When the UIF obtained the data, the balance was €72,039,066.74 (about US$81.2 million). That was then worth 1.433 billion pesos (about US$78 million at 18.28 pesos per dollar). Latinus founder Carlos Loret de Mola repeated the figures in his El Universal column on 2 October.

Reported UBS account balance compared with Olán’s declared annual income, rent and school fees, in million pesos. Source: Latinus / El Universal, 1–2 Oct 2026.

According to the column, the UIF has mapped Olán’s government contracts, the agencies that paid him and which recipient firms were genuine or shell companies. It also lists alleged front men, relatives, cash, shares and property.

Life in Ticino

Latinus reports that Olán declared an annual income of 17.9 million pesos (about US$979,000) to obtain long-term residence in Ticino, Switzerland. He moved there with his family in September 2025.

He allegedly paid rent equal to 200,000 pesos a month (about US$10,900), partly through his sister. His two children attend an international school costing 1.5 million pesos (about US$82,000).

TV Azteca reported that transfers to the Swiss bank were made by two of his siblings. Its reporter had earlier found Olán in Lugano, as covered in Mexico: Sheinbaum Opens Door to Probe of AMLO-Linked Businessman Amílcar Olán.

Head of a Network, the Column Says

Some headlines described Olán as the “head” of a criminal group. In the column, the word refers to the UIF’s link chart, which reportedly places Olán at the centre of the network.

Latinus calls that circle “El Clan”. Andrés Manuel López Beltrán, the former president’s son, is not named in the file, Loret de Mola wrote.

Expansión, citing Latinus, says his brother Luis Alberto was flagged as a link to an alleged Jalisco cartel member. That person is suspected of fuel smuggling, and the claim remains unproven.

Earlier reporting tied Olán’s firms to state oil firm Pemex, the Dos Bocas refinery and the army, Expansión noted. It also cites medicine sales and ballast for the Maya and Interoceanic trains. The family faced other scrutiny in US Revokes Visa of López Obrador’s Son, Who Fires Back at Trump.

What Is Not Yet Known

The UIF has issued no statement, and TV Azteca noted that the file’s existence and scope remain publicly unconfirmed. All figures come from one outlet’s access to documents, repeated by others.

Days earlier, Attorney General Ernestina Godoy said there was no arrest warrant for Olán, TV Azteca reported. On 28 September President Sheinbaum said the federal prosecutor should act if there is evidence.

Whether the UIF freezes accounts, files a complaint or seeks Swiss cooperation is still open.

Sources: Latinus (Mario Gutiérrez Vega, 1 Oct 2026); El Universal (Carlos Loret de Mola column, 2 Oct 2026); Expansión Política (1 Oct 2026); TV Azteca (2 Oct 2026); El Informador (2 Oct 2026). Exchange rates: open.er-api.com, 2 Oct 2026.

POLITICS · BOLIVIA

Key Facts — The country Bolivia is an Andean nation of about 11 million people. Its national congress, the Plurinational Legislative Assembly, elects the attorney general, who heads the Public Prosecutor’s Office.

— What happened On 2 October 2026 presidential spokesman José Luis Gálvez said “narco-terrorism” had financed decisions such as appointments with bribes, and that Attorney General Roger Mariaca’s election involved bribes to lawmakers (El Deber, Opinión).

— Who is involved Mariaca, in police custody since 30 September; his lawyer Jerjes Justiniano, who called the claim irresponsible; and the Assembly, which met on the case the same morning.

— What it means for you The government is pressing lawmakers to suspend Mariaca. While leadership of the prosecution service is disputed, criminal complaints in Bolivia may move slowly.

— Still open Gálvez named no lawmaker and showed no evidence in public. No court has charged Mariaca, and the Assembly session went into recess before any decision.

Bolivia’s government alleged on Friday that the Mariaca election to attorney general was arranged through bribes to some lawmakers. Presidential spokesman José Luis Gálvez cited it at a morning press conference as an example of narco-terrorism.

He spoke hours before the Assembly met to discuss Mariaca, who has been in police custody since 30 September. Gálvez offered no evidence in public, and Mariaca’s lawyer called the remarks irresponsible.

What the spokesman said

Gálvez speaks for President Rodrigo Paz, in office since November 2025. El Deber, a Santa Cruz daily, published his remarks at 8:39 a.m. Bolivia time on Friday.

“This narco-terrorism has got so far into some institutions,” he said, that it has “even financed, with bribes, important political decisions, such as the selection of authorities.” In Spanish he spoke of decisions financed “con sobornos”, meaning with bribes.

He then turned to the Mariaca election itself. Rumours and available information, he said, show the vote “se gestó con sobornos a algunos asambleístas”. That means it was arranged through bribes to some lawmakers.

El Deber, Red Uno and Opinión all carried that sentence. El Deber headlined the remarks as a claim that narco-terrorism financed the Mariaca election.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

A warning about vote-buying

Gálvez said rumours had resurfaced since Thursday of plans “to buy votes with drug-trafficking money”. The aim, he said, was to keep intact a scheme that “was a friend of Marset”, the Uruguayan drug trafficker Sebastián Marset.

He urged lawmakers to suspend Mariaca and other questioned officials temporarily while legal proceedings run. “Today’s session is historic,” he said, asking for a decision rather than a debate on procedures.

The government accuses Mariaca of leading a criminal network inside the prosecution service that protected drug traffickers. Police detained him at Viru Viru airport, as reported in Bolivia Attorney General Mariaca Detained at Airport.

Mariaca’s defence responds

Jerjes Justiniano, Mariaca’s lawyer, called the statements “somewhat irresponsible”, the broadcaster Unitel reported. He asked why the government did not take its complaint to the formal authorities.

Justiniano said procedures exist to protect the rule of law. He described the spokesman’s words as a “veiled threat” against lawmakers who disagree with the government.

Mariaca rejects a US accusation of 28 September that he took bribes to protect drug traffickers. He and two senior prosecutors have filed a freedom suit against President Paz, covered in Bolivia’s Detained Attorney General Seeks Release.

The Assembly meets, then pauses

The Assembly opened its session at 10:25 a.m., chaired by Senate president Diego Ávila, El Deber reported. Vice-President Edmand Lara, who normally presides, was travelling in Spain.

Three ministers attended: Fernando Aramayo of the Presidency, Ernesto Justiniano of Defence and Marco Antonio Oviedo of Government, the interior ministry. Shortly before 11 a.m., lawmakers demanded written reports and the session went into recess, Unitel reported.

Deputy Sandra Rivero said verbal reports alone would make it “a coffee chat”. The agenda covers official reports on the arrest and possible legislative action, the news site eju.tv reported.

What Is Not Yet Known

Gálvez did not name any lawmaker said to have taken bribes, or give amounts. He cited “rumours” and unspecified information, and no prosecutor has announced a bribery inquiry.

A La Paz constitutional chamber on Friday morning denied the freedom suit of detained senior prosecutor Martín Irusta, El Deber reported. No ruling on Mariaca’s own petition had been reported by midday.

No court has charged Mariaca, and the Assembly session remained in recess at midday. It is unclear whether lawmakers will suspend him or name an interim chief.

ECONOMY · ARGENTINA

Key Facts — The country Argentina, whose government is seeking hard currency to strengthen its fiscal and financial position, according to the Economy Ministry.

— What happened On 2 October 2026 Economy Minister Luis Caputo announced in Paris a citizenship by investment programme, opening to applications in the fourth quarter of 2026.

— The numbers US$350,000 as a non-refundable gift to the Treasury, or a US$800,000 purpose-made government bond. A couple with two minor children pays US$500,000 in total (Economy Ministry, 2 October).

— What it means for you Foreign investors gain a passport route with no residence requirement. Applicants face checks by intelligence, financial and security agencies before any approval.

— Still open Whether a 30 June 2026 Electoral Chamber ruling, which barred the government from handing citizenship decisions to the migration office by decree, will block the final approval step.

Argentina citizenship by investment now has a price list. Economy Minister Luis Caputo said on Friday that foreigners can buy a passport for US$350,000 paid straight to the Treasury.

He made the announcement in Paris on 2 October, alongside Cabinet Chief Diego Santilli, on the last day of the government’s Argentina Week investor event. Applications are due to open during the fourth quarter of 2026.

Two ways to pay, and a family rate

Contributions required under Argentina's citizenship by investment programme, by applicant type (spouse etc. = spouse or unmarried child aged 18 to 25). Source: Argentine Economy Ministry, 2 October 2026.

The ministry’s statement sets two routes for the main applicant. One is a direct, non-refundable payment of US$350,000 to the Treasury; the other is buying a US$800,000 government bond created for the scheme.

Spouses and unmarried children aged 18 to 25 without children of their own pay US$100,000 each. Children under 18 cost US$25,000, so a couple with two minors pays US$500,000.

All money must move through the formal banking system and meet anti-money-laundering rules. The ministry says the proceeds will go towards strengthening Argentina’s fiscal and financial position.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Argentina markets Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Who checks the applicants

A dedicated body, the Agency for Citizenship by Investment Programmes, will lead the review. The State Intelligence Secretariat (SIDE), the financial intelligence unit (UIF) and the security and interior ministries take part.

Checks cover identity, the origin of the funds, criminal and reputational records and migration history. The agency then sends a recommendation to the National Migration Directorate, which approves or rejects each case.

The ministry says the screening follows standards of the OECD, the rich-country policy club, and the Financial Action Task Force. It did not name the international advisory firms it says are helping it.

The legal question over who decides

The route itself is not new. Decree 524/2025, published in the Official Gazette on 31 July 2025, let foreigners naturalise after a “relevant investment” regardless of residence time.

That built on Decree 366/2025, an emergency decree that rewrote the citizenship law and moved naturalisation from federal judges to the migration office. On 30 June 2026 the National Electoral Chamber annulled that decree.

Infobae and Perfil reported that the court found the change breached Article 99 of the Constitution, which bars presidents from legislating on electoral matters by decree. Citizenship, the judges said, opens the door to political rights such as voting.

Friday’s plan still names the migration office as the body that grants approval. The ministry statement did not address the ruling, and no new decree for the programme had been published by Friday afternoon.

Why the government wants it

Caputo presented the scheme as part of a drive to draw foreign capital, during a Paris trip that also produced energy pledges. Milei’s visit included TotalEnergies plans for nearly US$10 billion in Argentine oil and gas.

Supporters see a fresh source of dollars that adds no debt in the cash route. Critics, in coverage such as Sitio Andino’s, note that the payments carry no duty to invest locally or create jobs.

Foreigners seeking to live in the country rather than buy a passport have other options. A separate guide on how to get residency in Argentina in 2026 sets out the routes and fees.

What Is Not Yet Known

For Argentina citizenship by investment, the ministry set no opening date beyond the fourth quarter and no revenue target. It gave no terms for the US$800,000 bond, nor how many passports it expects to issue.

The government is contesting the June ruling. La Nación reported on 1 July that it would appeal to the Supreme Court.

The weekly Semanario Nuestra Gente reported on 22 July that the appeal had been filed. No Supreme Court ruling had been reported by Friday afternoon.

SECURITY · BOLIVIA

Key Facts — The country Bolivia is a landlocked Andean nation of about 11 million people. President Rodrigo Paz has governed since November 2025 and has rebuilt security ties with Washington.

— What happened On 1 October 2026 the US State Department released a joint statement in which the United States and 13 other governments, with Bolivia itself, backed Bolivia’s antidrug effort.

— Who is involved Members of the Shield of the Americas, a US-led security alliance formed in March 2026. The official text lists 15 signatory governments, Bolivia included.

— What it means for you The statement is political support, not new money or troops. Disruption at the prosecution service, where the attorney general is detained, may still delay criminal cases.

— Still open No court has charged or convicted Attorney General Roger Mariaca, who denies wrongdoing. Who will lead the prosecution service in the meantime is disputed.

Bolivia’s antidrug effort has won public backing from the United States and 13 other governments in the Americas. The joint statement, released by the US State Department on 1 October and co-signed by Bolivia, follows the detention of the country’s attorney general.

The signatories praised what they called decisive action against drug trafficking and corruption. They urged Bolivia to keep investigating and prosecuting the networks involved, according to the text published by the State Department.

What the statement says

The governments “commend the Government of Bolivia” for confronting drug trafficking and corruption, the State Department text says. They encourage its “continued investigation and prosecution of these networks”.

The statement adds that illicit influence will no longer be tolerated in the hemisphere, “no matter how high it reaches”. It closes with the line: “Today, we stand firmly with Bolivia.”

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Which forum and which countries

The statement came from the Shield of the Americas, a security alliance created at a presidential summit in Florida in March 2026. Costa Rica’s La Nación reported that it is led by the United States.

The State Department text lists 15 signatories: the United States, Argentina, Bolivia, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica and the Dominican Republic. The rest are Ecuador, El Salvador, Guyana, Honduras, Panama, Paraguay, Peru and Trinidad and Tobago.

Bolivia co-signed, so 13 governments besides Washington and La Paz back its effort. Brazil, Mexico and Venezuela are not signatories.

Why it comes now

On 28 September the State Department accused Attorney General Roger Mariaca of taking bribes to protect drug traffickers. Police detained him at Viru Viru airport near Santa Cruz on 30 September. Details are in Bolivia Attorney General Mariaca Detained at Airport.

Santa Cruz chief prosecutor Alberto Zeballos and senior prosecutor Martín Irusta were also detained, Unitel reported. The three have filed a constitutional action for their release, covered in Bolivia’s Detained Attorney General Seeks Release.

The Public Prosecutor’s Office, which decides who is charged with crimes, has contested the detention. It says no formal arrest warrant existed and called the detention a kidnapping, Pura Noticia reported.

A closer partnership, with friction

The statement fits a wider shift under Paz. On 15 June Bolivia and the United States signed a cooperation deal worth up to US$20 million, Los Tiempos reported. It funds training, equipment and technical support.

On 5 June the alliance backed Paz against protests it said drug money financed, La Nación reported. Both statements back a government that restored security ties with Washington.

The risk is that foreign governments are endorsing an arrest before any court has ruled. Mariaca denies the accusations, and the prosecution service disputes the legality of his detention.

What Is Not Yet Known

It is unclear who will lead the prosecution service. Senior prosecutor Luis Montaño declared himself interim attorney general, but the government rejects this and says Congress must choose, Infobae and ABI reported.

It is also unclear whether the statement brings new cooperation or funding. The outcome of the court hearing on Mariaca’s release had not been reported by Friday afternoon.
