World.title: Crown seeks life sentence for Krismar Espinosa in execution-style murder of Wilbert Banks Jr.
World.content:
Crown seeks life sentence for Krismar Espinosa in execution-style murder of Wilbert Banks Jr.

By Breaking Belize News Staff: The Crown is asking the High Court to impose a life sentence on convicted murderer Krismar Espinosa for the execution-style killing of cyclist and bicycle technician Wilbert “Yellow” Banks Jr., arguing that several aggravating factors make a fixed-term sentence inappropriate.

During mitigation before Justice Nigel Pilgrim, Crown Counsel Maria Nembhard-Santana stressed that Espinosa had previously been convicted of manslaughter in another killing and had only been out of prison for approximately nine months when he was charged with Banks’ murder. The Crown also pointed to the use of a firearm, the seven gunshot wounds suffered by Banks and evidence that the killing had been planned in advance.

Espinosa, meanwhile, declined to personally address the court and called no character witnesses. Through his attorney, he continued to maintain his innocence and relied on a Social Inquiry Report prepared for sentencing.

Justice Pilgrim has reserved sentencing until October 13, 2026. Espinosa remains on remand at the Belize Central Prison.

Banks, 38, was shot seven times on April 5, 2024, in the Lake Garden area near Ladyville. He attempted to drive away after being shot but crashed his vehicle. Police recovered nine 9mm expended shells and a cellphone from the scene.

The prosecution’s key witness was Banks’ former girlfriend, who was Espinosa’s girlfriend at the time. She testified by video link that Espinosa threatened to kill her and her young son unless she lured Banks to the Lake Garden area. She said Banks later drove her there, where Espinosa emerged and opened fire.

Justice Pilgrim found Espinosa guilty of murder on July 31 following a trial without a jury. The court accepted the woman as a credible and reliable witness and rejected Espinosa’s account that he was at home when Banks was killed.

The court also heard emotional victim-impact statements from Banks’ employer Andrew Ordonez, his father Wilbert Banks Sr. and his 14-year-old daughter. His daughter recalled Sunday barbecues, Valentine’s Day gifts and the sense of safety she felt around her father, telling the court that “Father’s Day is no longer the same.”

Banks was well known in Belize’s cycling community and worked at Ordonez Bike Shop. His death was widely mourned after the 2024 killing.

World.title: UNICEF Belize and Special Envoy join forces to promote inclusion of children with disabilities
World.content:
UNICEF Belize and Special Envoy join forces to promote inclusion of children with disabilities

By Zoila Palma: UNICEF Belize and the Special Envoy for the Development of Families and Children have joined forces to promote the rights, inclusion, and well-being of children with disabilities across Belize, under the message: “Every Child Seen. Every Child Heard. Every Child Included.”

The partnership aims to challenge stereotypes, raise awareness, and promote a more inclusive Belize where every child is valued, supported, and empowered to reach their full potential.

The initiative will also amplify the voices of children with disabilities and highlight their strengths, achievements, and contributions.

The partners emphasized that children with disabilities should not be defined by their challenges, noting that they are dreamers, leaders, learners, creators, and changemakers whose stories, voices, and rights matter. The initiative encourages families, schools, communities, and organizations to help create environments where every child can thrive.

Through the partnership, UNICEF Belize and the Special Envoy are calling for greater inclusion and support for children with disabilities, with the goal of making inclusion the norm rather than the exception.

World.title: Government and Global Fund strengthen partnership to support vulnerable Belizeans
World.content:
Government and Global Fund strengthen partnership to support vulnerable Belizeans

By Zoila Palma: The Government of Belize and the Global Fund have reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening collaboration and supporting vulnerable populations across the country. The discussions were held between Minister of Economic Transformation Dr. Osmond Martinez and Global Fund Portfolio Manager Marcos Patino Mayer.

Minister Martinez was accompanied by Director Leroy Martinez and Project Manager Ferdy Cabb during the meeting.

Discussions focused on the performance and achievements of Global Fund Cycle 7 being implemented under the Ministry of Economic Transformation, as well as potential funding opportunities and priority areas for Cycle 8.

Minister Martinez expressed appreciation to Patino Mayer and the Global Fund for their continued support to Belize. He highlighted the importance of the organization’s commitment to reaching and supporting some of the country’s most vulnerable populations.

The meeting reaffirmed the commitment of the Government of Belize and the Global Fund to continued partnership and collaboration.

World.title: Julius Espat: “The police officers need to know who their leader is”
World.content:
Julius Espat: “The police officers need to know who their leader is”

By Zoila Palma: Today, Minister Julius Espat reiterated the need for a Home Affairs Minister to be named.

“That is sad for Belize not for me. The police department needs a substantial minister, whoever that is.

It is not a regular ministry. It is, the police officers need to know who their leader is and that’s all I’m asking for, for the prime minister to make a decision on one of the most important ministries in this country,” Espat said.

Espat says that he understands the needs within the Belize Police Department and it needs a Minister willing to put in the time to help address crime.

“I understand the needs and I understand that he needs somebody there that is willing to put in the time to help us address the crime problems in this country and the police officers are capable. They just need guidance and we need as a government to provide that to them,” Espat explained.

World.title: Julius Espat: “Some people don’t like my style but I MAKE IT HAPPEN”
World.content:
Julius Espat: “Some people don’t like my style but I MAKE IT HAPPEN”

By Zoila Palma: During an interview following today’s Sitting of the House of Representatives, Minister Julius Espat said that, at times, some ministries operate as though they are their own “turf.”

“It’s been a great experience. That’s what’s lacking in Belize a bit, each Ministry starts acting like it’s a turf and if we learn to work a little bit better together but it always ends up to who is the leader because if the leader doesn’t lobby for it, it won’t happen,” Espat said.

Espat emphasized the importance of working together.

“You can be in any ministry and if you sit back and blame everybody that it wont happen, it wont happen

Some people don’t like my style but I make it happen,” Espat added.

World.title: Ministry of Agriculture hosts training for coconut farmers on pest and disease management
World.content:
Ministry of Agriculture hosts training for coconut farmers on pest and disease management

By Zoila Palma: The Ministry of Agriculture, Food Security and New Growth Industries (MAFSNGI) has completed a series of specialized training workshops aimed at strengthening coconut pest and disease management among farmers in the Belize and Orange Walk Districts. The initiative forms part of the Food and Agriculture Organization’s (FAO) global “One Country One Priority Product” (OCOP) initiative, which promotes sustainable value chains for priority agricultural products.

The two-day workshops were led by the FAO’s national coconut pest and disease specialist, with technical and field support from personnel attached to MAFSNGI’s Fruit Tree Program, Research Unit and Extension Unit. Training sessions were held on September 17 and 24 in the Belize District and September 18 and 25 in Orange Walk.

More than 30 coconut farmers from each district participated in the sessions, which included female and youth farmers. The training was designed to strengthen farmers’ ability to protect coconut crops and support the continued development and sustainability of Belize’s growing coconut sector.

The workshops combined classroom-based presentations with practical field exercises, allowing participants to gain hands-on experience in detecting, identifying and managing pests and diseases affecting coconut production.

Following the completion of the Belize and Orange Walk sessions, additional training workshops are being scheduled for other districts across the country.

Coconut farmers and other interested stakeholders are encouraged to participate and can contact their respective district agriculture offices for information on upcoming sessions and registration.

World.title: Food, music and tradition: Benque Viejo’s Día de los Muertos Street Fest returns
World.content:
Food, music and tradition: Benque Viejo’s Día de los Muertos Street Fest returns

By Zoila Palma: The Benque Viejo Town Council, in collaboration with Blazeful Vibes, will host the 3rd Annual Día de los Muertos “Street Fest”on Sunday, November 1, 2026, bringing together residents and visitors for an evening celebrating culture, tradition, remembrance and community.

The event will take place from 4 p.m. to 11 p.m. in front of Cancha Marshalleck in Benque Viejo Town.

The Benque Viejo Town Council noted that more than 35 vendors are expected to participate, offering food, drinks and locally made products.

The event will also feature music, performances and activities for the community.

The celebration will highlight the cultural significance of Día de los Muertos, with candles, offerings and decorations serving as tributes to the lives and memories of loved ones who have passed.

World.title: Historic Baron Bliss Lighthouse set for major reconstruction
World.content:
Historic Baron Bliss Lighthouse set for major reconstruction

By Zoila Palma: The Baron Bliss Lighthouse in Belize City is set to be rebuilt, with reconstruction works which was scheduled to begin in September 2026, following engineering and structural assessments that found the lighthouse’s foundation had been compromised.

The Belize Tourism Board (BTB), in collaboration with the Baron Bliss Trust, Belize City Council, National Institute of Culture and History (NICH), and the Ministry of Infrastructure Development and Housing (MIDH), said the project is necessary to ensure public safety while preserving the historic landmark.

The BTB noted that the lighthouse will be dismantled and reconstructed to replicate its original design and appearance while maintaining its historic character.

Before the works begin, the lighthouse, Baron Bliss Tomb and surrounding area will be comprehensively documented, while original architectural elements will be assessed and incorporated into the reconstructed structure where practicable.

Protecting the Baron Bliss Tomb will remain a priority throughout the project. A purpose-designed protective enclosure, approved by the project engineers, will be installed before demolition begins. Reconstruction is expected to be completed by January 2027, with the project partners saying the works are intended to preserve the landmark for future generations.

During construction, members of the public will be prohibited from entering the designated construction zone around the lighthouse.

Vehicles will also be prohibited from parking or stopping along the roadway immediately adjacent to the park frontage.

Marine vessels must observe a No Wake Zone, while anchoring, mooring or lingering within the designated marine safety zone will be prohibited unless authorized.

World.title: Triggerman gets life sentence for murder of Paulwell’s daughter and her mother
World.content:
Toshyna Patterson and her daughter Serayah Paulwell were kidnapped and murdered in September 2023.

David Smith, the triggerman in the murder of Member of Parliament Phillip Paulwell’s 10-month-old daughter, Sarayah, and her mother, Toshyna Patterson, has been sentenced to life in prison for the crime.

The Kingston-based painter is to serve a minimum of 45 years behind bars before becoming eligible for parole.

The sentencing was handed down by Chief Justice Bryan Sykes on Friday under a reported plea deal.

Smith was among a number of persons charged in the double murder which rocked the nation.

Patterson and her daughter were reported missing on September 9, 2023. Prosecutors say the mother and daughter were taken to Warieka Hills in St Andrew where they were shot and killed and their bodies burnt.

The alleged mastermind behind the killing, former United States Navy culinary specialist Leoda Bradshaw is charged with two counts of conspiracy to murder, two counts of conspiracy to kidnapping, two counts of kidnapping, and two counts of capital murder.

World.title: Gov’t says its committed to fair resolution in doctors pay dispute
World.content:
In this file photo Minister of Labour and Social Security, Pearnel Charles Jr, speaking during a post-Cabinet press briefing.

Government says its “committed to a fair, lawful and peaceful resolution” to the standoff over overtime pay that has led to junior doctors taking industrial action on Friday.

READ: Brace for delays in health services, JMDA warns amid pay dispute

In a release on Friday, the Minister of Labour and Social Security said it acknowledges the concerns of members of the Jamaica Medical Doctors’ Association (JMDA) as they await the Industrial Disputes Tribunal’s award in the dispute between the association and the Government of Jamaica.

The matter is before the IDT for compulsory arbitration under the Labour Relations and Industrial Disputes Act.

The ministry said the tribunal must be allowed to carry out its functions independently.

Accordingly, the release stated, the minister and the ministry will refrain from commenting on the merits of the dispute or taking any action that could be construed as seeking to influence the tribunal’s decision.

“Our medical doctors provide an invaluable service to Jamaica. Their dedication and sacrifice deserve recognition, and the ministry understands the importance of a timely resolution to these longstanding matters,” it said. “The Government remains committed to a fair, lawful and peaceful resolution and has confidence in the Tribunal’s consideration of the evidence and the issues before it.”

The ministry said it encourages all parties to maintain constructive engagement and industrial harmony while the proceedings are concluded.

“A timely resolution, consistent with due process, remains important to our doctors, the healthcare system and the public we all serve,” the ministry said.

World.title: WATCH: Mandeville Regional in emergency mode amid junior doctors strike
World.content:
MANCHESTER, Jamaica — Senior Medical Officer at the Mandeville Regional Hospital Dr Everton McIntosh is appealing to medical doctors to assist in manning the facility where junior doctors are currently on strike.

“I just want to make an appeal, so if there are any doctors out there who are willing to do some sessions at the hospital, we are inviting persons to come forward… especially for the emergency departments. We would appreciate the assistance,” he told journalists Friday morning.

READ: Brace for delays in health services, JMDA warns amid pay dispute

The doctors on strike are protesting what they say is the slow pace of the review process by the Industrial Disputes Tribunal (IDT) to hand down a ruling as it relates to overtime payments.

Dr McIntosh said over 100 junior doctors have stayed off the job with about 24 consultants manning all the wards and departments at the regional facility.

“We should have a total of 133 doctors on duty, but just the consultants are here which is around 24 who are working, so you can see the discrepancy there, out of a total of 133. That has grave implications for the ability for us to cover all of the areas adequately in terms of the wards, the emergency department, the outpatient clinics,” he said while pointing out that there are 315 patients admitted at the hospital as of Friday morning.

— Kasey Williams

World.title: Dad vs son in clash of Butlers
World.content:
Craig Butler (left) and Kyle Butler

KINGSTON, Jamaica — For 90 minutes on Saturday, football will pit father against son when Mona High technical director Craig Butler comes face-to-face with Vauxhall High coach, his son Kyle Butler in an intriguing ISSA Walker Cup quarterfinal.

But while Craig will be desperate to see Mona advance, the veteran football developer admits there would be something special about watching his son lift the Walker Cup with Vauxhall.

Craig, who has spent years nurturing young Jamaican footballers through his Phoenix Academy, said his ultimate wish is for Kyle and his daughter Kaycie to surpass his own achievements.

“I have raised Kyle and Kaycie to surpass my achievements. Only a father who doesn’t love his children would want them not to succeed,” Craig said.

The father-son showdown — set for 2pm at Waterhouse stadium — is an unusual twist to what is already one of the more intriguing Walker Cup quarterfinals, but Craig believes football has provided the family with a unique opportunity to work together, travel and share memorable moments.

“In football, we have an opportunity as a family to work and to spend valuable time and banter,” he said.

Craig has travelled extensively during his football career, taking Jamaican football talent to various parts of the world.

He recently pointed to the progress of Phoenix graduate Daniel Scarlett, who has signed with Australian club Central Coast Mariners, as another example of the opportunities available to young local players.

But on Saturday, the focus will be squarely on Mona and Vauxhall.

Craig has been impressed with the transformation of Vauxhall under Kyle and believes his son has earned the respect of the school community.

“It would be wonderful for Kyle to win the Walker Cup and Manning Cup with Vauxhall. He is well loved there and has done wonders with the school and the players,” he said.

However, Craig knows Kyle faces a major obstacle in Mona, who have developed a football identity over several years.

“Mona is in another mode now. They have ascended with a team built over the last six years,” he said.

“It is a brand of football that is embedded in the school and its players, and it will be hard,” Craig added.

There is also a strong Phoenix connection between the two teams, making Saturday’s contest even more significant for the Butler family.

Craig, however, is not allowing the rivalry to overshadow the bigger picture.

“Both teams are Phoenix and, either way it goes, it will be love again after the game,” he said.

And that sentiment is likely to define the Butler family story long after the final whistle — regardless of whether father Craig or son Kyle is celebrating a place in the Walker Cup semi-finals.

– Howard Walker

World.title: Senior doctors pick up the slack in western region
World.content:
Cornwall Regional Hospital

ST JAMES, Jamaica — Clinical Coordinator for the Western Regional Health Authority (WRHA), Dr Delroy Fray, is seeking to reassure the public that contingency measures are in place to minimise any disruption caused by industrial action taken by doctors.

The doctors are protesting what they say is the slow pace of the review process by the Industrial Disputes Tribunal (IDT) to hand down a ruling as it relates to overtime payments.

“We’ve made contingency plans so that our urgent and emergency cases will not be compromised in any way,” Fray told Observer Online on Friday morning.

“We knew what would happen today so yesterday was a planning day for us and the plan was to have our senior doctors cover the gaps,” he said.

The Western Region has four major health care facilities which includes the Cornwall Regional Hospital and Fray said that since 8:00am on Friday, the senior doctors have taken action.

However, he said that they are managing based on the plans put in place.

“I have checked in the morning and we are moving along that line very well. I am going to be monitoring that every four hours to see what the flow is like and how we are coping,” he said.

“Based on the plans I have in place for all the four hospitals, I’m not worried, I think we should be alright and the fact that it is just 24 hours, I think we can manage,” he added.

It was reported that the Noel Holmes hospital in Lucea currently has five doctors on staff which would have normally been nine.

World.title: Brace for delays in health services, JMDA warns amid pay dispute
World.content:
Doctors say if there is no ruling in their wage dispute with the Government by Friday, October 2, 2026, they cannot guarantee normalcy within the health sector across the island (Photo: Adobe Stock)

Jamaicans have been warned to brace for longer wait times and delays in the completion of procedures in the healthcare sector as junior doctors remain restive over the matter of overtime rates which has been before the Industrial Disputes Tribunal (IDT) for the past year.

In a press release on Friday, Jamaica Medical Doctors Association (JMDA) President Dr Jubilee Brown said the body “cannot guarantee normalcy from 8 am on Friday, October 2, 2026 to 8 am on Saturday, October 3, 2026.

“Only emergency services will be provided during this period,” the JMDA president said.

She added that the association has activated relevant protocols to minimise adverse outcomes during the period.

According to the JMDA, the Government owes the doctors $31 billion in retroactive overtime, but the Government’s calculation sits at $23 billion.

“We have been working at the same overtime rates since 2021. This is unacceptable. The JMDA calls upon the Industrial Disputes Tribunal to hand down its award without further delay,” Brown said.

World.title: No fallout
World.content:
The scene in Black River in the immediate aftermath of Hurricane Melissa last October. (Photo: Garfield Robinson)

DESPITE concerns from some quarters over the slow spending of Hurricane Melissa donations, permanent secretary in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Foreign Trade Sheila Sealy Monteith says the Jamaican Diaspora has not raised any complaints about how its contributions are being used.

Sealy Monteith told Parliament’s Internal and External Affairs Committee on Thursday that the ministry had “many opportunities” to receive feedback from the Diaspora but had not received any indication of concern. The assurance came against the backdrop of concerns about the pace at which millions of dollars donated following Hurricane

Melissa have been utilised. Category 5 Melissa left immense damage after slamming into Jamaica’ south-western coast on October 28, 2025 and swept across western and north-western parishes.

During the committee’s deliberations with the ministry, Opposition Member of Parliament Dr Kenneth Russell raised the Auditor General’s finding that only about 1.7 per cent of the donated funds had been used months after the contributions were made.

“Has the ministry, one, received any feedback from the members of the Diaspora and the donors about the slow use of their contributions? And secondly, is the ministry concerned about the reputational risks done to the country and the effect it will have on your ability to raise funds should a similar situation recur?”

Russell queried.

Sealy Monteith responded that the ministry had not seen evidence of a decline in confidence in Jamaica’s ability to handle international support.

“We have used the strength of our diplomacy to ensure that countries who wish to contribute are enabled to contribute, that we are able to record it. We are providing direction for them, and we pass them on to the relevant authorities.

We have not received any indication to date that there has been a loss of confidence in our abilities to use it,” she revealed.

The permanent secretary stressed that the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Foreign Trade’s role is primarily to facilitate international assistance, rather than to determine how the funds are ultimately spent.

She said the ministry works with other government entities to ensure that countries and other contributors wishing to assist Jamaica are able to do so and are directed to the relevant authorities.

Sealy Monteith also suggested that the pace at which contributions are absorbed and deployed must be considered in the context of the capacity of the receiving authorities to use the support.

“I think people understand also that when support comes in, it requires the ability to be able to assimilate and to use, and that comes over time as well,” she said. “So, if you’re asking me whether there’s been a fallout of interest and solidarity, I have not seen that. We continue to be a preferred guest on many agendas, and Minister [Kamina Johnson Smith] had a schedule in New York last week that was head-turning because everybody wants Jamaica to be at the table, to sit on our committees, to be there,” she added

World.title: Kevin Smith spoke in  tongues, detective testifies
World.content:
SMITH… late pastor of Pathways International Restoration Kingdom Ministries

A detective constable testified on Thursday that Kevin Smith, the now deceased pastor of Pathways International Restoration Kingdom Ministries in Albion, St James, refused to speak to him on the night of October 17, 2021 when the clergyman was alleged to have killed a male member of his church and ordered another to cut the throat of 39-year-old Taneka Gardner, who was also a member of his flock.

The detective constable is the seventh witness to take the stand in the murder trial of Andre Ruddock,

who is accused of killing Gardner, allegedly on Pastor Smith’s command.

While Smith refused to engage the detective constable in conversation, it was a different story with

Ruddock, who was allegedly eager to speak about the shocking events that unfolded at the church on the night.

According to the investigator, both Smith and Ruddock were wearing nothing but briefs while they were handcuffed and seated on the ground, in the driveway, close to the entrance gate of the premises.

“I spoke to Kevin Smith but he didn’t speak to me. Instead, gate of the premises. “I spoke to Kevin Smith but he didn’t speak to me. Instead, he started talking in a loud voice, in a way I couldn’t understand. It was like when someone was talking in tongues in a church. I informed both Andre Ruddock and Kevin Smith that they would be taken into custody under reasonable suspicion of double murder and wounding with intent. I caused them to be taken to the Montego Bay Police Station lockup,” the detective said.

In relation to Ruddock, the detective explained that he was more cooperative than Smith. The cop testified that he spoke to Ruddock before his futile attempt to talk with Smith. He said that after completing a walkthrough of the church property where the bizarre events unfolded he went to Ruddock, lifted him from off the ground, and took him to an area of the premises where Smith could not hear their conversation.

“After completing the walkthrough and speaking to the detective inspector I came back to where Andre Ruddock was by the big gate. I introduced myself to him and took him up from where he was by the big gate and took him to the area I described as a bathroom right next to the fencing,” the detective constable testified.

“I wanted to speak to him outside of the presence of Kevin Smith. I allowed him to put on some clothes because he was in his underpants. He stated that he had clothes nearby,” he said.

He told the court that Ruddock confessed to killing Gardner by cutting her throat after receiving instructions to do so. When asked who gave the instructions, Ruddock did not say who, but looked in the direction where Pastor Smith was seated on the ground in the driveway of the church.

Prosecutor Latoya Bernard showed the detective numerous photographs of the bizarre scene. He will continue to identify more photographs today when the trial resumes.

World.title: ‘Maxi merde’: French presidential campaign rattled by a week of chaos
World.content:
Though that individual, who was granted anonymity to candidly discuss the current situation, was only referring to the increasingly violent demonstrations outside secondary schools and the government’s slow-footed response to them, it’s a sentiment likely shared by French voters after a week of particularly bleak headlines.

If there are political winners, it’s not immediately clear who they are. Establishment candidates and moderate voices are still struggling to seize the narrative from far-right presidential front-runner Marine Le Pen and her surging far-left challenger Jean-Luc Mélenchon — both of whom want to fundamentally reshape France and its relationship with Europe.

A survey by pollster Odoxa this week found that the French disapprove of the government’s handling of the student school protests, but they also disapprove of Mélenchon and his far-left party France Unbowed’s involvement.

Mélenchon’s allies have joined demonstrators outside schools, saying they were there to show support and protect minors from confrontations with police. But the government and France Unbowed’s political opponents accuse them of fanning the flames of violence — allegations they deny.

“There’s a battle over the narrative” between the political extremes, a Socialist Party adviser said.

Whatever the case, the week’s crises are showing just how nasty the campaign can get with two populist candidates unafraid to stoke partisan divisions leading the polls.

World.title: Polanski’s Greens look for their next opening
World.content:
Polanski added: “Through our sustained pressure — and our historic wins — we have held the worst instincts of the Labour government in check. And started to move them in the right direction.”

The Labour washout in May’s local elections, courtesy of voter defections to right-wing populist Reform UK as well as to the Greens, accelerated Starmer’s exit as prime minister over the summer. Burnham has since promised many of the things that under Starmer were within the Greens’ sole purview — public ownership, care, and housing.

The task for the Green leader now is to decide where to push Labour next.

“It won’t surprise you to hear that I’m not hopeful about Labour’s backbone,” he told the crowd.

Hackney Mayor Zoë Garbett, who won her job in May’s local elections, said there were still “key differences” with the governing party, particularly on Gaza, climate and rent control — but conceded that Burnham had made it more difficult for the Green message.

She said: “People were so fed up in May, they were done with people making promises and not delivering, but we need to put forward what our vision is as well, that’s what this conference and Zack’s speech is about.”

World.title: 17 countries join forces to oppose EU budget cuts
World.content:
"We therefore believe that the overall funding for Cohesion Policy and the CAP must be preserved in the next MFF," the seventeen countries wrote in the letter to Irish Taoiseach Micheal Martin seen by POLITICO.

The signatories include Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czechia, Estonia, Greece, Hungary, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Malta, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain.

Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni and Romanian President Nicușor Dan coordinated the initiative and will host an informal meeting of those countries in the margins of the next European Council on Oct. 15 and 16.

The Multiannual Financial Framework, or MFF, finances everything from farmers’ subsidies to development aid, and is among the toughest negotiations in Brussels. In 2025, the European Commission proposed a budget of nearly €2 trillion for the 2028-2034 period and shifted hundreds of billions from agriculture and regional payouts, known as cohesion policy, to new priorities such as defense and competitiveness.

The so-called Friends of Cohesion group warned that further reductions to agricultural and cohesion "would only weaken it [budget] and risk undermining public support for the European project."

Ireland’s negotiating document, or negobox, will set the scene for discussions among the EU’s 27 leaders during the summit in Brussels in October.

World.title: G7 agrees to release oil reserves after U.S. push
World.content:
Trump had also threatened to ban exports of diesel altogether — a major worry for European countries because U.S. diesel accounts for more than half of the continent's imports of the fuel.

But that threat is now off the table, G7 leaders said Friday. Under the agreement there would be "no restrictions or bans on exports among G7 countries," the statement read.

French President Emmanuel Macron denied European leaders had been strong-armed into making the concession with the threat of a diesel export, telling press on Friday: "The tone of our discussion was not one of threats; it was constructive."

He added that Trump had been "very clear" that there would be no export ban.

The leaders' statement did not specify that the releases would come from European reserves, but U.S. President Donald Trump said in a social media post that European countries had agreed to make a major contribution.

"Europe has just agreed to release a massive amount of their heavily stocked Diesel Oil," Trump wrote on Truth Social. "The process will begin immediately."

World.title: Šefčovič: Verhandlung mit China noch ohne  Ergebnisse
World.content:
Über die Ergebnisse der Reise sprechen die EU-Staats- und Regierungschefs am 15. und 16. Oktober bei ihrem EU-Gipfel in Brüssel. Die EU droht damit, den Zugang chinesischer Unternehmen zum Binnenmarkt einzuschränken, sollten die Gespräche scheitern.

Die EU und China verhandeln seit Juni. Die Staats- und Regierungschefs der EU haben erklärt, sie wollten die große Menge chinesischer Importe und das hohe Handelsdefizit mit China, nicht länger hinnehmen.

„Ich glaube, unsere chinesischen Partner haben verstanden, dass dies direkte Auswirkungen auf die Zukunft bedeutender europäischer Unternehmen hat – buchstäblich Tausende von Arbeitsplätzen“, berichtete Šefčovič. „Und auch auf das soziale Gefüge und das Sozialmodell, das in Europa über viele, viele Jahrzehnte hinweg entwickelt wurde.“

Im Mittelpunkt der Gespräche steht das wachsende Handelsdefizit der Union mit China von einer Milliarde Euro pro Tag. Um dieses Defizit zu verringern, müssen die Importe aus China reduziert und/oder die EU-Exporte nach China gesteigert werden.

Šefčovič erklärte, er hoffe, aus Peking Ergebnisse zu drei Hauptthemen mitbringen zu können: plötzliche Exportanstiege Chinas in wichtigen Industriezweigen, Maßnahmen zur Steigerung europäischer Warenexporte nach China, Klarheit hinsichtlich chinesischer Exportbeschränkungen für Rohstoffe, insbesondere für Seltene Erden.

In Milwaukee traf sich Šefčovič mit dem chinesischen Vizeminister Li Chenggang. Der slowakische Kommissar erklärte, China habe Verständnis für die Bedenken Europas: „Alle von uns angesprochenen Themen liegen auf dem Tisch. Ich sage nicht, dass wir Zusicherungen haben, dass wir sie lösen werden, aber sie liegen auf dem Tisch.“

World.title: G7 to hold emergency talks over possible diesel release
World.content:
U.S. President Donald Trump speaks with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney next to French President Emmanuel Macron at a working lunch with leaders of G7, on June 16, 2026 in Evian-les-bains, France. | Pool photo by Evelyn Hockstein via Getty Images

The meeting comes as Trump threatens to ban U.S. diesel exports.

BRUSSELS — The G7 club of rich countries is preparing to convene later today to explore whether to release further diesel reserves to bring down fuel prices.

Four people familiar with the matter confirmed the plan to POLITICO. The meeting will take place after the U.S. pressured European countries to act on their reserves or face an export ban.

The meeting of the Group of Seven, which includes France, Germany, Italy, the U.K., the U.S., Canada and Japan, will come on Friday afternoon amid growing concern over rising diesel costs that have triggered a pressure campaign by Washington.

World.title: Frankreich erwägt Freigabe von Öl- und Dieselreserven nach US-Druck
World.content:
Berlin hingegen zögerte laut den Informanten, überhaupt Barrel freizugeben. „Deutschland und andere Länder wollen nicht instrumentalisiert werden; sie möchten ihre Vorräte nur aus echten Gründen der Versorgungssicherheit freigeben“, sagte einer von ihnen POLITICO unter der Bedingung der Anonymität, um – wie auch andere in diesem Artikel – offen sprechen zu können. Deutschland und Frankreich verfügen laut offiziellen EU-Statistiken über die größten Reserven an Öl und Erdölprodukten in Europa.

„Frankreich ist sehr daran interessiert, sich zu beteiligen und der Bitte nachzukommen … es ist klar, dass die EU etwas unternehmen wird, sofern sie sich auf etwas einigen kann“, sagte die zweite Person. Sie fügten hinzu, dass unklar sei, ob die Freigabe gemeinsam von der EU koordiniert oder auf bilateraler Basis erfolgen werde, angesichts des „chaotischen“ Vorgehens der USA, die unterschiedliche Anfragen an verschiedene Länder gerichtet hätten. „Das ist eine typische Anfrage der USA – sie nutzen nicht die üblichen offiziellen Kanäle.“

Ein Sprecher des französischen Wirtschaftsministers Roland Lescure wies den Vorschlag als „Gerüchte“ zurück und lehnte eine weitere Stellungnahme ab. In einer Erklärung teilte der Élysée-Palast mit, dass Emmanuel Macron „so bald wie möglich“ ein Treffen der G7-Staats- und Regierungschefs einberufen werde, „um die erforderlichen Maßnahmen zu koordinieren, die dazu beitragen sollen, den Preisdruck zu mildern und die Versorgung mit Rohöl und Raffinerieprodukten in den G7-Ländern sowie weltweit sicherzustellen“.

Macron führte am Donnerstagabend ein Telefongespräch mit US-Präsident Donald Trump, um „die weltweite Energiesituation zu erörtern“ und „die weltweite Verfügbarkeit von Raffinerieprodukten sicherzustellen“, teilte der Élysée-Palast mit.

Britische Regierungsvertreter erwarten die Einberufung eines G7-Treffens bereits am Freitag, doch seien unmittelbare Ergebnisse unwahrscheinlich, so eine mit der Angelegenheit vertraute Person, der Anonymität gewährt wurde, um über sensible Fragen der Treibstoffversorgung zu sprechen. Eine etwaige Freigabe von Reserven in Europa würde unter der Leitung der IEA erfolgen, so die Person.

Die USA sind zunehmend frustriert über EU-Länder, die ihre Zusagen zu der 400-Millionen-Barrel-Freigabe Anfang des Jahres nicht eingehalten haben. Diese hatte die Internationale Energieagentur (IEA) nach Ausbruch des Krieges im Iran und der Schließung der Straße von Hormus koordiniert. Bei der Sitzung der hochrangigen Energy Union Taskforce am Freitag kritisierten einige EU-Länder laut einer der informierten Personen auch Frankreich und Deutschland dafür, dass sie keine nennenswerten Ölreserven auf den Markt gebracht hätten.

POLITICO berichtete am Donnerstag, dass führende EU-Länder und Großbritannien auf den Druck der USA mit einer „entschlossenen“ Haltung reagieren wollten, gleichzeitig aber eine Deeskalation anstrebten.

Nicolas Camut und Charlie Cooper haben zu diesem Bericht beigetragen. Der Text erschien zuerst auf Englisch bei POLITICO.

World.title: Feijóo: In Ceuta, it’s up to Europe to clean up the Spanish government’s mess
World.content:
The response of the current Spanish government, incapable of acknowledging the true nature of the problem and implementing the correct solution, obliges me to reiterate, first and foremost, the obvious, as the President of Ceuta did last week during his visit to Brussels. We are not witnessing a conventional migration crisis, but rather the consequences of an invasion originating from Morocco, which must therefore be held responsible for having condoned or instigated it.

Normality has disappeared from Ceuta for more than six weeks, and the scenes of chaos, overcrowding and insecurity should both shame us and compel us to act. To think that the prolongation of this situation will have no consequences is a mistake we cannot afford to make: it affects our sovereignty, our collective capacity to defend the rule of law, the safety of our citizens, and the credibility of the European project in ensuring its own stability.

Undoubtedly, the national authorities are the first to bear the responsibility for resolving this crisis, in accordance with a non-negotiable principle shared by all EU member states under the Pact on Migration and Asylum: those who have entered irregularly must be returned. All of them. The Spanish government’s obligation is not to find accommodation for them, but to expedite their departure.

That said, given the time that has elapsed and the escalation of violent incidents in Ceuta, Europe as a whole must recognize the failure of the Spanish government and exert the necessary pressure to prevent this crisis from becoming entrenched, spreading, or happening again. Just as Europe has responded when faced with other hybrid threats — on energy, trade or disinformation — the attack on our southern border now demands the same determination.

Firstly, the European Union must ensure that Spain implements, with due rigor and efficiency, all the European instruments available to facilitate returns. Secondly, it must clarify why the Kingdom of Morocco itself has reiterated in an official statement its willingness to take back all those who entered on July 30, while Spanish ministers maintain that no such cooperation exists.

Thirdly, it must make full use of all its diplomatic resources to ensure that the relationship with Morocco, a strategic partner for Spain and for the rest of Europe, continues to develop on the basis of transparency and mutual respect. While I advocate the need to establish a loyal and stable relationship with our neighboring country, I believe it is in the interests of the entire European Union to ensure that this relationship is not undermined by the exploitation of migration flows or by the questioning of the Spanish identity of Ceuta and Melilla, territories that are just as European as Berlin, Paris or Brussels.

World.title: Tension rises in Ceuta: two migrant children stabbed and bacteria-contaminated beach
World.content:
Two underage migrants were injured in a knife attack on Thursday during a fight in the La Marina area of Ceuta, in a new outbreak of violence amid the migration emergency gripping the city. The National Police intervened after the incident and emergency health services treated the two youths, who had cuts around their ankles.

 

The incident comes as Ceuta struggles with the impact of the arrival of tens of thousands of migrants and with the difficulties of providing accommodation for those who remain in the city.

Health alert at Trampolín beach

Ceuta’s Department of Health has also warned of a health risk from contact with the water at Trampolín beach, where a migrant encampment remains in place.

Tests on samples taken on 23, 25 and 28 September found "very high" concentrations of intestinal enterococci and Escherichia coli, above the limits set for coastal waters.

The report released this Friday concludes that there is a "health risk" associated with contact with the water. The Ceuta authorities have also decided to put up fencing on Benítez beach to prevent new encampments from being established in this bathing area.

Migrants sleeping in garages, vehicles and on rooftops

The difficulty of finding accommodation is forcing some migrants to seek alternative places to spend the night. Garages, cars and empty vans are being used as makeshift sleeping areas. In some neighbourhoods, rooftop spaces are being offered for around 12 euros per night.

The security forces have also identified homes being used to house large groups of people. In one of these so-called "patera flats", the police and Civil Guard found up to 30 people inside, most of them minors.

The situation has prompted criticism from some local residents, who complain that people are profiting from migrants’ urgent need for somewhere to stay.

Growing pressure on public services

The UGT-Ceuta local union has demanded "sufficient resources" to maintain the quality of public services and protect workers in the face of the arrival of thousands of migrants. The union has called on the government for a coordinated plan to safeguard public services and restore normality in the city.

The Ombudsman, Ángel Gabilondo, is visiting Ceuta this week to assess first-hand the scale of the humanitarian emergency. He is due to meet the president of the autonomous city, Juan Jesús Vivas, and to visit Ceuta University Hospital.

World.title: US suspends consular services in Brazil as Lula and Bolsonaro fight for election
World.content:
The nail-biter poll is being "very closely" watched by US President Donald Trump, who has championed Latin America's swing to the right in recent elections.

 

Washington suspended consular services in Brasilia over "security concerns," and Australia closed its embassy for the same reason. Neither gave details.

Pressure from Trump has loomed large over a campaign dominated by scandals and insults that has done little to ease Brazil's deep political polarization.

Edinho Silva, president of Lula's Workers' Party (PT), told journalists that the US closing its consulates "makes absolutely no sense. It is one of the ways Trump has to vie for Brazilian public opinion."

Veteran leftist Lula, 80, is in a dead heat with the son of far-right former president Jair Bolsonaro, and opinion polls predict the vote will go to a runoff on 25 October.

"The race is tied but not at a standstill," said Felipe Nunes, director of the Quaest polling institute.

Many of the nation's 160 million registered voters are disenchanted with their options.

Marcelo Vilanova, a 32-year-old fish market manager in the southeastern city of Juiz de Fora, said he was voting for Lula as the "lesser of two evils."

Lucas Sales, 38, a cell phone shop owner in the city, is voting for Flavio Bolsonaro even if "he himself isn't the best option," citing his promise to be tough on crime — a key concern for many Brazilians in this election.

Opposition presidential candidate Sen. Flavio Bolsonaro, center, wearing a green shirt and looking up, campaigns in Sao Paulo, Brazil, Monday, 28 September2026. Copyright 2026 The Associated Press. All rights reserved

'Turned into a circus'

The scramble for undecided voters has had both sides on alert for anything they can twist to their advantage.

In recent days, Brazil's patron saint, Our Lady of Aparecida, became the focus as rumours erupted that Flavio Bolsonaro planned to strip her of her position if elected.

Bolsonaro, 45, issued fierce denials as Lula took to the campaign trail clutching a statue of the beloved saint, declaring that "messing" with her was "unacceptable."

The electoral court ordered Thursday that posts with the "untrue" claims be taken down.

Next, Bolsonaro and his supporters pounced when Lula said that men were "cowards" when it comes to getting their prostates examined, while "women learn to receive a touch from a young age," referring to gynecological exams.

Clips of his comment circulated widely on social media as if it were an allusion to abuse.

"It's really turned into a circus," said Gisele Sousa, 45, a clothing shop employee. "My vote won't go to any of them."

In another jab during a podcast on Thursday, Lula said he was sure he would win in the first round, over a rival he said was not even qualified "to serve as a building manager."

A tough foe

Lula is seeking a fourth non-consecutive term, boasting he is fitter than ever despite his advanced age.

He made Brazilian sovereignty a central plank of his campaign, warning Trump not to "meddle" in his country's elections.

The former union leader has overseen a drop in inflation and unemployment while massively curbing deforestation in the Amazon rainforest.

Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, who is running for reelection, waves to supporters during a campaign rally in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil on 2 October 2026. Copyright 2026 The Associated Press. All rights reserved

Nevertheless, voters complain about the high cost of living and are fed up with violence and crime.

Lula unveiled a flurry of measures in the election run-up to win over voters, increasing social welfare payments and banning sports betting that has ensnared many in gambling addiction.

Bolsonaro was also confident of a first-round win, vowing that Lula would be "ousted from the presidency" on Sunday.

"Brazil can't stand you anymore," he said.

The once little-known Bolsonaro, a senator since 2019, has proven a tough foe for Lula, even as it emerged that he was under investigation for corruption over the financing of the biopic "Dark Horse" about his father.

He was forced during the campaign to admit he had asked jailed banker Daniel Vorcaro, at the heart of one of Brazil's largest financial fraud cases, to bankroll the film.

World.title: Sánchez begins reflection on early election as protesters call for general strike
World.content:
Pedro Sánchez enters a period of reflection. The Prime Minister will use this weekend to decide whether to bring forward the general election after Congress on Friday threw out two housing decrees put forward by his Socialist government.

 

The parliamentary defeat leaves the government facing a new scenario and Sánchez having to decide on the future of the legislature. According to government sources cited by several national media outlets, the prime minister will, over the coming days, consider whether to call elections before the end of the year.

Hours before the votes, the government had played down that possibility and insisted that an early election was not on the table because "hoy no toca" (today is not the day). After the result unfolded, the executive said it would analyse the situation without ruling out any option.

The two decrees were rejected after more than four hours of debate. The first fell by 178 votes to 172, with the Popular Party, Vox, Junts, and UPN all voting against. The second was defeated by 184 votes to 166, after the PNV and Canary Islands Coalition joined the 'no' camp.

Sánchez's political future hanging

While Sánchez's political future hangs in the balance, the reaction outside Congress has been immediate. Protesters who had been camped out for days in Puerta del Sol marched to Congress on Friday to follow a vote they regarded as crucial to their demands.

Once the rejection of the first decree was confirmed, some of the protesters headed back to Sol chanting "general strike". A general assembly was scheduled for the afternoon to decide the next steps in the movement and the future of the camp itself.

The Confederation of Tenants' Unions has also called demonstrations this Saturday in more than 50 Spanish cities and is already signalling an escalation in protest: "the next step is a general strike", the organisation said.

The spokesperson for the Tenants' Union, Alicia del Río, had already on Friday called for a general strike over housing and warned that the mobilisation would not end with the vote in Congress.

A weekend with two unknowns

The fall of the decrees opens a weekend marked by two key questions. The first will be answered in the political arena: whether Sánchez chooses to continue the legislature or bring forward the general election.

The second lies on the streets. Protests will continue this Saturday in dozens of cities, and housing campaign groups will have to decide how far to step up their mobilisation and how to put into practice their call for a general strike.

Two very different responses to the same vote, which has put on hold both the government's next move and that of a housing protest which, for now, shows no sign of ending.

World.title: Russia 'tearing Kyiv apart', mayor says, as strikes paralyse traffic
World.content:
President Volodymyr Zelensky accused his Russian counterpart, Vladimir Putin, of ripping up the rulebook of armed conflict by sanctioning massive attacks on civilian areas, an accusation the Kremlin has rejected.

 

The grinding conflict, which began with Russia's full-scale invasion in February 2022, has largely focused on ground fighting in the east, with Kyiv mostly spared from the devastation wrought near the frontline.

But Kyiv mayor Vitali Klitschko said the city should now be on a war footing.

"The capital is in a very dramatic situation," he posted on Telegram. "It's no longer possible to pretend that we can live now as we lived in peacetime."

"The enemy is tearing Kyiv apart."

His message came as the authorities shut one of Kyiv's main bridges and restricted movement on a second after another wave of deadly strikes by fast-moving, jet-powered drones.

Traffic heavily disturbed

Long lines of stationary cars and buses were gridlocked on main roads as commuters sought alternative routes — or even made their way on foot.

"I've been travelling for three hours... to get to work," said Tetiana Osypenko, a 49-year-old seamstress whose bus was stuck in a traffic jam.

"There's just no way to get there. Nothing. It's impossible to cross the bridges today," she said.

Traffic built up due to the complete closure to all vehicles going in both directions on the Southern Bridge, one of eight bridges connecting the east and west of Kyiv over the Dnipro river.

A residential building is seen damaged following a Russian drone strike, in Kyiv, Ukraine, Friday, 2 October 2026. Copyright 2026 The Associated Press. All rights reserved

The cable-stayed bridge has been hit several times since Thursday, with new strikes confirmed by Klitschko on Friday afternoon.

The Paton Bridge, further north, was open in one direction only, though there were no reports that it had been struck.

On X, Zelensky accused Putin of last month declaring there were "no rules now", citing unnamed intelligence and people around Putin.

"The Russians couldn't occupy us. So now they are doing massive attacks and massive killings," Zelensky said in remarks first made in a Financial Times interview.

The Kremlin made no immediate public response to the claim.

Daily bombing fear

Kyiv has been increasingly under aerial bombardment in recent months, putting the city on near-constant alert and disrupting daily life.

Air raid sirens warning of approaching threats in the skies sound almost round the clock, urging the city's estimated three million people to seek shelter.

Repeated strikes on trains and petrol stations have already hit the rail and road networks while attacks on energy facilities threaten power and heating as winter approaches.

Osypenko, the seamstress, said previous disruptions to subway services during air raids have forced her to spend the night in a metro station near the Southern Bridge.

Local residents look at fragments of Shahed drone near a multi-storey residential building damaged following a Russian strike, in Kyiv, Ukraine. Copyright 2026 The Associated Press. All rights reserved

Loss of earnings compounds the financial pressures caused by the war, she added. "You just spend the whole day feeling completely beaten down."

The latest Russian attacks killed one person and wounded at least two other people when a 25-storey residential building was hit in southeast Kyiv.

Two people were killed and dozens more injured when Russian shelling hit residential areas in the eastern city of Kharkiv, city mayor Igor Terekhov said on Telegram.

'Political will'

Zelensky urged tougher sanctions to prevent Russia from manufacturing jet-powered drones, which are harder to intercept.

Russia's production of the weapons was "critically dependent" on foreign components, he wrote on social media on Friday.

"Every Russian drone can actually be stopped right at the production line. What is needed is the political will of these countries," he added.

Zelensky has repeatedly called on Ukraine's Western allies for more military support, particularly for US-made Patriot missile interceptors.

People carry an injured woman into an ambulance after a Russian drone strike in Kyiv, Ukraine, Monday, 28 September 2026. Copyright 2026. The Associated Press. All rights reserved

On Thursday, he said Ukraine had used its FP-7 tactical ballistic missile in combat for the first time, without disclosing where or what it had been used against.

He also said Ukraine was testing five of its own interceptors against drones.

Ukraine's military on Friday said it struck an oil refinery in Volgograd and another facility in Samara, both in southwest Russia, for allegedly supplying fuel to Russian forces.

Kyiv also dismissed reports that its F-16 fighter jets — another key tool used against jet-powered drones — could be grounded due to delays in maintenance inspections and the supply of parts.

But Zelensky told the Financial Times that around half of Ukraine's fleet was spending lengthy maintenance periods in Europe.

World.title: Debt-saddled Argentina pitches 'golden passport' scheme to woo wealthy foreigners
World.content:
As an attempt to curb Argentina's debt, President Javier Milei announced a plan to give out passports to wealthy foreigners for cash or investments.

 

Economy Minister Luis Caputo unveiled the so-called "golden passport" scheme at an investor event in Paris, saying applications are expected to open before the end of the year.

Applicants have two options: make a nonrefundable €311,000 contribution to the Argentine Treasury or invest €711,000 in a new government bond that must be held for seven years. Contributions would increase depending on family size, with a family of four expected to pay €444,000, officials said.

Securing dollars is critical for Milei as he prepares to seek reelection next year. Argentina’s Treasury faces nearly €22 billion in foreign-currency debt payments coming due in 2027. But having narrowed its financing options by holding off on a return to international bond markets, the government is searching for alternative sources of revenue.

A consortium of investment firms advising the government estimated that the paid-citizenship program could raise up to €2.2 billion for Argentina if it receives the expected number of applicants.

'A kind of status symbol'

So-called "golden visa" programs have become increasingly common among cash-strapped countries battling to attract deep-pocketed foreigners, with about 60 nations offering residency privileges in exchange for one-off investments. U.S. President Donald Trump launched his own "gold card" program for the U.S. last year.

Citizenship-for-investment programs go further, offering more rights and a passport that opens doors abroad. Only about a dozen countries have active programs, including small Caribbean island states.

"I think every wealthy American will consider this," Nuri Katz, president of Apex Capital Partners, told Forbes. "It’s so unique that it’ll be seen both as an insurance policy and as a kind of a status symbol, like the Amex Black Card. As in, ‘oh, you don’t have Argentina."

Milei announces 'Golden passports' for wealthy foreigners that would pay a cash contribution or invest in government bonds. Argentine Ministry of Foreign Affairs

Argentina, a G-20 nation of 46 million people home to a vast Patagonian wilderness and culturally vibrant capital, is set to become the first South American country to join their ranks.

"The Argentine passport is highly valued, accepted in more than 140 countries," Caputo said, referring to destinations Argentines can visit without obtaining a visa in advance — from China and Russia to Europe’s Schengen area and most of Latin America.

For wealthy people from countries that face visa restrictions, whether in Southeast Asia or the Arab world, Argentine citizenship could make it easier to travel and do business internationally, said Kristin Surak, a professor at the London School of Economics and author of "The Golden Passport: Global Mobility for Millionaires."

"It’s not only the benefits that you get within Argentina," she said. "You also get benefits globally in terms of where you can go."

Plan B passport

The clientele of such programs has shifted since the COVID-19 pandemic, industry experts say, with more Americans and Europeans — whose passports already offer extensive visa-free travel — seeking a foothold abroad as an escape hatch at a time of mounting geopolitical uncertainty.

“The Southern Cone of South America is the ultimate Plan B destination. It’s not on the way to anywhere strategically important. It’s a region that’s always staying out of global armed conflict,” said Christian Nesheim, editor of Investment Migration Insider, a trade journal. "It’s self-sufficient when it comes to food, to energy."

A country with a history of military coups, debt defaults and runaway inflation that long sent its own business elite seeking opportunities abroad might seem an unlikely refuge for investors chasing stability. But Milei is trying to recast Argentina as a destination for foreign wealth, slashing public spending, dismantling regulations and courting investment in the country’s vast oil and mineral resources.

Argentina's Minister of Economy Luis Caputo delivers a statement at the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) headquarters on 1 October 2026. Copyright 2026 The Associated Press. All rights reserved

Caputo said the idea for the citizenship-for-investment program emerged during Milei’s July 2024 visit to Sun Valley, Idaho, when tech executives expressed interest in obtaining Argentine citizenship.

A self-proclaimed "anarcho-capitalist," Milei has cultivated close ties with libertarian-minded tech billionaires such as Elon Musk, a vocal supporter of Milei's drive to shrink government. Last year, he brandished a chainsaw gifted by the Argentine leader as a symbol of his own campaign to slash U.S. government spending.

Another ideological ally is Peter Thiel, a co-founder of software firm Palantir who temporarily moved his family to Buenos Aires in April. Corporate records obtained by The Associated Press show that a company linked to his investment firm, Thiel Capital, owns a €12 million mansion in the city’s upscale Barrio Parque neighborhood. Thiel also secured New Zealand citizenship in 2011, receiving a special exemption from the usual residency requirements.

"I think that this 'Peter Thiel in Argentina' story is maybe a bit of a proof of concept (for the citizenship program)," said Philippe Amarante, managing partner and head of government advisory at Henley & Partners, a consultancy that helps clients obtain passports around the globe.

"He stands for this idea that independent, wealthy, successful people do have choices around the world. And if you provide the right environments and right habitats, the right ecosystem, they might choose you."

Selling citizenship vulnerable to corruption

Golden passport programs have long drawn criticism over their vulnerability to corruption. The Financial Action Task Force, the global money-laundering watchdog, has warned that criminals exploit citizenship and residency programs to conceal their identities, launder illicit wealth and evade justice.

In a blow to the investment migration industry, the European Union’s top court ruled Malta’s golden passport program unlawful in April 2025, declaring that EU citizenship could not be sold. Other countries have also scrapped cash-for-residency programs, citing concerns ranging from dirty money to housing affordability.

Caputo vowed to prevent such pitfalls, with intelligence and financial oversight agencies helping to vet applicants’ identities, criminal records and sources of funds.

The aim, he said, is to protect "the international standing of Argentine citizenship."

World.title: DR Congo Ebola outbreak killed more than 4,000: official figures
World.content:
The Ebola outbreak, officially detected in mid-May, has hit unstable regions in the vast central African country where armed clashes and violence, alongside a critical lack of resources, have hindered the health response to the deadly virus in recent days.

 

According to the latest official data, there have been 4,018 fatalities from 8,300 cases, with 2,162 people recovering, giving a fatality rate to date of 48.4 percent.

Also recorded have been four deaths among six cases in North Kivu province in the northeast in areas controlled by the anti-government group M23, the Kigali-backed group stated Friday.

After starting in Ituri, also in the northeast, the current outbreak has spread to seven provinces in the north and east.

The response has been hindered by conflict but also mistrust of authority which runs deep among inhabitants of several provinces.

Violent clashes disturbing health aid

Recent days have seen violent clashes between local militias that have hampered the response in Ituri, with more than 5,000 people displaced, the UN said on Thursday.

A transit centre for Ebola patients burned down Tuesday in the same province after soldiers entered a site for displaced people who promptly fled, according to the UN.

A contractor responsible for detecting cases was also killed in an attack on a health facility in North Kivu province, Congolese authorities said Wednesday.

French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot was due in Ituri capital Bunia on Friday to show Paris' support for local authorities and humanitarian workers.

Medical workers work inside a mobile lab set up to test rapidly for Ebola virus in Butembo, DR Congo. Copyright 2026 The Associated Press. All rights reserved

There is no indication France is offering fresh humanitarian aid, but the country did allocate €13.4M to the fight against Ebola between January and July.

The United States has meanwhile announced it is releasing a further €237M to combat the spread of the disease.

Healthcare workers are notably at risk of contracting the virus in poor and remote regions where healthcare infrastructure is poor.

Several vaccines and treatments are currently being studied to combat the Bundibugyo strain of the Ebola virus, which is behind the current outbreak.

The first doses of the Ervebo vaccine — which has been proven effective against the Zaire strain, the most common variant, in the past — have been administered in recent weeks to volunteers among frontline staff as part of a clinical trial.

World.title: Christa Pike unconscious after failed execution — attorneys
World.content:
Lawyers for Christa Pike said she's unconscious and on a ventilator after a botched execution attempt. Pike is believed to be the first person to have survived the administration of lethal drugs in the modern era.

Christa Pike was unconscious and on a ventilator in a Nashville hospital in the hours after her bungled execution attempt in Tennessee, her attorneys said in a court filing on Friday.

Pike, who was sentenced to death for the 1995 murder of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer, was audibly snoring after she was injected with two doses of lethal injection on Wednesday.

The court filing is the first account of what Pike went through in the hours after the botched execution attempt.

Pike's attorneys said they believed problems with the IV lines caused the lethal drug, called pentobarbital, to flow into her body instead of her bloodstream.

"Apparently at no point did any member of the execution team realize that the IV lines were not correctly placed or that the veins had blown and that the pentobarbital was, in whole or in part, entering Ms. Pike's body," they wrote in the court filing.

Instead of "remedying this failure," they prepared and administered a second dose of pentobarbital, her lawyers said.

Pike believed to be first person to survive administration of lethal drugs

There are now questions about what happens next and whether the state can attempt to execute Pike again given her medical state.

Tennessee Governor Bill Lee, a Republican, temporarily paused the state execution on Thursday, saying there would be a "comprehensive, third-party review" of the case.

Pike, who is 50 years old, was set to become the first woman executed in Tennessee in 200 years.

She is believed to be the first person to survive after being injected with lethal doses of execution drugs in the modern era of the death penalty, according to the Death Penalty Information Center .

World.title: North Korea fires ballistic missile into sea, Seoul says
World.content:
North Korea fired a ballistic missile toward the sea off its east coast, the South Korean military has said.

South Korea’s Joint Chiefs of Staff said North Korea fired a ballistic missile on Saturday.

"Our military detected a ballistic missile launched from the Wonsan area of North Korea toward the East Sea," the Joint Chiefs of Staff said, referring to the body of water also known as the Sea of Japan.

The test came amid heightened tensions between the countries.Land mine blasts injured three South Korean soldiers last month. South Korea and the US-led UN Command have said North Korean mines caused the blasts.

On Friday, ​Pyongyang's Kim Yo Jong, the influential sister of ​leader Kim Jong Un, dismissed Seoul's demand for an apology over the blasts in the Demilitarised Zone, the heavily fortified 4-kilometer-wide (2.5-mile) area between the two Koreas.

Seoul called on Pyongyang to end efforts to fortify the border, including the use of mines and anti-tank barriers.

Kim Yo Jong called those demands "utterly pathetic," adding that the North intended to cut ties with the South.

The projectile launch on Saturday came after weeks of North Korean military displays, including tests of a purported hypersonic missile system, live-fire exercises and the commissioning of a new warship.

Kim Jong Un has also continued to flaunt his growing nuclear program despite US calls to revive diplomacy.

World.title: UK: Man charged with planning to attack Nigel Farage
World.content:
The suspect was already charged with the killing of Reform UK's Ann Widdecombe.

A man has been charged with planning acts of terrorism, including against far-right politician and Reform UK leader Nigel Farage, British police said.

"We have been running a hugely intensive and complex investigation for some time," Deputy Assistant Commissioner Vicki Evans said, saying the investigation resulted in "this very serious charge."

The suspect, Joshua Kerry, was also charged with the murder of former MP and Reform UK spokesperson Ann Widdecombe.

According to the prosecutor handling the case, Kerry allegedly hit Widdecombe on her head 21 times with a hammer while she had been eating lunch.

Widdecombe's murder triggered reactions from across British politics, including demands to improve lawmakers' security arrangements.

The new charges against Kerry include one count of preparing acts of terrorism for actions allegedly carried out between May 31, 2024 and July 8, 2026.

According to the police's statement, the 28-year-old suspect is due to appear in a London magistrates' court on October 7.

Apart from Widdecombe, two other politicians were murdered this decade. Labor's Jo Cox was murdered by a neo-Nazi sympathizer in 2016 and Conservative David Amees was killed in 2021 by an "Islamic State" supporter.

World.title: New York governor condemns handling of Cornell rape case
World.content:
An 2024 alleged gang rape at the prestigious Cornell University has gained national attention after the accuser, identified only as Jane Doe, filed a lawsuit. A special prosecutor has been appointed to handle the case.

New York Governor Kathy Hochul said the accuser of the six Cornell University students of gang rape was "failed" by those whose obligation was protecting her.

This includes both campus police and the county prosecutor, Hochul said.

At a press conference on Friday, she also announced the appointment of Attorney General Letitia James as a special prosecutor to take over the investigation due to the fact she had lost faith in the local district attorney's ability to handle the case.

This came after she learned the "troubling" details of the authorities' handling of the accuser's case so far.

"In what world does the district attorney not even interview her, or anyone else involved, or even request the full transcript?" Hochul asked.

"This young woman had already endured something that is utterly unspeakable. And then at every turn, she was failed by people and institutions with an obligation to protect her."

Cornell Univesity defended its handling of the case Image: Heather Ainsworth/AP Photo/picture alliance

According to Hochul, the woman, identified only by the placeholder name Jane Doe, told police "exactly what happened to her," including her firm belief that she had been raped.

"Yet, shockingly, those words never made it into the account that the Cornell police sent to prosecutors."

Investigation to take time

Attorney General Letitia James said she did not know how long her investigation might take.

"I know that you want answers. I do too. A comprehensive investigation of this nature takes time, but my office is committed to seeing it through," James said, adding that evidence gathering and interviews will be carried out.

The original investigation into the case was closed without any charges in 2024.

Jane Doe's lawsuit in 2026 gained national attention Image: Melissa Bender/NurPhoto/picture alliance

According to Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten, who was responsible for the decision, the woman's sworn statement did not include her allegation of being drugged against her will without any ability to consent and forced into sex.

Van Houten reopened the investigation after the accuser filed a new lawsuit in September, 2026, against seven fraternity members, as well as against Cornell.

The lawsuit has since made national headlines and sparked protests at Cornell and across the United States.

Sanctions have been taken against the Chi Phi fraternity, involved in the case Image: Heather Ainsworth/AP Photo/picture alliance

Cornell said it launched a comprehensive investigation and barred the Chi Phi fraternity involved in the allegations, while also imposing a range of disciplinary measures.

The school also said it supports James' appointment and is "committed to an independent external review of all aspects" of its handling of the case.

Edited by: Zac Crellin
