World.title: Russia ‘tearing Kyiv apart’, mayor says, as strikes paralyse traffic
World.content:
Kyiv – Russian attacks on key infrastructure were “tearing Kyiv apart”, the city’s mayor said Friday, as strikes on a bridge linking the capital’s east and west brought traffic to a standstill.

President Volodymyr Zelensky accused his Russian counterpart, Vladimir Putin, of ripping up the rulebook of armed conflict by sanctioning massive attacks on civilian areas, an accusation the Kremlin has rejected.

The grinding conflict, which began with Russia’s full-scale invasion in February 2022, has largely focused on ground fighting in the east, with Kyiv largely spared from the devastation wrought near the frontline.

But Kyiv mayor Vitali Klitschko said the city should now be on a war footing.

“The capital is in a very dramatic situation,” he posted on Telegram. “It’s no longer possible to pretend that we can live now as we lived in peacetime.

“The enemy is tearing Kyiv apart.”

His message came as the authorities shut one of Kyiv’s main bridges and restricted movement on a second after another wave of deadly strikes by fast-moving, jet-powered drones.

Long lines of stationary cars and buses were gridlocked on main roads as commuters sought alternative routes — or even made their way on foot.

“I’ve been travelling for three hours… to get to work,” said Tetiana Osypenko, a 49-year-old seamstress whose bus was stuck in a traffic jam.

“There’s just no way to get there. Nothing. It’s impossible to cross the bridges today,” she told AFP.

Traffic built up due to the complete closure to all vehicles going in both directions on the Southern Bridge, one of eight bridges connecting the east and west of Kyiv over the Dnipro river.

It was hit several times on Thursday and Friday morning.

The Paton Bridge, further north, was open in one direction only, though there were no reports that it had been struck.

In a post on X, Zelensky accused Putin of last month declaring there were “no rules now”, citing unnamed intelligence and people around Putin.

“The Russians couldn’t occupy us. So now they are doing massive attacks and massive killings,” Zelensky said.

The Kremlin made no immediate public response to the claim, which Zelensky first made in an interview with the Financial Times.

– Daily disruption –

Kyiv has been increasingly under aerial bombardment in recent months, putting the city on near-constant alert and disrupting daily life.

Air raid sirens warning of approaching threats in the skies sound almost round the clock, urging the city’s estimated three million people to seek shelter.

Repeated strikes on trains and petrol stations have already hit the rail and road networks while attacks on energy facilities threaten power and heating as winter approaches.

Osypenko, the seamstress, said she would not get home because of the traffic jams. Previous disruption to subway services during air raids forced her to spend the night in a metro station near the Southern Bridge.

Not being able to work costs her money, compounding the financial pressures caused by the war, she added. “You just spend the whole day feeling completely beaten down.”

The latest Russian attacks killed one person and wounded at least two other people when a 25-storey residential building was hit in southeast Kyiv.

– ‘Political will’ –

Zelensky urged tougher sanctions to prevent Russia from manufacturing its new jet-powered drones, which are faster and harder to intercept.

Russia’s production of the weapons was “critically dependent” on foreign components, he wrote on social media on Friday.

“Every Russian drone can actually be stopped right at the production line. What is needed is the political will of these countries,” he added.

Zelensky has repeatedly called on Ukraine’s Western allies for more military support, particularly for US-made Patriot missile interceptors.

On Thursday, he said Ukraine had used its FP-7 tactical ballistic missile in combat for the first time, without disclosing where or what it had been used against.

He also said Ukraine was testing five of its own interceptors against drones.

Ukraine’s military on Friday said it struck an oil refinery in Volgograd and another facility in Samara, both in southwest Russia, for allegedly supplying fuel to Russian forces.

Kyiv also dismissed reports that its F-16 fighter jets — another key tool used against jet-powered drones — could be grounded due to delays in maintenance inspection and the supply of parts.

But Zelensky told the Financial Times that around half of Ukraine’s fleet was spending lengthy maintenance periods in Europe.

World.title: Man City verdict a ‘big topic’ for England players, says Tuchel
World.content:
London – Thomas Tuchel said that Manchester City were the talk of the England camp after the club were found guilty of multiple breaches of Premier League financial rules, but insisted that the case would not affect his selection for Saturday’s match in Croatia.

The findings by an independent commission, announced earlier this week, have sent shockwaves through English football.

City, the dominant Premier League force over the past 15 years, face severe sanctions, which could include expulsion from the top division.

Marc Guehi and Elliott Anderson are the only two City players remaining in Tuchel’s squad for the Nations League match in Rijeka after Nico O’Reilly was forced to withdraw due to injury.

“We had some time off and some time between the matches, and it’s a big subject,” Tuchel told his pre-match press conference on Friday.

“Of course the players talk about it, and City players talk about it, and we talk to them, but only briefly.

“They’re ready to go for tomorrow, that’s what they show on the pitch and that’s what they show in camp, but of course it’s a big topic.”

City deny wrongdoing and on Friday lodged an appeal against the ruling.

But unless they can overturn the decision of the commission, they are likely to face at least a points deduction, which would threaten their place in the Premier League.

Tuchel was asked if the club’s players would still be in his mind for selection should they be playing regularly in the lower divisions.

“There’s always a possibility,” he said. “I think I would always try to pick the best team for the camp, for the occasion, for the tournament, and I will never rule out that they don’t play in the top flight in their country.

“So we need to look at this from case by case.”

England’s clash with Croatia, which will take place behind closed doors, is their third of four Nations League games in the current international window.

The Three Lions were beaten 3-2 by world champions Spain on home soil last weekend, but bounced back to beat the Czech Republic 2-0 on Tuesday.

World.title: US posts weak job growth data in September
World.content:
Washington – Employment in the United States grew by 29,000 jobs in September, missing analysts’ expectations significantly, with the unemployment rate rising slightly to 4.2 percent, government data showed on Friday.

Adding to the weak data, the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) also revised down job figures for July and August by a combined 60,000 jobs, the department said in a statement.

The revision to July’s data showed that the world’s largest economy lost jobs that month, as opposed to posting a gain of 21,000 as previously reported.

The data comes ahead of key midterm elections in November where President Donald Trump’s Republican Party is facing a stern test over his handling of the economy.

Analysts polled by Dow Jones Newswires and the Wall Street Journal had expected the US economy to add 84,000 jobs in September.

– Health care leads –

Employment in most major sectors was largely unchanged, the BLS reported, with health care posting notable gains of 17,000.

The sector has propped up the labor market in the United States in the last year, as an aging population requires more care both in hospitals and at home.

Still, September’s gains in the sector were slower than its average monthly gain of 33,000 over the last year.

The financial sector continued its downward slide, losing 7,000 jobs in September and bringing its overall slump from a recent peak in May 2025 to 129,000.

Most of the losses in that sector have been among insurance companies.

– Fed implications –

Average hourly earnings for all employees were up 3.0 percent, the BLS said, with wages continuing to lag behind stubbornly high inflation — meaning most workers are seeing real wage losses.

Democratic Senator Elizabeth Warren seized on the data to criticize Trump’s performance since taking office last year.

“Paychecks are growing at their slowest rate in nearly seven years, outside of the Covid-19 pandemic,” she said in a statement.

“Since the start of Trump’s war, real wages have fallen 0.7 percent as his failed agenda keeps pushing prices up,” she said, referring to the US war against Iran launched in late February.

The conflict has plunged the Middle East into violence and sent global energy prices skyrocketing, as Tehran’s retaliatory action has targeted Washington’s regional allies and choked a key trading route.

The data comes after the US Federal Reserve — which has a dual mandate to maintain inflation at a long-term two-percent target while ensuring maximum employment — raised interest rates last month to address high prices.

The US labor market has been largely in balance this year, with modest job gains and a relatively steady unemployment rate.

That steadiness has allowed the Fed to focus on the inflation side of its mandate, but any weakness in the labor market may give policy makers pause.

Raising interest rates tends to cool inflation but can also limit economic activity, which can affect the job market.

This week, two key Fed policymakers indicated that the central bank may not raise rates again at its October meeting, although markets continue to expect a further hike before the end of the year.

Friday’s jobs data “lends support to the less hawkish Fed officials that indicate no need to rush and deliver the next rate hike at the end of this month,” said Kathy Bostjancic, chief economist at Nationwide, in a note.

She added that this could release some pressure on bond yields — which have been spiralling in part due to expectations of interest rate hikes.

Nancy Vanden Houten at Oxford Economics, however, disagreed, expecting upside risks to inflation to continue to dominate Fed policymakers’ thinking.

“We think the upside risks to inflation are still a bigger concern for the Federal Reserve and expect they will raise rates at the end of the month,” she said.

World.title: Ethiopia’s conflict: the regional dimension
World.content:
Addis Ababa – Renewed fighting between the Ethiopian government and Tigrayan rebels has worsened regional tensions, with Ethiopia and Eritrea breaking diplomatic ties on Thursday.

Heavy fighting resumed between federal forces and the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) last week, and fighting has been ongoing across several fronts in northern Ethiopia.

The geopolitics of the Horn of Africa are fiendishly complex, with shifting alliances and the involvement of many outside actors with conflicting interests.

Here is what is at stake for the countries concerned:

– Eritrea –

Ethiopia accuses Eritrea of backing the TPLF, including with troops, which it has denied.

On Thursday, they expelled each other’s diplomats and shut down their respective embassies.

Eritrea gained independence from Ethiopia in 1993, and the two sides fought a brutal border war between 1998 and 2000.

Relations improved markedly with the rise of Ethiopia’s Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed in 2018, and Eritrea even fought alongside Ethiopia during the last civil war against the TPLF in 2020-2022.

But relations have since cratered, with Eritrea fearing landlocked Ethiopia plans to invade and seize access to the Red Sea.

“The TPLF is silently allied with its former foe, Eritrea, with supply lines chiefly secured through Tigray’s northern border,” the Chatham House think tank said in a report.

Eritrea’s “priority is to keep war away from its own territory”, it added, before cautioning the country’s actions increase the risk of regional escalation.

– Sudan –

The Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) have close ties with the TPLF and Eritrea. Tigrayan fighters have reportedly fought with the SAF in Sudan’s civil war.

Ethiopia is accused of assisting the United Arab Emirates in supplying the SAF’s opponent, the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), which it has denied.

Sudan was accused of funnelling weapons and supplies to the TPLF during the last war. There were clashes along the shared border in August, suggesting it remains an active concern for the Ethiopian government.

– Egypt –

Egypt is strongly opposed to Ethiopia’s new Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam, which it says will affect downstream Nile waters. It has forged closer ties with Eritrea and Somalia in an apparent anti-Ethiopia front.

Ethiopia expelled an Egyptian diplomat on Thursday, without giving a reason. Cairo responded by expelling an Ethiopian diplomat.

– United Arab Emirates –

The UAE has invested deeply across east Africa as it seeks security partnerships to counter rivals and control the Red Sea, as well as agricultural land, and investments.

It has been one of Abiy’s principal backers, giving him a $3 billion loan and investment package when he came to power in 2018, and building his giant new palace in Addis Ababa, as well as providing military drones and logistical support during the last civil war.

In return, it is alleged that Ethiopia has helped funnel arms to the UAE’s allies in Sudan, though that is denied by both countries.

– United States –

Washington was closely involved in the peace deal that ended the last civil war in 2022.

Its focus has lately been on the Red Sea — and its efforts to contain Iran and its proxies. As a result, it allowed sanctions on Ethiopia and Eritrea to end, with the ill-timed claim that the “national emergency… has expired”.

– Somalia –

Ethiopia’s relations with Somalia were ruptured in January 2024 when Addis Ababa signed a sea-access deal with the breakaway region of Somaliland.

Relations were ultimately restored with Turkish mediation and the deal with Somaliland seemingly put on the back burner.

World.title: Swiss president to quit government
World.content:
Geneva – Swiss President Guy Parmelin announced Friday that he will quit the government at the end of the year, in a sudden move after more than a decade of ministerial service.

Switzerland’s presidency rotates annually among the seven members of the government, called the Federal Council, of which Parmelin, 66, was the longest-serving minister.

Parmelin told a press conference in Bern that he had informed ministerial colleagues of his decision to step down on December 31.

“By then, it will have been 11 years since I was elected to this role, and the time has come for me to make way for new energy in these times of great uncertainty,” he said, admitting to feeling “a certain weariness”, while insisting he was not stepping down for medical reasons.

– Tariff tussle with Trump –

A pragmatist, Parmelin seemed to make more headway with US President Donald Trump than his predecessor Karin Keller-Sutter.

Trump shocked Switzerland in August 2025 when he announced 39-percent duties on imports of Swiss goods, among the highest in his global tariff blitz.

Parmelin, the economy minister, went to Washington three times in a bid to reduce the rate.

Eventually, Switzerland and the United States announced a declaration of intent to cut tariffs to 15 percent, with the Swiss vowing to invest $200 billion in the United States.

A winegrower by trade, Parmelin is from the French-speaking western canton of Vaud. He is from the hard-right Swiss People’s Party (SVP), which is the biggest in the country,

Parmelin was previously president in 2021 and took centre-stage as Switzerland hosted a summit in Geneva between Russian President Vladimir Putin and US President Joe Biden.

The president of the Swiss Confederation is first among equals on the Federal Council, chairs its meetings and typically represents the country in major domestic and international matters.

The position goes to whoever has had the longest run on the council without being president.

Foreign Minister Ignazio Cassis will become president in 2027.

Parmelin joined the Federal Council in 2016 as defence minister and has held the economy brief since 2019.

The Federal Council seven seats are shared 2-2-2-1 among the four main political parties under a decades-old tacit agreement known as “the magic formula”.

Parmelin’s successor will come from the SVP. Candidates have until October 23 to come forward, and parliament will choose on December 9.

Parmelin will visit India for a three-day state visit from Monday.

World.title: Pilot in flydubai attack says could not let ‘all those people die’
World.content:
Dubai – An Indian pilot attacked by his co-pilot aboard a flight from the UAE to Israel said Friday that he “could not let all those people die”, in his first public remarks after he helped stop the plane from crashing.

His actions on Wednesday helped avert disaster when he managed to open the cockpit door despite suffering injuries, allowing passengers and crew to take control of the plane and make an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia.

The co-pilot has been returned to the United Arab Emirates, where the incident is under investigation to determine any “terrorist activity or intent”.

The mostly Israeli passengers on the flight have been flown back to Israel on a replacement plane.

Flydubai captain Smit Machchhar told Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi during a call from his hospital bed that he knew he had to act quickly, saying his opening the cockpit door was a “last push” to get help.

“I had suffered so many injuries that I had collapsed. At that time, I could feel that the aircraft was going down. I knew this was the last push, that the door was right there,” he said.

“I was being hit even then, but I just opened the door and everyone came in.”

Machchhar, who has 17 years of aviation experience — 11 as a captain — described the moment he realised the plane was going down while he was lying injured.

He told Modi that during the ordeal, he had recited a Hindu devotional prayer dedicated to the deity Hanuman.

“I know God himself saved me,” he said.

He said years of aviation experience allowed him to understand what was happening even while he was wounded.

– ‘Kill me, kill me’ –

The circumstances of the confrontation are under investigation, but the co-pilot allegedly attacked Machchhar, leaving him wounded and triggering a struggle for control of the aircraft.

Passengers described rushing the cockpit and a fight for control after the plane suddenly plummeted — losing around 17,000 feet of altitude in the span of a minute, according to the Flightradar24 website.

Modi said Machchhar’s actions helped save many lives and avert “a great tragedy”.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu earlier also credited Machchhar, as well as the flight’s passengers, with averting catastrophe.

US President Donald Trump warned on Thursday that if Iran was found to be linked to the attack the country would be “hit very hard”.

Netanyahu has said the suspect had undergone “Islamist radical indoctrination”.

“The attacker, he calls out to the aircrew, ‘Kill me, kill me’,” Netanyahu told US media, adding it was “clear he was suicidal”.

The Israeli leader identified the co-pilot as an Omani national and said Israel would check how he had been cleared to work on flights to the country.

“We have constraints that say that you can’t have pilots from countries that don’t have diplomatic relations with Israel. Obviously he was able to go through that,” Netanyahu told Fox News.

Flydubai has suspended flights to and from Israel since the attack, leaving some Israelis stranded in the UAE.

Israel’s flag carrier El Al is planning replacement flights to bring them home but was forced to cancel them Friday, saying Emirati authorities had not given landing permission.

“As soon as approval is received from the authorities, we are prepared to carry out the special flights to Dubai and return the Israelis home as soon as possible,” El Al said in an online notice.

World.title: Disney president says layoffs ‘extremely painful’ but necessary
World.content:
Los Angeles – The Walt Disney Company’s President Dana Walden said on Thursday that the company’s layoffs were “extremely painful” but necessary for its survival.

Disney has carried out several rounds of cost cutting measures in recent years to combat intense competition in streaming, while advances in AI tools have also become a cheaper production alternative for the billion-dollar company.

“We’ve exited colleagues who I’ve worked with for most of my career… It is in many ways a harsh reality,” Walden said during the Bloomberg Screentime conference in Los Angeles.

“It is extremely painful,” she added.

More than 300 people were laid off from Disney on Tuesday, most of whom work in human resources and information technology, according to US media reports.

It comes after Disney eliminated around 1,000 positions in April, primarily across the company’s marketing group, following the arrival of new chief executive Josh D’Amaro, trade media reported.

Walden said the company had also offered a group of executives “the opportunity to make their own decision around whether the timing was right to leave or to stay” as part of a voluntary retirement plan. It remains unclear if the latest wave of layoffs made use of the initiative.

“There is a need to constantly evaluate how you’re structured,” Walden said about Disney and its competitors in the technology industry.

“Technology set their sights on our business, and we must survive and thrive and grow. And that’s what we’re going to do,” she said.

The Walt Disney company did not immediately reply to a request for comment.

World.title: Indian flydubai pilot opened cockpit door to save passengers
World.content:
New Delhi – Indian flydubai captain Smit Machchhar knew he had to act quickly after an alleged in-flight attack by his co-pilot, opening the cockpit door in a “last push” to get help and avert disaster, he said Friday.

“I was trying to save my own life, but I knew I could not let all those people die,” Machchhar said during a call from his hospital bed to Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, according to a video posted by the leader on social media.

The Boeing 737 flight to Tel Aviv, operated by Dubai-based flydubai, was carrying 174 passengers when the altercation took place on Wednesday.

Machchhar, who has 17 years of aviation experience — 11 as a captain — described the moment he realised the plane was going down while he was lying injured.

“I had suffered so many injuries that I had collapsed. At that time, I could feel that the aircraft was going down. I knew this was the last push, that the door was right there,” he said.

“I was being hit even then, but I just opened the door and everyone came in.”

Machchhar told Modi that during the ordeal, he had recited a Hindu devotional prayer dedicated to the deity Hanuman.

“I know God himself saved me,” he said.

Machchhar said years of aviation experience allowed him to understand what was happening even while he was injured.

The circumstances of the confrontation are under investigation.

– ‘Very proud’ –

The co-pilot allegedly attacked Machchhar, leaving him wounded and triggering a struggle for control of the aircraft.

Passengers described rushing the cockpit and a fight for control after the plane suddenly plummeted — losing around 17,000 feet of altitude in the span of a minute, according to the Flightradar24 website — before eventually making an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia.

Modi said Machchhar’s actions helped save many lives and avert “a great tragedy”.

“You have done such a great thing that people across the country and around the world are eager to see you and speak to you,” Modi told him.

“You have truly made the whole country proud.”

Machchhar became emotional during the conversation, telling Modi that he felt proud of himself for the first time since the incident.

“I am feeling very proud right now. I had not felt proud of myself until now,” he said.

The pilot, his head wrapped in bandages, and with a breathing tube in his nose, said the path to recovery was long.

“I am not thinking of it as a wound, I am thinking of it as a journey,” he said.

“And it will take time, but I am very, very confident that I will recover.”

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu earlier credited Machchhar, as well as the flight’s passengers, with averting catastrophe.

World.title: India reviews security SOPs, measures after flydubai event
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Indian security and intelligence establishment is on alert following the failed hijacking of a flydubai flight, undertaking a confidential evaluation of SOPs and security measures in place for the aviation sector, sources said.

In response to new hijacking threats, security authorities are reassessing both ground-level passenger screening, cockpit access vulnerabilities and in-flight countermeasures.

They aim to ascertain whether existing in-flight security measures like two-person cockpit presence mandates and physical barrier protocols require reinforcement.

While Indian authorities are not directly involved in investigating the flydubai incident, intelligence agencies are closely monitoring developments after initial findings attributed the hijacking attempt to radicalisation.

World.title: UAE terms flydubai stabbing 'terrorist act', hails Indian pilot

Calling the flydubai incident a dangerous terrorist act, UAE presidential adviser Anwar Gargash lauded Indian co-pilot Smit Machchhar's critical role in preventing an air disaster by describing him as a true hero.

The remarks suggest that the UAE is not going to downplay the attack, while also serving as the first official acknowledgement by the UAE government of the remarkable fightback by Machchhar against his Omani co-pilot under extreme pressure.

Gargash's comments, which came in the middle of the probe to ascertain if the incident was indeed linked to terrorism, followed the announcement by Israeli ambassador to India Reuven Azar that Israel will suitably honour the Indian pilot.

World.title: Unsolicited advice to Supreme Court lands trial judge in trouble
World.content:
NEW DELHI: It sounds inconceivable that a trial judge will advise the top court of the country on how to decide a case. But it happened recently, and the judge is now in trouble, with the Supreme Court seeking an explanation from him for advising it on when to grant bail.

The case pertains to the bail petition of an accused from West Bengal who has been an undertrial prisoner for the last five years, and the apex court, while rejecting his plea, had asked the trial court to complete the proceedings within three months. The order, which was passed on May 11, directed the trial court to file a report after disposal of the case.

As the trial court could not honour the SC order, the judge wrote to the apex court seeking more time to conclude the trial.

But the judge, the additional district and sessions judge, 3rd court, North 24 Parganas at Barasat, also gave some unsolicited advice to the apex court on bail jurisprudence - when to grant bail and when not.

After reading the letter, which was placed before a bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran, the court expressed shock over its contents, which were uncalled for and directed its registry to ask the judge why he wrote what he wrote.





The bench, however, did not reveal the exact wording of the letter but noted in its order that the judge conveyed words of advice.

"We are quite disturbed with the manner in which the trial judge has addressed a letter to this court requesting some more time. It is not for the presiding officer to convey words of advice as to when this court should grant bail and should not grant bail. The last two paragraphs of the letter are something which we have not appreciated.

Registry to call for an appropriate explanation from the presiding officer at the earliest," SC said.

The judge had written the letter dated Aug 11 addressed to the assistant registrar, Supreme Court, and prayed for some more time to complete the trial. Fixing the time for completion of the trial, SC in May had noted the case was proceeding at a snail's pace and asked that the trial be expedited as the accused had been languishing in jail for the last five years.

World.title: Can't invoke anti-slaughter law in case of mere illegal cattle transportation: SC
World.content:
NEW DELHI: At a time when vigilante groups are active in stopping cattle smuggling purportedly to prevent slaughter, the Supreme Court has ruled that the police cannot presumptively invoke stringent provisions of anti-cattle slaughter laws against people for mere illegal transportation of bovine animals.

Acquitting a person convicted by a trial court and Chhattisgarh HC for illegally transporting 32 bulls under Chhattisgarh Agricultural Cattle Preservation Act, 2004, a bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said police have failed to establish the intention of the accused that cattle were being transported for slaughter. The prosecution said the intercepted truck did not have any document that authorised the driver and cleaner to transport cattle from Chhattisgarh to Odisha.

World.title: Taiwan receives 2 long-delayed US F-16Vs, awaits additional fighter jets
World.content:
Taiwan on Friday received the first two of 65 F-16V fighter jets ordered from the US, the island's air force said, following years of delays.

The two F-16V Block 70 jets landed at Chihhang Air Base in Taitung. There are 63 more to be delivered. The self-ruled island, which is also claimed by Beijing as part of its territory, placed an order for the F-16Vs in 2019.

Taiwan largely purchases arms from the U.S., its largest unofficial ally, to boost its defences in the face of a military threat from China. China sends fighter jets and ships toward the island almost daily. Taiwan's defence minister said on Tuesday that the island remains in continuous discussions with the US about its weapons sales.

The shipment is the first in a long list of backlogged U.S. orders worth almost USD 30 billion. The F-16Vs represent USD 8 billion, or roughly 25 per cent of the entire backlog, according to Taiwan Security Monitor at George Mason University.

The order had been delayed partly owing to production and supply chain issues.

The delivery of the jets comes as the island waits for the US administration to approve an additional USD 14 billion arms package.

That package has stalled after U.S. President Donald Trump met with China's President Xi Jinping in May. US defence sales to Taiwan are a major source of tension between the US and China. Beijing has repeatedly called for Washington to halt sales to Taiwan, with President Xi Jinping personally raising the issue.

World.title: FBI arrests Energy Department employee on charge of trying to support Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen
World.content:
A Department of Energy electrical engineer has been arrested on charges of providing support to the Iranian-backed Houthi rebels, including by buying materials for homemade explosives and drones and travelling to Yemen, the Justice Department said on Thursday (October 1, 2026).

Ashton Hamed Ellaboudy, 51, of Richland, Washington, was arrested on Thursday (October 1, 2026) and is due to make his first court appearance Friday. Court records do not list an attorney available to speak on his behalf.

The FBI says Ellaboudy had a goal of helping the Houthis improve their communications capabilities and traveled last September to Yemen, where the Houthis and Saudi-backed government forces are now engaged in renewed violence that has killed hundreds and displaced tens of thousands. The conflict began in 2014 when the Iran-backed rebels took over the capital, Sanaa, forcing the country's government to settle into exile in Saudi Arabia.

Upon his return to the United States, authorities say, Ellaboudy told Customs and Border Protection officials that he was traveling back from Oman on a work trip and was part of a US government mission to inspect missile defense systems. But investigators interviewed Ellaboudy's supervisor, who reported having no knowledge of any international travel or of an Energy Department missile inspection program that Ellaboudy would have been assigned to, an FBI affidavit said.

Ellaboudy himself was recorded telling FBI informants, whom officials had introduced into the investigation, that he had to be smuggled into and out of Yemen and that he had hoped to reach the country's capital to make government-level connections, the affidavit says. He was ultimately unable to make it to Sanaa, the FBI said.

The FBI says investigators began looking into Ellaboudy after learning that he had purchased precursor chemicals commonly involved in the construction of homemade explosive devices, including acetone and sodium bisulfate, as well as parts used for drones.

During the course of the investigation, the FBI says, he communicated with multiple informants — including one who purported to be a Houthi colonel — and provided advice and assistance on communications equipment.

Ellaboudy is charged under a law that makes it a crime to provide material support to a group designated by the United States as a foreign terrorist organization, of which the Houthis are one.

“These allegations are so deeply disturbing that they almost defy imagination,” John Eisenberg, the assistant attorney general in charge of the Justice Department's National Security Division, said in a statement.

World.title: Ukraine denies F-16 crisis over maintenance and parts
World.content:
Ukraine on Friday (October 3, 2026) denied that it was facing maintenance and supply problems with its F-16 fighter jets, insisting that it can keep them in the air throughout winter.

The Wall Street Journal reported this week that delays in maintenance and a shortage of parts had grounded more than half of Ukraine's fleet, and all of its US-made aircraft could be affected by the year-end.

Kyiv pushed its Western allies for it to be given advanced fighter jets after Russia's full-scale invasion in February 2022 and finally received its first batch of F-16s two years later.

The jets are used to counter the threat from fast-moving jet-powered drones, which Russia is increasingly using across Ukraine, including the capital, Kyiv, and which are harder to shoot down.

The WSJ said there was a "support failure" because of the time it takes to inspect engines, hydraulics, fuel lines and other systems after 300 hours of flying.

Foreign ministry spokesman Georgiy Tykhy acknowledged that Ukraine's F-16s operate "intensively and under demanding conditions" and maintenance was "challenging".

"Certain components for this early F-16 variant are no longer in production and are becoming increasingly difficult to source," he wrote on X on Friday.

"However, recent reports alleging catastrophically low aircraft availability rates and excessively long maintenance turnaround times are simply false," he added.

Mr. Tykhy said overhauled aircraft from allies were now being delivered faster than before.

"We have full confidence in our industry partners and their ability to further optimise sustainment processes, ensuring the highest possible levels of F-16 readiness and availability during the coming winter months, when these capabilities will be needed most," he said.

Belgian company Sabena Engineering, which services Ukraine's F-16s, also denied what it called "erroneous reports citing significant delays in this critical maintenance program".

"All appropriate measures are being proactively implemented, in collaboration with its government and industry partners, to maximise aircraft availability and return the aircraft to service," it said in a statement on Thursday.

President Volodymyr Zelensky, who is pushing for advanced US-made Patriot interceptors to combat Russian drones and missiles, said on Tuesday that Belgium would supply three more F-16s by the year-end.

World.title: At least 5,700 killed, wounded in Haiti gang crisis this year: UN
World.content:
Haiti's gang violence crisis has left at least 5,700 people dead or wounded this year while more than 1,000 women and girls have been raped, UN human rights chief Volker Turk said on Friday (October 2, 2026).

The figures, compiled by the UN mission in Haiti up to September 11, also include 230 kidnappings, though Mr. Turk said "the real figures are likely much higher".

Addressing the UN Human Rights Council, Mr. Turk warned that gangs continue to expand despite the deployment of an international security force intended to help Haitian authorities restore order.

"Despite some success in containing their activity in parts of the capital, Port-au-Prince, gangs continue to adapt and expand, re-emerging in new areas and constantly rearming," he said.

Mr. Turk said the deployed Gang Suppression Force remained significantly understrength. The mission is intended to reach 5,500 personnel but currently has about 1,500 so far.

"The force remains far below the strength needed," Mr. Turk said.

At the same time, he said, the UN had "serious concerns about the unnecessary and disproportionate use of force" by Haiti's national law enforcement and self-defence groups.

"Since the beginning of the year, more than half of all casualties occurred in the context of security operations, with hundreds of people struck by stray bullets and explosive drones," he said.

Mr. Turk said that "so-called self-defence groups" had killed or injured some 280 people so far this year.

'Head of the snake'

William O'Neill, Turk's designated expert on human rights in Haiti, told reporters that the situation was "dire but not hopeless".

He said that if a full-strength Gang Suppression Force had the right capacities — intelligence, night vision, helicopters — it could be highly effective against the gangs, where power resides in a few hands.

He said it was no secret who the gang leaders are and where they are, so if a team could swoop in and arrest the leadership, "most likely the gang collapses".

The gangs understand power, "and if you're more powerful than they are — game over", said lawyer O'Neill, who helped establish the Haitian National Police in 1995.

Capturing a group of top leaders "to cut the head of the snake" would be "absolutely a game-changer", he told the UN correspondents' association.

Through arms embargoes and sanctions, "if you can cut off and strangle their access to financing and weaponry, it becomes much easier than to do anything kinetic", he added.

Of guns recovered from gangs, an "overwhelming number" could be traced back to gun shops in "10 to 12 zip codes in Florida", and he said that the United States "needs to do much more".

Mr. O'Neill said the gangs had no underpinning ideology and were based on "pure criminality", while about half of their members were minors.

"The gangs have no popular support; it's zero. The population hates them, and with good reason," he said.

World.title: India standardises names of 28 places in Ladakh
World.content:
The Government of India, in consultation with the Union Territory administration of Ladakh, has identified 28 places and geographical features in the region by standardised names on the official Survey of India (SoI) map.

The government said the formal identification on the map was aimed at ensuring accurate recognition and creating greater awareness among the public. The latest notification comes days after India standardised the names of places in Arunachal Pradesh amid cartographic aggression by China.

The list in Ladakh includes 11 peaks, five mountains, six land areas, two glaciers, two passes, one valley, one river, one lake and one other water body.

Among the peaks identified are Atisha Giri, Kanishka Peak, Martand Giri, Zorawar Peak, Rinchen Zangpo, Sakyasri Giri, Marpa Lotsava Ri, Milarepa Kangri, Shiva Ri, and Maheshvara Ri. The list also includes Karun Pir, Drak Karpo and Jolmori as mountains.

The government has identified Brangsa, Kuksel, Dehra Compass, Gogra, Kumarayana Point, Panglung, and Shamal Lungpa as land areas. Parpik and Skamri Glacier have been classified as glaciers, while Chapchingal Pass and Shachmirk Pass have been identified as passes.

Other features on the list include Shkorga Valley, Yangpa River, Guru Rinpoche, which has been identified as a lake, and Hot Spring, classified as a water body.

The government said the map of Ladakh, incorporating the additional places and geographical features, can be viewed on the Survey of India website.

Since April 2020, the Chinese People’s Liberation Army (PLA) has amassed a large number of troops and armaments in eastern Ladakh and other areas along the 3,488-km-long LAC. The PLA moved into Indian territory and built fortified structures and defences, in an attempt to permanently alter the status quo on the ground.

While there are differences in perception on the alignment of the LAC, over the years, both sides had concluded a series of agreements to maintain peace on the border, and a moratorium on patrolling was implemented following the June 15, 2020 violent clashes at Galwan, where 20 Indian soldiers were killed. Before this, on May 5, 2020, clashes erupted on the north bank of the Pangong Tso, in which over 70 Indian soldiers were injured.

World.title: Delhi poll officials named ‘objectors’ in 25 cases; ‘reason’ column left blank
World.content:
NEW DELHI

Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) and Assistant Electoral Registration Officers (AEROs) were named as ‘objectors’ for as many as 25 voters among thousands of objections filed against electors in Delhi’s draft roll, according to an analysis of Form 10 reports — a public list of all objections to the inclusion of names in electoral rolls — between September 21 and 27.

These were the only entries among the 1,997 electors whose names were objected to using Form 7 during the seven-day period in which the ‘reason’ column was left blank.

The 25 include 12 objections in Sadar Bazar, three of them by EROs; seven in Malviya Nagar; four in Chhattarpur; and one each in Kirari and Vikaspuri.

All 25 electors had been flagged for notices for either a ‘logical discrepancy’ or ‘no mapping’ in the draft roll published on August 31.

Former Election Commissioner Ashok Lavasa said while the practice of EROs and AEROs filing Form 7s was “unheard of”, using the form to initiate an inquiry could be a “technical requirement” and would not in itself be “illegal” if followed up by due process.

The cases form part of the 4,401 objections received during the claims and objections phase of the ongoing special intensive revision (SIR) drive in Delhi.

Response of officials

When reached for comment on why they had filed the objections, the EROs and AEROs concerned cited reasons such as deaths, field-verification reports by Booth Level Officers (BLOs), complaints from relatives and cases where electors did not appear for notice hearings.

“An objection does not mean deletion of a voter’s name. It is part of the verification process in which electors receive notices and get 15 days to respond on why their names should not be removed,” said an ERO.

Mala Sood, an ERO from Sadar Bazar, said, “This is merely an objection, which could be due to various reasons, including the voter’s death or based on BLO reports. No deletion will happen without verification. A mandatory notice is generated and sent again to the elector.”

The Hindu had on September 27 reported that around 32 electors in Sadar Bazar were marked ‘ineligible’ out of a total of 350 such cases in Delhi for not appearing for hearings or not submitting required documents.

Officials in Malviya Nagar said the objections were raised against the names of ‘ineligible’ voters. “This was done based on a BLO field report, according to which the elector was not at their registered address when the BLO visited to deliver the SIR notice,” an official said.

Form 7 is used to seek deletion of an existing name or to object to the inclusion of a name on grounds such as death, duplicate enrolment, non-citizenship, absence or having permanently shifted. The onus of proof is on the objector, who must be an elector in the same constituency.

What rules say

While the Election Commission’s (EC) Manual on Electoral Rolls 2023 and SIR guidelines are silent on whether an ERO and an AERO can raise objections through Form 7s, EROs are empowered to initiate an inquiry based on BLO reports to examine whether a name should be deleted. The deletion must follow an inquiry, and a reason must be cited for the action. An ERO exercises final authority over the preparation of the roll and decides on all claims and objections.

The Hindu sent queries to Delhi Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) Ashok Kumar’s office on whether EROs and AEROs are expected to use Form 7 to initiate suo motu inquiry. No response was received till the time of going to press.

‘Could be formality’

“If the official concerned has followed it [filing of Form 7] up with an inquiry, he could be fulfilling a technical formality. Although I am not sure whether the technical formality was required,” said Mr. Lavasa.

The deadline for filing claims and objections is October 30 while the final electoral roll is scheduled to be published on December 4. Since the publication of the draft roll, 1.76 lakh applications for inclusion and 4,401 objections seeking deletion of names have been received.

World.title: New EC portal options let EROs in Delhi clear voters without documents, hearings
World.content:
New options have been introduced on the Election Commission’s ECINET portal allowing Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) in Delhi to mark an elector as eligible without requiring documents or a hearing to dispose of a notice issued against the elector’s name, officials told The Hindu on Friday.

The change comes amid allegations of “centralisation” of the functioning of ECINET, which is being used by poll officials for the special intensive revision of electoral rolls in several States.

Sources said a new dialogue box, which now lets EROs clear voters for the final roll without scheduling a hearing or seeking documents, was not available before September 30. While clearing an elector, the ERO is required to upload a declaration that they are satisfied with the voter’s eligibility and have completed the verification.

EROs exercise the final authority over the preparation of the roll and decide on all claims and objections. Officials across constituencies said the options should have been made available from the beginning of the notice phase on August 31.

“The option to bypass hearings on a case-by-case basis should have been available to us from the start. We should have been allowed to take calls in cases where none of the prescribed documents is available,” said an ERO.

Another ERO said, “I first saw the options on Wednesday. So now if I am satisfied with cases where electors don’t have prescribed documents, I can submit a declaration that I have completed verification and proceed. I have disposed of hundreds of cases a day since then.” He could not clear more than 50 cases a day earlier.

‘Nov. 30 deadline’

According to latest data, proceedings have been concluded in fewer than 5 lakh of the 33.1 lakh cases in which notices were generated. In one West Delhi constituency, only two cases have been cleared so far.

The last date for the disposal of notices is November 30.

The limited options had been a concern for EROs dealing with cases where electors were struggling to produce the required documents within the stipulated hearing period.

More than 350 electors were marked ‘ineligible’ for not turning up for hearings, prompting Delhi Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) Ashok Kumar to caution EROs against choosing the option without proper verification.

When reached for response on the new options and why they were introduced at this stage, the Delhi CEO’s Office and the EC did not respond.

What changed

Earlier, uploading a hearing order was mandatory only in cases involving deletion or marking an elector ‘ineligible’.

For an elector to be marked for the final roll after a notice and hearing, the process involved the BLO and ERO and, in ‘no-mapping’ cases, the District Election Officer (DEO).

After the BLO uploaded documents along with an undertaking and photo attendance, the ERO checked the case and sent it to the DEO for verification. The ERO would then place the elector on the final roll based on the DEO’s feedback.

“Even electors who have not been flagged for any notice do not get marked for the final roll automatically. The ERO has to do it case by case,” said a source.

The new options alter that process. EROs can now place an elector in the final roll without uploading documents and, in certain cases, without scheduling a hearing.

World.title: Govt raises petrol price by Rs2.10 per litre, high-speed diesel by Re0.30 per litre
World.content:
The government on Friday raised the price of petrol by Rs2.10 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Re0.30 per litre.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs392.76 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs399.64 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices are applicable from Oct 3 (Saturday) to Oct 5 (Monday).

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm and fuel allocations for official vehicles has been cut by 50 per cent for three months.

On September 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices.

Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Sept 29 appreciated the success of the scheme , saying that it reflected a “whole of government” approach.

Chairing a meeting of the National Steering Committee on Fuel Subsidy to review the implementation of the scheme, the deputy premier noted that the information, IT and petroleum ministries, as well as the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra), the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) and all provinces, had made “concerted” efforts for the scheme.

It was noted that to date, around 7.60 million registrations have been successfully made, and the token redemption process has entered the second week. Moreover, 7.71m tokens have been redeemed.

Previously, on July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: Dar says Makkah defence pact committee to meet next week on Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia
World.content:
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar said on Friday that a meeting of Makkah Defence Alliance’s Strategic Political Defence Committee (SPDC) would take place in Riyadh next week, adding that it would focus on Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia.

He made the remarks while addressing a press briefing detailing the Pakistan delegation’s engagements at the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) in New York in September, as well as high-level meetings that took place on its sidelines.

“We made a plan because all three of us countries were present [in New York],” Dar said, referring to himself, Turkiye’s Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan and Saudi Arabia’s Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud.

He said the SPDC, established under the trilateral “Makkah Accord”, comprises three members from each country — the foreign ministers, defence ministers and chiefs of army staff.

On Sept 25, a special meeting took place of the three army chiefs in Riyadh, he said, adding that the foreign ministers had met prior to this in New York in the wake of increased Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia.

“Very soon, a meeting of the whole SPDC … has been agreed to in principle, to take place in Riyadh,” the deputy premier said, noting that the current situation and “ground reality” would be examined during the meeting, particularly vis-a-vis Saudi Arabia.

Responding to a question, Dar said that this upcoming meeting was an emergency one, and the committee would meet again as planned after “the end of October or beginning of November”, when its work was expected to be completed.

He said that the meeting would focus on the Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia, as the previous meeting of foreign ministers in New York had done. Later, he said that the meeting would take place “next week”.

Regarding yesterday’s airstrike on a power plant in Madina, which was attributed to the Houthis, he highlighted that Pakistan had already condemned it and said it was “not acceptable”.

The deputy prime minister also noted that he had spoken to Iran in detail regarding the Houthi attacks, reminding them that Pakistan had its trilateral agreement to honour. Iran, he said, denied association “both with the Houthis and with the Iraqi militia”.

Iran also advised that the Houthis be “engaged politically”, rather than using “kinetic action”, he said, although he clarified that this was simply a “brainstorming between two foreign ministers, and in all good faith, a suggestion”.

He added that the decision would be taken between the three countries of the SPDC after the upcoming meeting.

Dar also stated, responding to a question about the potential expansion of the Makkah defence pact, that while he would not name them, “at least six countries” were keen to join the accord.

He added that this would not be possible until after the agreement was made “fully operational”, which would take at least a year, but stressed that the document of the accord itself stated that it would be open to other countries if they agreed to the principles laid down by the existing members.

Dar’s remarks come amid fresh fighting between Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Houthis. The Houthis have declared a maritime blockade on the kingdom and targeted its ships in the Red Sea. Both sides have claimed strikes on each other as tensions remain high.

Meanwhile, the defence pact , signed on Aug 7, aims to strengthen collective deterrence and empower its signatory states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them.

The first meeting of the SPDC was held in Istanbul on Aug 31, during which it was decided that the alliance’s secretariat will be initially headed by Pakistan for three years. Retired Lieutenant General Nauman Mahmood has been appointed as the first secretary general of the alliance.

UN chief to visit Pakistan before end of tenure

During the briefing, the foreign minister also said that UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres would visit Pakistan “soon”, likely before the end of his tenure.

He said that the UN chief held a meeting with the Pakistan delegation at the UNGA session, adding: “We have invited him to Pakistan and the UN secretary general has accepted.”

Calling Guterres a great supporter of Pakistan, the deputy premier recalled the “unforgettable” role he played in aiding the country through calamities.

He added that the UN chief’s term will end on Dec 31 of this year, and said that the visit would “likely” take place before this.

He noted that the programme for the visit would be released by the government and would take place “very soon” on the invitation of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif.

“I think it will be a memorable visit,” Dar added.

During the premier’s meeting with Guterres on the sidelines of the UNGA last week, the two exchanged views on major regional and international developments. The UN chief also commended Pakistan’s role in the Middle East peace process, according to the Prime Minister’s Office.

World.title: 2 civilians martyred in firing by Indian forces near Kasur border: state media
World.content:
State-run Radio Pakistan reported on Friday that two unarmed Pakistani civilians were martyred and another was injured in firing by India’s Border Security Force (BSF) near the border in Kasur.

Citing security sources, the report said that three residents of Ladhar village went a few steps ahead of a border pillar when the BSF “opened fire on them without warning”.

“The sources said two civilians were martyred while another sustained injuries in the firing. All three individuals were unarmed,” the report said.

It identified the deceased as Azmat Rasool and Mohsin Jutt, both residents of Jattan Wali Haveli, Ladhar.

“The security sources further said that none of the three individuals had attempted to cross the border fence. They said the incident constitutes a violation of the border agreement and the standard operating procedures governing the Pakistan-India international border,” the report added.

“Indian media, while continuing its tradition of a false-flag narrative, labelled the innocent civilians as alleged infiltrators,” the report said.

The development comes a day after Inter-Services Public Relations Director General Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry lampooned India’s claims of “neutralising” a “terrorist” allegedly linked to the Pakistani military, presenting the individual during a press conference.

Asked whether the recent allegations could trigger another armed conflict between the neighbours during the press briefing, he affirmed that Pakistan’s armed forces were always ready for any such move and warned of “very harsh” retribution.

World.title: Army's top brass warns of 'decisive force' against any 'May 9-like situation'
World.content:
The army’s top brass on Friday warned that any attempt at creating agitation or a “May 9-like situation” would be dealt with “decisive force”, according to the military’s media wing.

The warning came during the 277th Corps Commanders’ Conference in Rawalpindi, which was presided over by Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir.

“[The] forum underscored the importance of internal stability and resolved that any attempt to cause agitation or create [a] May 9-like situation, on any pretext whatsoever, will be dealt with decisive force and rule of law, without hesitation and discrimination,” a statement from Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said.

The warning comes as the PTI is gearing up for a long march to Islamabad, to demand the release of former prime minister and party founder Imran Khan. The protest was originally scheduled for Sept 27 but was postponed to Oct 4.

The party is currently in talks with the government over its long march, with the first round of dialogue taking place earlier in the day.

It is worth mentioning that Imran’s arrest on May 9, 2023, had triggered widespread riots across Pakistan, during which government buildings and military installations — including the GHQ in Rawalpindi — were stormed and vandalised. Following the unrest, a crackdown was launched against the PTI, with dozens of terrorism cases lodged against its leaders and supporters.

Need for ‘targeted action’ against Afghanistan stressed

According to ISPR, the forum also reviewed the security landscape and resolved to maintain a “high state of readiness”. It hailed successful counter-terrorism operations, but stressed the need to blend kinetic and non-kinetic measures.

These included “people-centric governance at [the] grassroot level, strategic engagement with [the] public, dismantling of [the] terror-crime nexus operating under patronage of vested interests and police capacity building, in line with the National Action Plan and Vision Azm-i-Istehkam”.

Affirming Pakistan’s right to self-defence, the forum noted the need for “targeted action” against terrorism emanating from Afghanistan, stressing that “only the Taliban’s delusional leadership, facilitating terrorism on behalf of India, bears responsibility for its consequences”.

Since Sep 21, in the aftermath of terror incidents in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan has carried out three strikes in Afghanistan, targeting terrorist hideouts.

A day earlier, ISPR Director General Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry said that Pakistan had the right to self-defence and “everything that is necessary will be done” in response to terrorism emanating from Afghanistan .

Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia condemned

The army huddle on Friday also welcomed the Makkah Defence Alliance between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye and its contribution to “longstanding strategic and collective defence ties”, the statement read.

“It (the forum) strongly resented Houthi attacks against Saudi Arabia, expressed solidarity with the kingdom and affirmed Pakistan’s commitment to the security and sanctity of the Haramain Sharifain,” ISPR added.

The defence pact , signed on Aug 7, aims to strengthen collective deterrence and empower its signatory states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them.

Fresh fighting between the Houthis and the Yemeni government has dragged in Riyadh, with the Houthis declaring a maritime blockade on the kingdom and targeting its ships in the Red Sea. Both sides have claimed strikes on each other as tensions remain high.

The Corps Commander Conference on Friday also reiterated Pakistan’s position on Indian Illegally Occupied Jammu and Kashmir and expressed support for resolving the Kashmir dispute, in accordance with relevant UN Security Council resolutions and the aspirations of the Kashmiri people.

In his concluding remarks, CDF Munir commended the formations for their operational preparedness and professionalism, directing the commanders to bolster intelligence-based operations and enhance combat capabilities through the adoption of modern technology, training and multi-domain integration.

“He expressed confidence that the armed forces, with unwavering support of the nation, remain fully prepared to safeguard Pakistan’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and national security,” ISPR said.

The forum also offered prayers for the martyrs of the armed forces, law enforcement agencies and civil society and paid tribute to their sacrifices.

World.title: Pakistani national charged with defrauding US Postal Service of $126m
World.content:
A Pakistani national has been charged with defrauding the United States Postal Service (USPS) of $125 million by selling counterfeit postage labels online, it emerged on Friday.

According to a press release by the US Attorney’s Office of the Southern District of Florida, issued on Monday on the website of the Department of Justice (DOJ), a federal grand jury returned an indictment charging a Pakistani national, a 33-year-old from Khanewal, with operating “an unauthorised website that allegedly sold more than five million counterfeit US postage labels”.

According to court records, these were sold at a fixed rate, “typically $2 per label”, regardless of the size, weight or destination of the package in question. This allowed customers to post items for cheap at rates “far below legitimate USPS prices”.

The statement also pointed out that the website used for this purpose was not authorised to sell USPS products and services.

The investigation revealed that over 5,200 individuals used the website to buy more than 5.1m counterfeit shipping labels. The losses caused to the service as a result were reported to be over $126m, the press release highlighted.

“Through the work of the US Postal Inspection Service and our prosecutors, the website has been shut down, the domain seized, and federal charges brought against its alleged operator,” US Attorney Jason Reding Quiñones for the Southern District of Florida said, according to the press release.

He termed the alleged scheme “simple but massive”.

According to the statement, the accused is charged with “one count of conspiracy to defraud the US and to make and sell counterfeit postage stamps; five counts of making and selling counterfeit postage stamp labels; and four counts of wire fraud”.

If convicted, he faces a maximum of five years in prison on the counts of conspiracy to defraud and sell counterfeit postage stamps, as well as 20 years in prison for each count of wire fraud.

“An indictment is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law,” the DOJ added.

In February, two Pakistani nationals were indicted in the US for their alleged role in a $10m healthcare fraud scheme that targeted Medicare and private insurance programmes.

World.title: New York governor vows to close legal loophole after alleged Cornell University gang rape
World.content:
New York Governor Kathy Hochul vowed on Friday to close a legal loophole allowing offenders in the state to avoid rape charges if their victims were willingly intoxicated, as in the case of an alleged gang rape at Cornell University.

There has been an outcry in the United States over a decision by prosecutors not to file charges in the case at the Ivy League college two years ago, prompting the governor to appoint state Attorney General Letitia James as a special prosecutor.

The investigation was reopened on Monday after the alleged victim filed a civil lawsuit, fueling allegations that the elite college failed to properly hold the men accountable.

The alleged victim said in her lawsuit that in 2024 she was drugged with ketamine, assaulted and raped by seven members of the Chi Phi fraternity, a social club for male students.

“It should not matter whether they chose to use drugs or alcohol. Voluntary intoxication is not a license for sexual assault or gang rape. Period,” Hochul said on Friday.

“I support closing this loophole, and will work with the New York State Legislature to accomplish this.”

Several US states, including New York, have provisions in their laws making it harder for prosecutors to bring charges against someone who engaged in sex with a person who voluntarily became intoxicated to the point where they could not meaningfully give or withhold consent.

Shiwali Patel, Senior Director of Education Justice at the National Women’s Law Centre, told AFP “it’s just astounding that this loophole still exists”.

“It does have a huge impact on college cases because the reality is that a significant majority of campus sexual assaults do involve alcohol and drugs,” she said.

‘Under the rug’

Hochul slammed the conduct of the initial investigation into the victim’s claims.

“She sat for hours and told (police) exactly what happened to her. And according to new reports, she could not have been clearer that she was 100 per cent confident that she had been raped,” Hochul said.

“In what world would the police learn from a victim that she’d been literally gang raped while intoxicated… in the fraternity house, and not elevate those allegations to the district attorney?”

James, a Democrat who has clashed repeatedly with US President Donald Trump, said on Friday she would “review the facts, gather evidence, interview witnesses, and if warranted, pursue prosecutions”.

Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten said this week that he planned to file criminal charges against the seven men.

He said his office declined to prosecute in 2024 because the victim’s testimony did not establish a lack of consent.

Following the allegations, Cornell closed the fraternity and temporarily suspended the students allegedly involved, several of whom were later expelled.

Cornell’s student body held a campus meeting on Thursday at which emotions ran high.

Speakers repeatedly attacked the college administrators for their handling of the case that has garnered nationwide attention.

“No public official gets to look the other way when the system breaks down and fails our young people. And as governor, I will not allow anyone to sweep this case under the rug,” Hochul said on Friday.

World.title: First round of talks between govt, opposition end as PTI’s Oct 4 protest looms over Islamabad
World.content:
The first round of talks between the PTI-led opposition and the ruling coalition over the party’s proposed Oct 4 long march concluded on Friday, with both sides agreeing to resume the dialogue on Saturday.

The meeting between government and opposition representatives, chaired by National Assembly Speaker Ayaz Sadiq, was aimed at defusing the country’s ongoing political crisis. It comes ahead of the the PTI’s planned Oct 4 protest march demanding the release of party founder Imran Khan, which has emerged as the latest point of contention between the party and the federal government.

According to a statement issued by the NA Secretariat, the participants held detailed discussions “on the prevailing political situation and exchanged views on various matters of national importance”.

“The government, PPP and opposition representatives apprised each other of their respective positions and held a detailed exchange of views in a constructive and cordial manner. The participants emphasised the need to resolve national issues through dialogue and negotiations,” it said.

The statement added that the second round of talks would be held on Saturday at 2pm in the NA speaker’s chamber.

“NA Speaker Sadiq played a key role in facilitating dialogue among the government, PPP and opposition,” the statement said.

The delegations were welcomed by Speaker Sadiq upon their arrival. “I am only playing the role of a mediator,” he said.

Sadiq said his office was “always open” to resolving issues through negotiations and that he had consistently invited the opposition to engage in dialogue. He maintained that negotiations were the only way to resolve differences and issues, adding that positions and offices were temporary.

“Parliament is the only forum where solutions to issues can be found,” he said.

In an earlier post on X, the Tehreek-i-Tahafuz-Ayin-i-Pakistan said the opposition side was being led by the leader of the opposition in the Senate, Allama Raja Nasir Abbas.

Minister for Kashmir Affairs and Gilgit-Baltistan Amir Muqam, Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry and Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry attended the meeting, along with PPP Senator Sherry Rehman and National Assembly members Syed Naveed Qamar and Ejaz Hussain Jakhrani.

The opposition was represented by PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Khan, Abbas, Amir Dogar, former NA speaker Asad Qaiser and PTI General Secretary Salman Akram Raja.

As the PTI remains resolute to go ahead with the march, federal ministers have warned that the Centre would have no other option but to impose governor’s rule or emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in light of the security situation in the province and the PTI’s protest call.

For its part, the opposition party has warned the government of dire consequences if such a decision is imposed.

‘PTI will have to call off its march’

Speaking to the media after the meeting, PPP’s Rehman said the party believed in resolving issues through negotiations.

She said that PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari had stated the party’s stance on the long march and that the PTI had to call it off “unconditionally”.

“They will have to call it off rather than postponing or deferring,” she said.

“Both parties have time; we will meet tomorrow. We will try to conclude this by tomorrow,” she stated.

Talking about the opposition’s reported demand of facilitating a meeting with incarcerated PTI founder Imran Khan, she said she could not answer the question. However, she said the opposition had asked for time and “we should respect it”.

“A political and democratic attitude requires sitting at the negotiation table and resolving the issues through dialogue,” she stated.

Later, Bilawal welcomed the government’s decision to work with his party and jointly engage with the opposition “to find political solutions to political problems”.

“The challenge of terrorism has become an existential threat to Pakistan, particularly given the active support these groups receive from neighbouring countries,” he wrote on X.

The PPP chief expressed hope that the talks would conclude with the opposition unconditionally calling off the long march, which would allow the country to come together to address the threat of terrorism and those from neighbouring countries.

“The PPP has been, and will always remain, committed to combating terrorism through any and all constitutional means,” he added.

‘Govt should engage with integrity’

The Senate opposition leader, speaking to the media at his office during a break in talks with the government, said the government should engage with the opposition “with integrity” and take steps towards resolving the issues.

“If the government cares about the political crisis, then it should sit with the opposition with integrity and step forward to find a solution,” Abbas said.

Regarding PTI’s long march, he said the call would remain “intact” until a solution was found.

“Negotiating is the way of political leaders; negotiations could resolve gigantic issues and war,” he said, adding that “it, however, depends on the government’s intention”.

He questioned whether the government, as the other party to the negotiations, genuinely wanted to resolve the issues.

“They are in government and it is their responsibility to maintain peace, resolve crises, and ensure economic stability,” he said.

Abbas reiterated that the outcome depended on how “autonomous” the government was and whether it had the “intent” to pursue negotiations.

Speaking to the media after the talks, PTI Chairman Gohar said that both parties had shared their stances on “all the issues”.

Regarding negotiations with the government, he added that “Abbas and Mehmood Khan Achakzai have the mandate for these things”.

During an opposition alliance meeting yesterday, he said, the party had decided to attend the talks with the government and give their stance if it called on the opposition.

“The positive aspect of this talk is that it is still continuing and we’ll meet again tomorrow,” he said, adding that tomorrow’s talks would be held by the same opposition committee that held them today.

Asked what the party would do if the PTI were to gain access to Imran and he were to once again call for a long march, he said: “We always act upon the directions given by Khan sahab.”

A day earlier, it emerged that a joint delegation of the PPP and the government would hold a meeting with the PTI leadership on Friday, during which the “current political situation” in the country would be discussed with the opposition.

The decision came after a meeting at President House attended by President Asif Ali Zardari, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi and other party leaders.

Sanaullah also said on Thursday that the federal government and PTI were engaged in “off-the-record talks” regarding PTI’s planned protest.

Sanaullah said that the decision on the proposed march rested with PTI’s senior leadership, “with whom off-the-record consultation is ongoing”.

“So let us see, even if they do not postpone it, we have arrangements in place to stop them,” he warned.

World.title: ECP proposes holding Punjab local govt elections on Dec 14
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) on Friday proposed holding local government elections in Punjab on Dec 14 and sent a draft of the suggested schedule to the Punjab chief secretary for consultation.

In a letter seen by Dawn, Chaudhry Nadeem Qasim, additional director general for local government elections, forwarded the draft schedule to the Punjab chief secretary on the commission’s behalf.

He also sought the provincial government’s opinion on the proposed timelines so that a final schedule could be notified after approval from the ECP.

According to the proposed schedule, nomination papers will be filed from Oct 27 to 30, while scrutiny will be conducted from Nov 2 to 5. Appeals against acceptance or rejection of papers can be filed from Nov 7 to 11, and will be decided by tribunals between Nov 12 and 16.

As per the letter, the last proposed date for withdrawal of candidature is Nov 18. The final list of candidates will be displayed on Nov 19 and election symbols will be allotted on Nov 20.

Polling is proposed for Dec 14, with returning officers to announce results by Dec 17, the letter said.

The letter also referred to a consultative meeting held on Aug 20 between the ECP and a provincial cabinet committee on the announcement of the poll date. It is worth noting that during the meeting, the ECP had agreed to the provincial government’s proposal to hold polls between Dec 15 and Jan 15, 2027.

On Aug 6, the Punjab cabinet had approved an allocation of Rs12.5 billion for holding local government elections in the province.

The last local government elections in Punjab were held in 2015 under the Punjab Local Government Act, 2013. Polling took place in phases between Oct and Dec 2015, and elected councils assumed office in 2017 after indirect elections for mayors and chairpersons. Since then, local body polls in Punjab have experienced repeated delays.

The PTI government had dissolved the elected local bodies in April 2019 before they completed their tenure. The move was later struck down by the Supreme Court, which restored them. They eventually completed their term on Dec 31, 2021.

Successive provincial governments repeatedly amended or replaced the Punjab Local Government Act. Each legislative change required the ECP to restart preparations, including delimitation and election planning.
